note: Proposed corrections to the Latin–English readings from the 9 November 2026 full reading of all 70 books, each confirmed or amended by a second reading. Nothing here has been applied to the staging site or to the book folders. proposed_english is the full reading with the correction made.

corrections.latin: Dixit etiam Deus : Producant aquæ reptile animæ viventis, et volatile super terram sub firmamento cæli.
corrections.english: God also said, “Let the waters bring forth swarming living creatures, and winged creatures above the earth beneath the firmament of heaven.”

first_reading.proposed: God also said, “Let the waters bring forth creeping living creatures, and winged creatures above the earth beneath the firmament of heaven.”
first_reading.reason: "reptile animæ viventis" is the creeping creature having life (reptile, from repere, to creep; rendered "creeping creatures" in 1:24-26). "Swarming" follows the Hebrew, not the Latin.

second_reading.note: "reptile animæ viventis" is a creeping thing (repere); "swarming" renders the Hebrew, not reptile.

corrections.proposed_english: God also said, “Let the waters bring forth creeping living creatures, and winged creatures above the earth beneath the firmament of heaven.”

corrections.latin: Et creavit Deus hominem ad imaginem suam : ad imaginem Dei creavit illum, masculum et feminam creavit eos.
corrections.english: God created humankind in His image; in the image of God He created them; male and female He created them.

first_reading.proposed: God created humankind in His image; in the image of God He created him; male and female He created them.
first_reading.reason: "creavit illum" is singular (him), set against the plural "creavit eos"; the English makes both "them", losing the Latin's change of number (cf. 5:1 "fecit illum", rendered "him").

second_reading.note: "creavit illum" is singular against the following "creavit eos"; the English flattens both to "them".

corrections.proposed_english: God created humankind in His image; in the image of God He created him; male and female He created them.

corrections.latin: Dixitque Lamech uxoribus suis Adæ et Sellæ : [Audite vocem meam, uxores Lamech ; auscultate sermonem meum : quoniam occidi virum in vulnus meum, et adolescentulum in livorem meum.
corrections.english: Lamech said to his wives Adah and Zillah, “Hear my voice, wives of Lamech; listen to my words. For I have killed a man for wounding me, and a young man for bruising me.

first_reading.proposed: Lamech said to his wives Adah and Zillah, “Hear my voice, wives of Lamech; listen to my words. For I have killed a man to my own wounding, and a young man to my own bruising.
first_reading.reason: "in vulnus meum ... in livorem meum" = to my (own) wounding / bruising (in + accusative of result). "For wounding me / for bruising me" gives the motive as in modern Hebrew-based versions, which the Latin does not say.

second_reading.note: "in vulnus meum ... in livorem meum" (in + accusative) gives the outcome for Lamech, not the victim's offence as "for wounding me" asserts.

corrections.proposed_english: Lamech said to his wives Adah and Zillah, “Hear my voice, wives of Lamech; listen to my words. For I have killed a man to my own wounding, and a young man to my own bruising.

corrections.latin: Generatione autem quarta revertentur huc : necdum enim completæ sunt iniquitates Amorrhæorum usque ad præsens tempus.
corrections.english: In the fourth generation they shall return here, for the iniquities of the Amorites have not yet reached their fullness.”

first_reading.proposed: In the fourth generation they shall return here, for the iniquities of the Amorites have not yet reached their fullness up to the present time.”
first_reading.reason: The closing phrase "usque ad præsens tempus" (until the present time) is left untranslated.

second_reading.note: "usque ad præsens tempus" is left untranslated in the current English.

corrections.proposed_english: In the fourth generation they shall return here, for the iniquities of the Amorites have not yet reached their fullness up to the present time.”

corrections.latin: Masculus, cujus præputii caro circumcisa non fuerit, delebitur anima illa de populo suo : quia pactum meum irritum fecit.
corrections.english: An uncircumcised male, whose foreskin's flesh has not been circumcised—that person shall be cut off from his people, because he has broken My covenant.”

first_reading.proposed: A male whose foreskin's flesh has not been circumcised—that person shall be cut off from his people, because he has broken My covenant.”
first_reading.reason: The Latin has only "Masculus, cujus præputii caro circumcisa non fuerit"; "uncircumcised" before "male" is not in the Latin and matches the Hebrew/KJV wording ("the uncircumcised male").

second_reading.note: Latin has only "Masculus, cujus præputii caro circumcisa non fuerit"; the prefixed "uncircumcised" is an addition from the Hebrew.

corrections.proposed_english: A male whose foreskin's flesh has not been circumcised—that person shall be cut off from his people, because he has broken My covenant.”

corrections.latin: Rursumque ait : Quis auditurus crederet Abraham quod Sara lactaret filium, quem peperit ei jam seni ?
corrections.english: Again she said, “Who would have believed, on hearing it, that Abraham's Sarah would nurse a son whom she bore him in his old age?”

first_reading.proposed: Again she said, “Who would have believed Abraham, on hearing it, that Sarah would nurse a son whom she bore him in his old age?”
first_reading.reason: "Abraham" stands in the main clause before "quod" (with "crederet"/"auditurus"), not as a genitive of Sara; "Abraham's Sarah" misconstrues "Quis auditurus crederet Abraham quod Sara lactaret filium".

second_reading.note: "Quis auditurus crederet Abraham quod Sara": Abraham goes with crederet before quod; it is not a genitive of Sara.

corrections.proposed_english: Again she said, “Who would have believed Abraham, on hearing it, that Sarah would nurse a son whom she bore him in his old age?”

corrections.latin: Exaudivit autem Deus vocem pueri : vocavitque angelus Dei Agar de cælo, dicens : Quid agis Agar ? noli timere : exaudivit enim Deus vocem pueri de loco in quo est.
corrections.english: God heard the boy's voice. The angel of God called to Hagar from heaven, saying, “What troubles you, Hagar? Do not fear, for God has heard the boy's voice from the place where he is.

first_reading.proposed: God heard the boy's voice. The angel of God called to Hagar from heaven, saying, “What are you doing, Hagar? Do not fear, for God has heard the boy's voice from the place where he is.
first_reading.reason: "Quid agis Agar ?" = What are you doing, Hagar? "What troubles you" is the modern Hebrew-based wording ("What ails thee"), not the Latin.

second_reading.note: "Quid agis Agar" asks what she is doing; "What troubles you" is the Hebrew-based wording.

corrections.proposed_english: God heard the boy's voice. The angel of God called to Hagar from heaven, saying, “What are you doing, Hagar? Do not fear, for God has heard the boy's voice from the place where he is.

corrections.latin: Tulit quoque ligna holocausti, et imposuit super Isaac filium suum : ipse vero portabat in manibus ignem et gladium. Cumque duo pergerent simul,
corrections.english: He took the wood for the whole burnt offering and laid it upon his son Isaac, while he himself carried the fire and the knife in his hands. As the two walked together,

first_reading.proposed: He took the wood for the whole burnt offering and laid it upon his son Isaac, while he himself carried the fire and the sword in his hands. As the two walked together,
first_reading.reason: "gladium" is a sword; "knife" follows the Hebrew-based versions rather than the Latin word.

second_reading.note: "ignem et gladium": gladius is a sword, not a knife (culter); "knife" follows the Hebrew.

corrections.proposed_english: He took the wood for the whole burnt offering and laid it upon his son Isaac, while he himself carried the fire and the sword in his hands. As the two walked together,

corrections.latin: Extenditque manum, et arripuit gladium, ut immolaret filium suum.
corrections.english: He stretched out his hand and grasped the knife to sacrifice his son.

first_reading.proposed: He stretched out his hand and grasped the sword to sacrifice his son.
first_reading.reason: "arripuit gladium" = took hold of the sword; "knife" follows the Hebrew-based versions rather than the Latin word.

second_reading.note: "arripuit gladium": gladius is a sword; "knife" follows the Hebrew.

corrections.proposed_english: He stretched out his hand and grasped the sword to sacrifice his son.

corrections.latin: et ait ad puerum : Quis est ille homo qui venit per agrum in occursum nobis ? Dixitque ei : Ipse est dominus meus. At illa tollens cito pallium, operuit se.
corrections.english: She said to the servant, “Who is that man coming through the field to meet us?” He said, “He is my master.” She quickly took her veil and covered herself.

first_reading.proposed: She said to the servant, “Who is that man coming through the field to meet us?” He said, “He is my master.” She quickly took her cloak and covered herself.
first_reading.reason: "tollens cito pallium": pallium is a cloak or mantle; "veil" is the wording of the Hebrew-based versions, not of the Latin.

second_reading.note: "tollens cito pallium": pallium is a cloak or mantle; "veil" renders the Hebrew, not this word.

corrections.proposed_english: She said to the servant, “Who is that man coming through the field to meet us?” He said, “He is my master.” She quickly took her cloak and covered herself.

corrections.latin: Quibus adultis, factus est Esau vir gnarus venandi, et homo agricola : Jacob autem vir simplex habitabat in tabernaculis.
corrections.english: When they grew up, Esau became a skilled hunter and a man of the fields, while Jacob was a simple man who lived in tents.

first_reading.proposed: When they grew up, Esau became a skilled hunter and a farmer, while Jacob was a simple man who lived in tents.
first_reading.reason: "homo agricola" = a husbandman, a tiller of the soil (so rendered at 4:2 and 9:20); "a man of the fields" reproduces the Hebrew idiom, not the Latin.

second_reading.note: "homo agricola" is a tiller of the soil; "a man of the fields" reproduces the Hebrew idiom instead.

corrections.proposed_english: When they grew up, Esau became a skilled hunter and a farmer, while Jacob was a simple man who lived in tents.

corrections.latin: Et ille discedens, ut veniret ad torrentem Geraræ, habitaretque ibi,
corrections.english: He departed, coming to the valley of Gerar to live there,

first_reading.proposed: He departed, coming to the torrent of Gerar to live there,
first_reading.reason: "ad torrentem Geraræ": torrens is a torrent or stream; "valley of Gerar" is the KJV/Hebrew-based wording.

second_reading.note: "ad torrentem Geraræ": torrens is a torrent or stream, not a valley.

corrections.proposed_english: He departed, coming to the torrent of Gerar to live there,

corrections.latin: Foderuntque in torrente, et repererunt aquam vivam.
corrections.english: They dug in the valley and found flowing water.

first_reading.proposed: They dug in the torrent and found flowing water.
first_reading.reason: "in torrente" = in the torrent (stream bed); "valley" is the KJV/Hebrew-based wording, as in 26:17.

second_reading.note: "Foderuntque in torrente": torrens is a torrent bed, not a valley.

corrections.proposed_english: They dug in the torrent and found flowing water.

corrections.latin: valet manus mea reddere tibi malum : sed Deus patris vestri heri dixit mihi : Cave ne loquaris contra Jacob quidquam durius.
corrections.english: my hand has power to repay you with harm, but yesterday the God of your fathers said to me, ‘Take care not to speak anything harsh against Jacob.’

first_reading.proposed: my hand has power to repay you with harm, but yesterday the God of your father said to me, ‘Take care not to speak anything harsh against Jacob.’
first_reading.reason: "Deus patris vestri" has the singular patris: the God of your father. The English plural "your fathers" changes the number.

second_reading.note: "Deus patris vestri": patris is singular, father not fathers.

corrections.proposed_english: my hand has power to repay you with harm, but yesterday the God of your father said to me, ‘Take care not to speak anything harsh against Jacob.’

corrections.latin: Elevans autem Jacob oculos suos, vidit venientem Esau, et cum eo quadringentos viros : divisitque filios Liæ et Rachel, ambarumque famularum :
corrections.english: Jacob raised his eyes and saw Esau coming, and with him four hundred men. He divided the children among Leah, Rachel, and the two maidservants.

first_reading.proposed: Jacob raised his eyes and saw Esau coming, and with him four hundred men. He divided the children of Leah, of Rachel, and of the two maidservants.
first_reading.reason: "filios Liæ et Rachel, ambarumque famularum" are genitives: he divided the children of Leah, Rachel and both handmaids. "Among Leah, Rachel..." is the Hebrew construction, not this Latin.

second_reading.note: "filios Liæ et Rachel, ambarumque famularum" are genitives dependent on filios, not recipients of a distribution.

corrections.proposed_english: Jacob raised his eyes and saw Esau coming, and with him four hundred men. He divided the children of Leah, of Rachel, and of the two maidservants.

corrections.latin: et suscipe benedictionem quam attuli tibi, et quam donavit mihi Deus tribuens omnia. Vix fratre compellente, suscipiens,
corrections.english: and accept the blessing I have brought you, which God gave me by granting me everything.” Only at his brother's urging did he accept it,

first_reading.proposed: and accept the blessing I have brought you, which God, who grants all things, gave me.” Only at his brother's urging did he accept it,
first_reading.reason: "Deus tribuens omnia" describes God as the one who bestows all things; the Latin has no "me" and no instrumental sense ("by granting me everything").

second_reading.note: "Deus tribuens omnia" describes God as giver of all things; no second "me" and no instrumental sense in the Latin.

corrections.proposed_english: and accept the blessing I have brought you, which God, who grants all things, gave me.” Only at his brother's urging did he accept it,

corrections.latin: Hoc quoque mortuo regnavit pro eo Saul de fluvio Rohoboth.
corrections.english: When he too died, Saul from Rehoboth by the river reigned in his place.

first_reading.proposed: When he too died, Saul from the river Rehoboth reigned in his place.
first_reading.reason: "de fluvio Rohoboth" is "from the river Rohoboth"; "Rehoboth by the river" is the Hebrew phrasing, not the Latin's.

second_reading.note: "de fluvio Rohoboth" is from the river Rohoboth; "Rehoboth by the river" is the Hebrew phrasing.

corrections.proposed_english: When he too died, Saul from the river Rehoboth reigned in his place.

corrections.latin: Præposuit itaque eis magistros operum, ut affligerent eos oneribus : ædificaveruntque urbes tabernaculorum Pharaoni, Phithom et Ramesses.
corrections.english: So he appointed taskmasters over them to afflict them with burdens. They built storage cities for Pharaoh: Pithom and Rameses.

first_reading.proposed: So he appointed taskmasters over them to afflict them with burdens. They built cities of tabernacles for Pharaoh: Pithom and Rameses.
first_reading.reason: "urbes tabernaculorum" is "cities of tabernacles (tents)"; "storage cities" renders the Hebrew, not this Latin.

second_reading.note: "urbes tabernaculorum" is cities of tabernacles, a distinctive Vulgate reading; "storage cities" is the Hebrew.

corrections.proposed_english: So he appointed taskmasters over them to afflict them with burdens. They built cities of tabernacles for Pharaoh: Pithom and Rameses.

corrections.latin: Quæ responderunt : Non sunt Hebreæ sicut ægyptiæ mulieres : ipsæ enim obstetricandi habent scientiam, et priusquam veniamus ad eas, pariunt.
corrections.english: They answered, “The Hebrew women are not like the Egyptian women. They themselves know how to give birth, and they deliver before we come to them.”

first_reading.proposed: They answered, “The Hebrew women are not like the Egyptian women. They themselves have the skill of midwifery, and they deliver before we come to them.”
first_reading.reason: "obstetricandi habent scientiam" means they have the knowledge of acting as midwife (obstetricare), not knowledge of "how to give birth".

second_reading.note: "obstetricandi habent scientiam": obstetricare is to act as midwife, not to give birth.

corrections.proposed_english: They answered, “The Hebrew women are not like the Egyptian women. They themselves have the skill of midwifery, and they deliver before we come to them.”

corrections.latin: Ait Moyses : Obsecro, Domine, non sum eloquens ab heri et nudiustertius : et ex quo locutus es ad servum tuum, impeditioris et tardioris linguæ sum.
corrections.english: Moses said, “Please, Lord, I have not been eloquent, either yesterday or the day before. Even since You spoke to Your servant, my tongue has been hindered and slow.”

first_reading.proposed: Moses said, “Please, Lord, I have not been eloquent, either yesterday or the day before. And since You spoke to Your servant, my tongue has been more hindered and slower.”
first_reading.reason: "et ex quo locutus es... impeditioris et tardioris linguæ sum": comparatives, "more hindered and slower" since God spoke; English drops the comparison and turns "et ex quo" into "Even since".

second_reading.note: "et ex quo ... impeditioris et tardioris linguæ sum": comparatives dropped, and "et ex quo" is "and since", not "even since".

corrections.proposed_english: Moses said, “Please, Lord, I have not been eloquent, either yesterday or the day before. And since You spoke to Your servant, my tongue has been more hindered and slower.”

corrections.latin: Et dixit Dominus ad Moysen : Ingredere ad Pharaonem : ego enim induravi cor ejus, et servorum illius, ut faciam signa mea hæc in eo :
corrections.english: The Lord said to Moses, “Go in to Pharaoh, for I have hardened his heart and those of his servants, so that I may perform these signs of Mine in his midst,

first_reading.proposed: The Lord said to Moses, “Go in to Pharaoh, for I have hardened his heart and those of his servants, so that I may perform these signs of Mine in him,
first_reading.reason: "ut faciam signa mea hæc in eo" is "in him" (Pharaoh); "in his midst" reflects the Hebrew idiom rather than the Latin pronoun.

second_reading.note: "signa mea hæc in eo" is "in him"; "in his midst" is the Hebrew idiom.

corrections.proposed_english: The Lord said to Moses, “Go in to Pharaoh, for I have hardened his heart and those of his servants, so that I may perform these signs of Mine in him,

corrections.latin: Oves vestras et armenta assumite ut petieratis, et abeuntes benedicite mihi.
corrections.english: Take your sheep and herds, as you requested, and go; bless me also.”

first_reading.proposed: Take your sheep and herds, as you requested, and go; bless me.”
first_reading.reason: "abeuntes benedicite mihi" is "as you depart, bless me"; the Latin has no word for "also", which comes from the Hebrew.

second_reading.note: "abeuntes benedicite mihi" has no word for "also"; it is added from the Hebrew.

corrections.proposed_english: Take your sheep and herds, as you requested, and go; bless me.”

corrections.latin: Dicturusque est Pharao super filiis Israël : Coarctati sunt in terra ; conclusit eos desertum.
corrections.english: Pharaoh will say of the children of Israel, ‘They are hemmed in by the land; the wilderness has shut them in.’

first_reading.proposed: Pharaoh will say of the children of Israel, ‘They are hemmed in in the land; the wilderness has shut them in.’
first_reading.reason: "Coarctati sunt in terra" is locative, 'straitened in the land'; the English makes the land the agent ('by the land').

second_reading.note: "Coarctati sunt in terra" is locative, not agent; proposed "hemmed in in the land" is right in sense but clumsy, so "within".

corrections.proposed_english: Pharaoh will say of the children of Israel, ‘They are hemmed in within the land; the wilderness has shut them in.’

corrections.latin: Filii autem Israël comederunt man quadraginta annis, donec venirent in terram habitabilem : hoc cibo aliti sunt, usquequo tangerent fines terræ Chanaan.
corrections.english: The children of Israel ate manna for forty years, until they came to an inhabited land. They were fed with this food until they reached the borders of the land of Canaan.

first_reading.proposed: The children of Israel ate manna for forty years, until they came to a habitable land. They were fed with this food until they reached the borders of the land of Canaan.
first_reading.reason: "terram habitabilem" means a habitable land (fit to dwell in), not an 'inhabited' land; 'inhabited' reflects the Hebrew rather than this Latin.

second_reading.note: "terram habitabilem" is habitable, not inhabited; the current word follows the Hebrew.

corrections.proposed_english: The children of Israel ate manna for forty years, until they came to a habitable land. They were fed with this food until they reached the borders of the land of Canaan.

corrections.latin: Quia manus solii Domini, et bellum Domini erit contra Amalec, a generatione in generationem.
corrections.english: “For the hand is of the Lord's throne, and the Lord's war against Amalek will be from generation to generation.”

first_reading.proposed: “For the hand of the Lord's throne and the Lord's war will be against Amalek from generation to generation.”
first_reading.reason: "manus solii Domini, et bellum Domini erit contra Amalec": hand and war are joint subjects of 'erit contra Amalec'; the English inserts 'is', making 'the hand is of the Lord's throne' a separate assertion.

second_reading.note: "manus solii Domini, et bellum Domini erit contra Amalec": both nouns are subjects of erit; the inserted "is" makes a separate clause.

corrections.proposed_english: “For the hand of the Lord's throne and the Lord's war will be against Amalek from generation to generation.”

corrections.latin: Cumque audisset Jethro, sacerdos Madian, cognatus Moysi, omnia quæ fecerat Deus Moysi, et Israëli populo suo, et quod eduxisset Dominus Israël de Ægypto,
corrections.english: When Jethro, the priest of Midian and Moses' father-in-law, heard everything God had done for Moses and His people Israel, and that the Lord had led Israel out of Egypt,

first_reading.proposed: When Jethro, the priest of Midian and Moses' kinsman, heard everything God had done for Moses and His people Israel, and that the Lord had led Israel out of Egypt,
first_reading.reason: "cognatus Moysi" means Moses' kinsman; 'father-in-law' (Latin socer) follows the Hebrew, not this Latin. Same word recurs in 18:5, 6, 7, 8, 12, 14, 27.

second_reading.note: "cognatus Moysi" is kinsman; father-in-law would be socer and follows the Hebrew.

corrections.proposed_english: When Jethro, the priest of Midian and Moses' kinsman, heard everything God had done for Moses and His people Israel, and that the Lord had led Israel out of Egypt,

corrections.latin: Venit ergo Jethro cognatus Moysi, et filii ejus, et uxor ejus ad Moysen in desertum, ubi erat castrametatus juxta montem Dei.
corrections.english: Jethro, Moses' father-in-law, came with Moses' sons and wife to Moses in the wilderness, where he was camped beside the mountain of God.

first_reading.proposed: Jethro, Moses' kinsman, came with Moses' sons and wife to Moses in the wilderness, where he was camped beside the mountain of God.
first_reading.reason: "cognatus Moysi" is 'kinsman of Moses'; 'father-in-law' follows the Hebrew, not the Latin word.

second_reading.note: "Jethro cognatus Moysi" is kinsman, not father-in-law (socer).

corrections.proposed_english: Jethro, Moses' kinsman, came with Moses' sons and wife to Moses in the wilderness, where he was camped beside the mountain of God.

corrections.latin: Et mandavit Moysi, dicens : Ego Jethro cognatus tuus venio ad te, et uxor tua, et duo filii cum ea.
corrections.english: He sent word to Moses, saying, “I, Jethro your father-in-law, am coming to you, with your wife and her two sons.”

first_reading.proposed: He sent word to Moses, saying, “I, Jethro your kinsman, am coming to you, with your wife, and two sons with her.”
first_reading.reason: "cognatus tuus" is 'your kinsman', not 'father-in-law'; "duo filii cum ea" is 'two sons with her', where 'her two sons' follows the Hebrew.

second_reading.note: "cognatus tuus" is kinsman; but "duo filii cum ea" is fairly given by "her two sons", so that further change is not needed.

corrections.proposed_english: He sent word to Moses, saying, “I, Jethro your kinsman, am coming to you, with your wife and her two sons.”

corrections.latin: Qui egressus in occursum cognati sui, adoravit, et osculatus est eum : salutaveruntque se mutuo verbis pacificis. Cumque intrasset tabernaculum,
corrections.english: Moses went out to meet his father-in-law, bowed, and kissed him. They greeted each other with words of peace. When he entered the tent,

first_reading.proposed: Moses went out to meet his kinsman, bowed, and kissed him. They greeted each other with words of peace. When he entered the tent,
first_reading.reason: "in occursum cognati sui": cognatus is 'kinsman'; 'father-in-law' follows the Hebrew, not the Latin.

second_reading.note: "in occursum cognati sui": cognatus is kinsman, not father-in-law.

corrections.proposed_english: Moses went out to meet his kinsman, bowed, and kissed him. They greeted each other with words of peace. When he entered the tent,

corrections.latin: narravit Moyses cognato suo cuncta quæ fecerat Dominus Pharaoni et Ægyptiis propter Israël : universumque laborem, qui accidisset eis in itinere, et quod liberaverat eos Dominus.
corrections.english: Moses recounted to his father-in-law everything the Lord had done to Pharaoh and the Egyptians for Israel's sake, all the hardship that had befallen them on the journey, and how the Lord had delivered them.

first_reading.proposed: Moses recounted to his kinsman everything the Lord had done to Pharaoh and the Egyptians for Israel's sake, all the hardship that had befallen them on the journey, and how the Lord had delivered them.
first_reading.reason: "cognato suo" is 'to his kinsman'; 'father-in-law' follows the Hebrew, not the Latin.

second_reading.note: "cognato suo" is to his kinsman, not father-in-law.

corrections.proposed_english: Moses recounted to his kinsman everything the Lord had done to Pharaoh and the Egyptians for Israel's sake, all the hardship that had befallen them on the journey, and how the Lord had delivered them.

corrections.latin: Obtulit ergo Jethro cognatus Moysi holocausta et hostias Deo : veneruntque Aaron et omnes seniores Israël, ut comederent panem cum eo coram Deo.
corrections.english: Jethro, Moses' father-in-law, offered whole burnt offerings and sacrifices to God. Aaron and all Israel's elders came to eat bread with him before God.

first_reading.proposed: Jethro, Moses' kinsman, offered whole burnt offerings and sacrifices to God. Aaron and all Israel's elders came to eat bread with him before God.
first_reading.reason: "cognatus Moysi" is 'kinsman of Moses'; 'father-in-law' follows the Hebrew, not the Latin.

second_reading.note: "Jethro cognatus Moysi" is kinsman, not father-in-law.

corrections.proposed_english: Jethro, Moses' kinsman, offered whole burnt offerings and sacrifices to God. Aaron and all Israel's elders came to eat bread with him before God.

corrections.latin: Quod cum vidisset cognatus ejus, omnia scilicet quæ agebat in populo, ait : Quid est hoc quod facis in plebe ? cur solus sedes, et omnis populus præstolatur de mane usque ad vesperam ?
corrections.english: When his father-in-law saw everything he was doing among the people, he said, “What is this you are doing among the people? Why do you sit alone while all the people wait from morning until evening?”

first_reading.proposed: When his kinsman saw everything he was doing among the people, he said, “What is this you are doing among the people? Why do you sit alone while all the people wait from morning until evening?”
first_reading.reason: "cognatus ejus" is 'his kinsman'; 'father-in-law' follows the Hebrew, not the Latin.

second_reading.note: "cognatus ejus" is his kinsman, not father-in-law.

corrections.proposed_english: When his kinsman saw everything he was doing among the people, he said, “What is this you are doing among the people? Why do you sit alone while all the people wait from morning until evening?”

corrections.latin: Dimisitque cognatum suum : qui reversus abiit in terram suam.
corrections.english: Moses sent his father-in-law away, and he went back to his own land.

first_reading.proposed: Moses sent his kinsman away, and he went back to his own land.
first_reading.reason: "cognatum suum" is 'his kinsman'; 'father-in-law' follows the Hebrew, not the Latin.

second_reading.note: "Dimisitque cognatum suum": cognatus is kinsman, not father-in-law.

corrections.proposed_english: Moses sent his kinsman away, and he went back to his own land.

corrections.latin: Cunctus autem populus videbat voces et lampades, et sonitum buccinæ, montemque fumantem : et perterriti ac pavore concussi, steterunt procul,
corrections.english: All the people witnessed the thunder, flashes, trumpet's sound, and smoking mountain. Terrified and shaken with fear, they stood at a distance,

first_reading.proposed: All the people witnessed the voices, flashes, trumpet's sound, and smoking mountain. Terrified and shaken with fear, they stood at a distance,
first_reading.reason: "videbat voces" is 'saw the voices'; 'thunder' (Latin tonitrua, as at 19:16) interprets after the Hebrew rather than rendering voces.

second_reading.note: "videbat voces" is voices; thunder would be tonitrua (as 19:16) and interprets after the Hebrew.

corrections.proposed_english: All the people witnessed the voices, flashes, trumpet's sound, and smoking mountain. Terrified and shaken with fear, they stood at a distance,

corrections.latin: offeret eum dominus diis, et applicabitur ad ostium et postes, perforabitque aurem ejus subula : et erit ei servus in sæculum.
corrections.english: his master shall bring him before the judges, and he shall be brought to the door and doorposts. His master shall pierce his ear with an awl, and he shall be his slave forever.

first_reading.proposed: his master shall bring him to the gods, and he shall be brought to the door and doorposts. His master shall pierce his ear with an awl, and he shall be his slave forever.
first_reading.reason: "offeret eum dominus diis" says 'to the gods'; 'before the judges' is an interpretation (as in the KJV), not what the Latin word says.

second_reading.note: "offeret eum dominus diis": diis is "to the gods"; "judges" is a gloss, not the Latin word.

corrections.proposed_english: his master shall bring him to the gods, and he shall be brought to the door and doorposts. His master shall pierce his ear with an awl, and he shall be his slave forever.

corrections.latin: Si quis aperuerit cisternam, et foderit, et non operuerit eam, cecideritque bos aut asinus in eam,
corrections.english: If someone opens or digs a cistern and does not cover it, and an ox or donkey falls into it,

first_reading.proposed: If someone opens and digs a cistern and does not cover it, and an ox or donkey falls into it,
first_reading.reason: "aperuerit cisternam, et foderit" joins the verbs with et, 'opens and digs'; 'or' follows the Hebrew.

second_reading.note: "aperuerit cisternam, et foderit" joins the verbs with et; "or" is the Hebrew.

corrections.proposed_english: If someone opens and digs a cistern and does not cover it, and an ox or donkey falls into it,

corrections.latin: Sin autem sciebat quod bos cornupeta esset ab heri et nudiustertius, et non custodivit eum dominus suus : reddet bovem pro bove, et cadaver integrum accipiet.
corrections.english: But if it was known that the ox had been accustomed to gore for some time and its owner did not restrain it, he shall repay ox for ox and receive the whole carcass.

first_reading.proposed: But if he knew that the ox had been accustomed to gore for some time and its owner did not restrain it, he shall repay ox for ox and receive the whole carcass.
first_reading.reason: "sciebat" is active, 'he (the owner) knew'; the impersonal passive 'it was known' follows the Hebrew and shifts who knew.

second_reading.note: "Sin autem sciebat" is active third singular, the owner knew; "it was known" is impersonal after the Hebrew.

corrections.proposed_english: But if he knew that the ox had been accustomed to gore for some time and its owner did not restrain it, he shall repay ox for ox and receive the whole carcass.

corrections.latin: si latet fur, dominus domus applicabitur ad deos, et jurabit quod non extenderit manum in rem proximi sui,
corrections.english: If the thief remains hidden, the householder shall be brought before the judges and swear that he has not laid his hand on his neighbor's property

first_reading.proposed: If the thief remains hidden, the householder shall be brought before the gods and swear that he has not laid his hand on his neighbor's property
first_reading.reason: "applicabitur ad deos" says 'to the gods'; 'the judges' is an interpretation (as in the KJV), not the Latin word. Compare 22:19, where diis is rendered 'gods'.

second_reading.note: "applicabitur ad deos" is to the gods; "judges" is a gloss, not the Latin word.

corrections.proposed_english: If the thief remains hidden, the householder shall be brought before the gods and swear that he has not laid his hand on his neighbor's property

corrections.latin: ad perpetrandam fraudem, tam in bove quam in asino, et ove ac vestimento, et quidquid damnum inferre potest : ad deos utriusque causa perveniet, et si illi judicaverint, duplum restituet proximo suo.
corrections.english: to commit fraud, whether concerning an ox, donkey, sheep, clothing, or anything that may involve a loss. Both parties' case shall come before the judges; if they give judgment against him, he shall repay his neighbor double.

first_reading.proposed: to commit fraud, whether concerning an ox, donkey, sheep, clothing, or anything that may involve a loss. Both parties' case shall come before the gods; if they give judgment against him, he shall repay his neighbor double.
first_reading.reason: "ad deos utriusque causa perveniet" says the case shall come 'to the gods'; 'the judges' interprets rather than renders deos.

second_reading.note: "ad deos utriusque causa perveniet": deos is gods; "judges" interprets rather than translates.

corrections.proposed_english: to commit fraud, whether concerning an ox, donkey, sheep, clothing, or anything that may involve a loss. Both parties' case shall come before the gods; if they give judgment against him, he shall repay his neighbor double.

corrections.latin: Diis non detrahes, et principi populi tui non maledices.
corrections.english: You shall not revile the judges or curse the ruler of your people.

first_reading.proposed: You shall not revile the gods or curse the ruler of your people.
first_reading.reason: "Diis non detrahes" is 'you shall not speak ill of the gods'; 'the judges' is an interpretation, not the Latin word diis.

second_reading.note: "Diis non detrahes": diis is gods; "judges" is an interpretation, not the Latin word.

corrections.proposed_english: You shall not revile the gods or curse the ruler of your people.

corrections.latin: Quos pones subter arulam altaris : eritque craticula usque ad altaris medium.
corrections.english: Place these beneath the altar's ledge; the grating shall reach halfway up the altar.

first_reading.proposed: Place these beneath the altar's hearth; the grating shall reach halfway up the altar.
first_reading.reason: "subter arulam altaris": arula is the hearth (fire-pan) of the altar, not a 'ledge'; 'ledge' reflects the Hebrew term rather than this Latin.

second_reading.note: "subter arulam altaris": arula is a small altar-hearth or fire-pan, never a ledge; "ledge" is the Hebrew term.

corrections.proposed_english: Place these beneath the altar's hearth; the grating shall reach halfway up the altar.

corrections.latin: Videns ergo Moyses populum quod esset nudatus (spoliaverat enim eum Aaron propter ignominiam sordis, et inter hostes nudum constituerat),
corrections.english: Moses saw that the people were stripped bare, for Aaron had stripped them to the shame of their disgrace and left them naked among their enemies.

first_reading.proposed: Moses saw that the people were stripped bare, for Aaron had stripped them on account of the shame of the filth and left them naked among their enemies.
first_reading.reason: "propter ignominiam sordis" is causal, 'on account of the shame of the filth'; the English turns it into a result ('to the shame') and loses sordis, 'filth'.

second_reading.note: "propter ignominiam sordis" is causal and sordis is filth; "to the shame of their disgrace" misrenders both.

corrections.proposed_english: Moses saw that the people were stripped bare, for Aaron had stripped them on account of the shame of the filth and left them naked among their enemies.

corrections.latin: et mittam præcursorem tui angelum, ut ejiciam Chananæum, et Amorrhæum, et Hethæum, et Pherezæum, et Hevæum, et Jebusæum,
corrections.english: I will send an angel before you to drive out the Canaanite, Amorite, Hittite, Perizzite, Hivite, and Jebusite,

first_reading.proposed: I will send an angel before you, that I may drive out the Canaanite, Amorite, Hittite, Perizzite, Hivite, and Jebusite,
first_reading.reason: "ut ejiciam" is first person, 'that I may drive out'; the English infinitive reads as though the angel drives the nations out.

second_reading.note: "ut ejiciam" is first person singular; the bare infinitive reads as the angel driving them out.

corrections.proposed_english: I will send an angel before you, that I may drive out the Canaanite, Amorite, Hittite, Perizzite, Hivite, and Jebusite,

corrections.latin: Dixitque Dominus ad Moysen : Loquere filiis Israël : Populus duræ cervicis es : semel ascendam in medio tui, et delebo te. Jam nunc depone ornatum tuum, ut sciam quid faciam tibi.
corrections.english: The Lord said to Moses, “Tell the children of Israel: ‘You are a stiff-necked people. Were I to go up among you for a moment, I would destroy you. Now remove your ornaments, so that I may know what to do with you.’”

first_reading.proposed: The Lord said to Moses, “Tell the children of Israel: ‘You are a stiff-necked people. Once I shall go up in your midst and destroy you. Now remove your ornaments, so that I may know what to do with you.’”
first_reading.reason: "semel ascendam in medio tui, et delebo te": future indicatives, and semel is 'once'; the hypothetical 'Were I to go up … for a moment, I would' follows the Hebrew.

second_reading.note: "semel ascendam in medio tui, et delebo te": semel is once, delebo a plain future; the counterfactual "for a moment ... would" is the Hebrew.

corrections.proposed_english: The Lord said to Moses, “Tell the children of Israel: ‘You are a stiff-necked people. Once I shall go up in your midst and destroy you. Now remove your ornaments, so that I may know what to do with you.’”

corrections.latin: In quo enim scire poterimus ego et populus tuus invenisse nos gratiam in conspectu tuo, nisi ambulaveris nobiscum, ut glorificemur ab omnibus populis qui habitant super terram ?
corrections.english: For how can we know, I and Your people, that we have found favor in Your sight unless You walk with us, so that we may be distinguished in glory from all peoples dwelling upon the earth?”

first_reading.proposed: For how can we know, I and Your people, that we have found favor in Your sight unless You walk with us, so that we may be glorified by all peoples dwelling upon the earth?”
first_reading.reason: "ut glorificemur ab omnibus populis" is 'that we may be glorified by all peoples' (ab of agent); 'distinguished … from all peoples' follows the Hebrew.

second_reading.note: "ut glorificemur ab omnibus populis" is glorified by all peoples (ab of agent); "distinguished from" is the Hebrew reading.

corrections.proposed_english: For how can we know, I and Your people, that we have found favor in Your sight unless You walk with us, so that we may be glorified by all peoples dwelling upon the earth?”

corrections.latin: Craticulamque ejus in modum retis fecit æneam, et subter eam in altaris medio arulam,
corrections.english: He made its bronze grating like a net, and beneath it a ledge halfway up the altar.

first_reading.proposed: He made its bronze grating like a net, and beneath it a hearth halfway up the altar.
first_reading.reason: "subter eam in altaris medio arulam": arula is the hearth (fire-pan) of the altar, not a 'ledge'; 'ledge' reflects the Hebrew term rather than this Latin (same word at 27:5).

second_reading.note: "subter eam in altaris medio arulam": arula is a hearth or fire-pan, not a ledge.

corrections.proposed_english: He made its bronze grating like a net, and beneath it a hearth halfway up the altar.

corrections.latin: Præcipe Aaron et filiis ejus : Hæc est lex holocausti : cremabitur in altari tota nocte usque mane : ignis ex eodem altari erit.
corrections.english: Command Aaron and his sons: This is the law of the whole burnt offering. It shall burn upon the altar all night until morning; the fire shall remain on that same altar.

first_reading.proposed: Command Aaron and his sons: This is the law of the whole burnt offering. It shall burn upon the altar all night until morning; the fire shall be from that same altar.
first_reading.reason: "ignis ex eodem altari erit" says the fire shall be of/from that same altar (its source); "shall remain on that same altar" misrenders "ex ... erit" and echoes the Hebrew sense instead.

second_reading.note: "ignis ex eodem altari erit": ex gives the source and erit is "shall be"; "shall remain on" follows the Hebrew.

corrections.proposed_english: Command Aaron and his sons: This is the law of the whole burnt offering. It shall burn upon the altar all night until morning; the fire shall be from that same altar.

corrections.latin: Hæc est unctio Aaron et filiorum ejus in cæremoniis Domini die qua obtulit eos Moyses, ut sacerdotio fungerentur,
corrections.english: This is the portion belonging to Aaron and his sons by their anointing in the Lord's sacred rites, from the day Moses presented them to exercise the priesthood.

first_reading.proposed: This is the anointing of Aaron and his sons in the Lord's sacred rites, on the day Moses presented them to exercise the priesthood.
first_reading.reason: "Hæc est unctio Aaron et filiorum ejus ... die qua" = this is the anointing ... on the day; English adds "the portion belonging to ... by" (Hebrew-based sense) and turns "die qua" into "from the day".

second_reading.note: "Hæc est unctio Aaron et filiorum ejus ... die qua": no "portion belonging to" in the Latin, and die qua is "on the day".

corrections.proposed_english: This is the anointing of Aaron and his sons in the Lord's sacred rites, on the day Moses presented them to exercise the priesthood.

corrections.latin: Quidquid super pectus quadrupes graditur, et multos habet pedes, sive per humum trahitur, non comedetis, quia abominabile est.
corrections.english: Whatever moves upon its belly, goes on four feet, has many feet, or drags itself along the ground, you shall not eat, because it is abhorrent.

first_reading.proposed: Whatever goes upon its breast on four feet, has many feet, or drags itself along the ground, you shall not eat, because it is abhorrent.
first_reading.reason: "super pectus quadrupes graditur" is one class (a four-footed thing going on its breast); English splits it into "moves upon its belly, goes on four feet" as in the Hebrew, and "pectus" is breast, not belly.

second_reading.note: "super pectus quadrupes graditur" is one class, a quadruped going on its breast; the English splits it and turns pectus into belly.

corrections.proposed_english: Whatever goes upon its breast on four feet, has many feet, or drags itself along the ground, you shall not eat, because it is abhorrent.

corrections.latin: extra velum testimonii in tabernaculo fœderis. Ponetque eas Aaron a vespere usque ad mane coram Domino, cultu rituque perpetuo in generationibus vestris.
corrections.english: outside the veil of the testimony in the tabernacle of the covenant. Aaron shall tend them before the Lord from evening until morning, as a perpetual observance and rite throughout your generations.

first_reading.proposed: outside the veil of the testimony in the tabernacle of the covenant. Aaron shall set them before the Lord from evening until morning, as a perpetual observance and rite throughout your generations.
first_reading.reason: "Ponetque eas Aaron" = Aaron shall set/place them (the lamps); "tend" is not a sense of "ponere" (compare "ponentur" rendered "set" in the next verse).

second_reading.note: "Ponetque eas Aaron": ponere is to set or place; "tend" is not a sense of the verb.

corrections.proposed_english: outside the veil of the testimony in the tabernacle of the covenant. Aaron shall set them before the Lord from evening until morning, as a perpetual observance and rite throughout your generations.

corrections.latin: Mortui sunt enim Nadab et Abiu cum offerrent ignem alienum in conspectu Domini in deserto Sinai, absque liberis : functique sunt sacerdotio Eleazar et Ithamar coram Aaron patre suo.
corrections.english: For Nadab and Abihu died when they offered unauthorized fire before the Lord in the wilderness of Sinai, without children; Eleazar and Ithamar exercised the priesthood in the presence of Aaron their father.

first_reading.proposed: For Nadab and Abihu died when they offered strange fire before the Lord in the wilderness of Sinai, without children; Eleazar and Ithamar exercised the priesthood in the presence of Aaron their father.
first_reading.reason: "ignem alienum" is strange/foreign fire; "unauthorized" is an interpretive gloss (modern versions of the Hebrew), not a sense of "alienum".

second_reading.note: "ignem alienum" is strange or alien fire; "unauthorized" is an interpretive gloss, not a sense of alienus.

corrections.proposed_english: For Nadab and Abihu died when they offered strange fire before the Lord in the wilderness of Sinai, without children; Eleazar and Ithamar exercised the priesthood in the presence of Aaron their father.

corrections.latin: Castrametabuntur ante tabernaculum fœderis, id est, ad orientalem plagam, Moyses et Aaron cum filiis suis, habentes custodiam sanctuarii in medio filiorum Israël. Quisquis alienus accesserit, morietur.
corrections.english: Before the tabernacle of the covenant, that is, on the eastern side, Moses and Aaron shall camp with Aaron's sons, keeping charge of the sanctuary among the children of Israel. Any outsider who approaches shall die.

first_reading.proposed: Before the tabernacle of the covenant, that is, on the eastern side, Moses and Aaron shall camp with their sons, keeping charge of the sanctuary among the children of Israel. Any outsider who approaches shall die.
first_reading.reason: "cum filiis suis" = with their sons (of Moses and Aaron, the subject); English narrows it to "Aaron's sons", as in the Hebrew.

second_reading.note: "Moyses et Aaron cum filiis suis": reflexive suis refers to both subjects, their sons; "Aaron's sons" narrows it after the Hebrew.

corrections.proposed_english: Before the tabernacle of the covenant, that is, on the eastern side, Moses and Aaron shall camp with their sons, keeping charge of the sanctuary among the children of Israel. Any outsider who approaches shall die.

corrections.latin: Cumque steterit mulier in conspectu Domini, discooperiet caput ejus, et ponet super manus illius sacrificium recordationis, et oblationem zelotypiæ : ipse autem tenebit aquas amarissimas, in quibus cum execratione maledicta congessit.
corrections.english: When the woman stands before the Lord, he shall uncover her head and place in her hands the sacrifice of remembrance and offering of jealousy. He himself shall hold the bitter water into which he has gathered the curses with an imprecation.

first_reading.proposed: When the woman stands before the Lord, he shall uncover her head and place in her hands the sacrifice of remembrance and offering of jealousy. He himself shall hold the most bitter water into which he has gathered the curses with an imprecation.
first_reading.reason: "aquas amarissimas" is superlative, most bitter waters; English has only "bitter" (as the Hebrew).

second_reading.note: "aquas amarissimas" is superlative; the English gives only "bitter".

corrections.proposed_english: When the woman stands before the Lord, he shall uncover her head and place in her hands the sacrifice of remembrance and offering of jealousy. He himself shall hold the most bitter water into which he has gathered the curses with an imprecation.

corrections.latin: Adjurabitque eam, et dicet : Si non dormivit vir alienus tecum, et si non polluta es deserto mariti thoro, non te nocebunt aquæ istæ amarissimæ, in quas maledicta congessi.
corrections.english: He shall put her under oath and say: If no other man has slept with you, and you have not been defiled by forsaking your husband's bed, this bitter water into which I have gathered curses shall not harm you.

first_reading.proposed: He shall put her under oath and say: If no other man has slept with you, and you have not been defiled by forsaking your husband's bed, this most bitter water into which I have gathered curses shall not harm you.
first_reading.reason: "aquæ istæ amarissimæ" is superlative, most bitter; English has only "bitter".

second_reading.note: "aquæ istæ amarissimæ" is superlative; the English gives only "bitter".

corrections.proposed_english: He shall put her under oath and say: If no other man has slept with you, and you have not been defiled by forsaking your husband's bed, this most bitter water into which I have gathered curses shall not harm you.

corrections.latin: purificatique sunt, et laverunt vestimenta sua. Elevavitque eos Aaron in conspectu Domini, et oravit pro eis,
corrections.english: They were purified and washed their clothes. Aaron presented them before the Lord and prayed for them,

first_reading.proposed: They were purified and washed their clothes. Aaron lifted them up before the Lord and prayed for them,
first_reading.reason: "Elevavitque eos" = lifted/raised them up (the elevation gesture); "presented" is not a sense of "elevare" and follows modern versions of the Hebrew.

second_reading.note: "Elevavitque eos Aaron": elevare is to lift up; "presented" is not a sense of the verb.

corrections.proposed_english: They were purified and washed their clothes. Aaron lifted them up before the Lord and prayed for them,

corrections.latin: Moveruntque castra primi juxta imperium Domini in manu Moysi.
corrections.english: They moved camp for the first time according to the Lord's command through Moses.

first_reading.proposed: The first moved camp according to the Lord's command through Moses.
first_reading.reason: "primi" is nominative plural, the first (to move camp), introducing Judah in v.14; "for the first time" renders the Hebrew adverb, not this Latin.

second_reading.note: "Moveruntque castra primi": primi is nominative plural, the first to move; "for the first time" (primum) is the Hebrew adverb.

corrections.proposed_english: The first moved camp according to the Lord's command through Moses.

corrections.latin: Ascenderuntque ad meridiem, et venerunt in Hebron, ubi erant Achiman et Sisai et Tholmai filii Enac : nam Hebron septem annis ante Tanim urbem Ægypti condita est.
corrections.english: They went up through the south and came to Hebron, where Ahiman, Sheshai, and Talmai, sons of Anak, were. Hebron had been founded seven years before Tanis, the city of Egypt.

first_reading.proposed: They went up to the south and came to Hebron, where Ahiman, Sheshai, and Talmai, sons of Anak, were. Hebron had been founded seven years before Tanis, the city of Egypt.
first_reading.reason: "ad meridiem" = to/toward the south; "through the south" follows the Hebrew phrasing, not the Latin "ad".

second_reading.note: "Ascenderuntque ad meridiem": ad is to or toward, not through.

corrections.proposed_english: They went up to the south and came to Hebron, where Ahiman, Sheshai, and Talmai, sons of Anak, were. Hebron had been founded seven years before Tanis, the city of Egypt.

corrections.latin: Pergentesque usque ad Torrentem botri, absciderunt palmitem cum uva sua, quem portaverunt in vecte duo viri. De malis quoque granatis et de ficis loci illius tulerunt :
corrections.english: They continued to the Valley of the Cluster and cut off a vine branch with its cluster of grapes, which two men carried on a pole. They also took pomegranates and figs from that place,

first_reading.proposed: They continued to the Torrent of the Cluster and cut off a vine branch with its cluster of grapes, which two men carried on a pole. They also took pomegranates and figs from that place,
first_reading.reason: "Torrentem botri": torrens is a torrent/brook, not a valley; "Valley" reflects the Hebrew place-name convention.

second_reading.note: "usque ad Torrentem botri": torrens is a torrent or brook, not a valley.

corrections.proposed_english: They continued to the Torrent of the Cluster and cut off a vine branch with its cluster of grapes, which two men carried on a pole. They also took pomegranates and figs from that place,

corrections.latin: qui appellatus est Nehelescol, id est Torrens botri, eo quod botrum portassent inde filii Israël.
corrections.english: which was called Nehelescol, that is, Valley of the Cluster, because the children of Israel carried a cluster from there.

first_reading.proposed: which was called Nehelescol, that is, Torrent of the Cluster, because the children of Israel carried a cluster from there.
first_reading.reason: "Torrens botri": torrens is a torrent/brook, not a valley.

second_reading.note: "id est Torrens botri": torrens is a torrent or brook, not a valley.

corrections.proposed_english: which was called Nehelescol, that is, Torrent of the Cluster, because the children of Israel carried a cluster from there.

corrections.latin: Misitque Moyses qui explorarent Jazer : cujus ceperunt viculos, et possederunt habitatores.
corrections.english: Moses sent men to explore Jazer. They captured its villages and dispossessed its inhabitants.

first_reading.proposed: Moses sent men to explore Jazer. They captured its villages and took possession of its inhabitants.
first_reading.reason: "possederunt habitatores" = took possession of (subdued) the inhabitants; "dispossessed" follows the Hebrew (drove out), not the Latin.

second_reading.note: "possederunt habitatores" is took possession of the inhabitants; "dispossessed" (drove out) is the Hebrew sense.

corrections.proposed_english: Moses sent men to explore Jazer. They captured its villages and took possession of its inhabitants.

corrections.latin: assumptaque parabola sua, dixit : [De Aram adduxit me Balac rex Moabitarum, de montibus orientis : Veni, inquit, et maledic Jacob ; propera, et detestare Israël.
corrections.english: Taking up his oracle, he said: Balak king of the Moabites brought me from Aram, from the eastern mountains. Come, he said, and curse Jacob; hurry and denounce Israel.

first_reading.proposed: Taking up his parable, he said: Balak king of the Moabites brought me from Aram, from the eastern mountains. Come, he said, and curse Jacob; hurry and denounce Israel.
first_reading.reason: "assumptaque parabola sua": parabola is a parable/figurative discourse; "oracle" is the modern versions' term for the Hebrew, not a sense of the Latin word.

second_reading.note: "assumptaque parabola sua": parabola is a parable or figurative discourse; "oracle" is not a sense of the word.

corrections.proposed_english: Taking up his parable, he said: Balak king of the Moabites brought me from Aram, from the eastern mountains. Come, he said, and curse Jacob; hurry and denounce Israel.

corrections.latin: At ille, assumpta parabola sua, ait : [Sta, Balac, et ausculta ; audi, fili Sephor :
corrections.english: Taking up his oracle, he said: Stand, Balak, and listen; hear, son of Zippor.

first_reading.proposed: Taking up his parable, he said: Stand, Balak, and listen; hear, son of Zippor.
first_reading.reason: "assumpta parabola sua": parabola is a parable/figurative discourse, not "oracle" (as at 23:7).

second_reading.note: "assumpta parabola sua": parabola is parable, not oracle.

second_reading.note: 'in holocaustum sempiternum' is in with accusative, for/as a perpetual holocaust; 'with the continual burnt offering' is the Hebrew 'besides', not this Latin.

corrections.proposed_english: which are duly poured out each Sabbath as a continual burnt offering.

corrections.latin: Hircus quoque offeretur Domino pro peccatis in holocaustum sempiternum cum libamentis suis.

first_reading.reason: "in holocaustum sempiternum cum libamentis suis": offered for/as a perpetual burnt offering with its libations; English "with the continual burnt offering and its drink offerings" follows the Hebrew, not the Latin.

second_reading.note: 'offeretur ... in holocaustum sempiternum cum libamentis suis': offered as a perpetual holocaust with its libations; current 'with the continual burnt offering and' follows the Hebrew.

corrections.proposed_english: A male goat shall also be offered to the Lord for sins as a continual burnt offering with its drink offerings.

corrections.latin: quo die audierit vir, et non contradixerit, voti rea erit, reddetque quodcumque promiserat.

second_reading.note: 'quo die audierit vir, et non contradixerit': on whatever day he hears; 'hears it that day' wrongly fixes his hearing to the day of the vow.

corrections.proposed_english: and on the day her husband hears it he does not object, she shall be bound by the vow and render whatever she promised.

corrections.latin: et de Sephama descendent termini in Rebla contra fontem Daphnim : inde pervenient contra orientem ad mare Cenereth,

first_reading.reason: "pervenient contra orientem ad mare Cenereth": they shall come eastward to the sea of Chinnereth; "the eastern side of the Sea" follows the Hebrew (shoulder of the sea), not the Latin.

second_reading.note: 'pervenient contra orientem ad mare Cenereth': reach eastward to the sea; 'the eastern side of the Sea' is the Hebrew 'shoulder of the sea', not the Latin.

corrections.proposed_english: From Shepham the borders shall descend to Riblah opposite the spring of Daphnim. From there they shall reach eastward to the Sea of Chinnereth

corrections.latin: vastantes cunctas civitates illius uno tempore. Non fuit oppidum, quod nos effugeret : sexaginta urbes, omnem regionem Argob regni Og in Basan.
corrections.english: laying waste all his cities at that time. No town escaped us: sixty cities, the entire region of Argob, the kingdom of Og in Bashan.

first_reading.proposed: laying waste all his cities at one time. No town escaped us: sixty cities, the entire region of Argob, the kingdom of Og in Bashan.
first_reading.reason: "uno tempore" means at one time, all at once; "at that time" renders the Hebrew phrase (illo tempore), not this Latin.

second_reading.note: 'uno tempore' is 'at one time'; 'at that time' would be 'illo tempore' and follows the Hebrew.

corrections.proposed_english: laying waste all his cities at one time. No town escaped us: sixty cities, the entire region of Argob, the kingdom of Og in Bashan.

corrections.english: also the wilderness plain, the Jordan and its territory, from Chinnereth to the sea of the wilderness, which is exceedingly salty, at the foot of Mount Pisgah to the east.

corrections.proposed_english: also the wilderness plain, and the Jordan, and the borders of Chinnereth as far as the sea of the wilderness, which is exceedingly salty, at the foot of Mount Pisgah to the east.

corrections.latin: Cum acceperit homo nuper uxorem, non procedet ad bellum, nec ei quippiam necessitatis injungetur publicæ, sed vacabit absque culpa domi suæ, ut uno anno lætetur cum uxore sua.
corrections.english: When a man has recently married a wife, he shall not go out to war or be assigned any public duty. He shall remain at home free of obligation, to rejoice with his wife for one year.

first_reading.proposed: When a man has recently married a wife, he shall not go out to war or be assigned any public duty. He shall be free at home without blame, to rejoice with his wife for one year.
first_reading.reason: 'vacabit absque culpa domi suae' = he shall be free at home without blame; 'absque culpa' (without fault) is not rendered, 'free of obligation' only covers 'vacabit'.

second_reading.note: 'vacabit absque culpa domi suae': 'absque culpa' (without blame) is not rendered; 'free of obligation' covers only 'vacabit'.

corrections.proposed_english: When a man has recently married a wife, he shall not go out to war or be assigned any public duty. He shall be free at home without blame, to rejoice with his wife for one year.

corrections.latin: Si deprehensus fuerit homo sollicitans fratrem suum de filiis Israël, et vendito eo acceperit pretium, interficietur, et auferes malum de medio tui.
corrections.english: If a man is caught kidnapping his brother from among the children of Israel and receiving money from selling him, he shall be killed. Remove the evil from your midst.

second_reading.note: 'sollicitans fratrem suum' is enticing or luring away, a distinctive Vulgate wording; 'kidnapping' renders the Hebrew 'stealing', not sollicitare.

corrections.proposed_english: If a man is caught enticing away his brother from among the children of Israel and receiving money from selling him, he shall be killed. Remove the evil from your midst.

corrections.proposed_english: His name shall be called in Israel: The House of the Unsandaled Man.

corrections.latin: Cumque audierit verba juramenti hujus, benedicat sibi in corde suo, dicens : Pax erit mihi, et ambulabo in pravitate cordis mei : et absumat ebria sitientem,

second_reading.note: 'Pax erit mihi, et ambulabo' are two coordinate futures; concessive 'though I walk' follows the Hebrew/KJV, not 'et ambulabo'.

corrections.proposed_english: Let no one who hears the words of this oath bless himself in his heart, saying: I will have peace, and I will walk in the perversity of my heart, so that the drunken one consumes the thirsty.

corrections.proposed_english: and consume him to destruction out of all the tribes of Israel, according to the curses contained in this book of the law and covenant.

corrections.proposed_english: all Naphtali, the land of Ephraim and Manasseh, and all the land of Judah as far as the farthest sea,

corrections.proposed_english: The boundary rises to Beth-hoglah and passes on the north to Beth-arabah, going up to the stone of Bohan son of Reuben.

corrections.proposed_english: Ebron, Rehob, Hammon, and Kanah, as far as Great Sidon.

corrections.proposed_english: He said to them, “Do what you see me do. I will enter a part of the camp; follow what I do.

corrections.latin: Ingressusque est Gedeon, et trecenti viri qui erant cum eo, in partem castrorum, incipientibus vigiliis noctis mediæ : et custodibus suscitatis, cœperunt buccinis clangere, et complodere inter se lagenas.

corrections.proposed_english: Gideon and the three hundred men with him entered a part of the camp at the beginning of the middle watch of the night, when the guards had been roused. They began to sound their trumpets and smash their jars together.

second_reading.note: 'adolescentis Levitae, qui erat in domo Michae': masculine 'qui' refers to the Levite; feminine 'domum' would need 'quae', so 'which' is wrong.

corrections.proposed_english: They turned aside a little and entered the house of the young Levite, who was in Micah's household, and greeted him with words of peace.

corrections.latin: Erat autem viro Elimelech consanguineus, homo potens, et magnarum opum, nomine Booz.

second_reading.note: 'Erat autem viro Elimelech consanguineus': 'viro' (husband, of Naomi just named) is left untranslated in the current English.

corrections.proposed_english: Her husband Elimelech had a kinsman named Boaz, a powerful man of great wealth.

corrections.latin: Et addidit Dominus ut appareret in Silo, quoniam revelatus fuerat Dominus Samueli in Silo juxta verbum Domini. Et evenit sermo Samuelis universo Israëli.

second_reading.note: 'juxta verbum Domini' is according to the word; instrumental 'through the word' follows the Hebrew/KJV 'by', not 'juxta'.

corrections.proposed_english: The Lord continued to appear at Shiloh, for the Lord had revealed Himself to Samuel at Shiloh according to the word of the Lord. And Samuel's word came to all Israel.

corrections.latin: Væ nobis : non enim fuit tanta exultatio heri et nudiustertius : væ nobis. Quis nos salvabit de manu deorum sublimium istorum ? hi sunt dii, qui percusserunt Ægyptum omni plaga in deserto.
corrections.english: “Woe to us! There was no such rejoicing yesterday or the day before. Woe to us! Who will save us from the hand of these mighty gods? These are the gods who struck Egypt with every plague in the wilderness.

first_reading.reason: "deorum sublimium istorum" = these lofty/exalted gods; "mighty gods" reflects the Hebrew (and KJV) wording rather than the Latin "sublimium".

second_reading.note: 'deorum sublimium istorum': sublimis is lofty or exalted, not 'mighty', which is the Hebrew/KJV word.

corrections.proposed_english: “Woe to us! There was no such rejoicing yesterday or the day before. Woe to us! Who will save us from the hand of these exalted gods? These are the gods who struck Egypt with every plague in the wilderness.

corrections.latin: Miseruntque nuntios ad habitatores Cariathiarim, dicentes : Reduxerunt Philisthiim arcam Domini : descendite, et reducite eam ad vos.

first_reading.reason: Latin 'reducite eam ad vos' = 'bring it back to you' (same verb as 'reduxerunt' just before); 'take it up' follows the Hebrew/KJV 'bring it up'.

second_reading.note: 'reducite eam ad vos' repeats 'reduxerunt': bring it back; 'take it up' follows the Hebrew 'bring up'.

corrections.proposed_english: They sent messengers to the inhabitants of Kiriath-jearim, saying, “The Philistines have brought back the ark of the Lord. Come down and bring it back to yourselves.”

corrections.latin: Venerunt ergo viri Cariathiarim, et reduxerunt arcam Domini, et intulerunt eam in domum Abinadab in Gabaa : Eleazarum autem filium ejus sanctificaverunt, ut custodiret arcam Domini.
corrections.english: The men of Kiriath-jearim came and took up the ark of the Lord. They brought it into Abinadab's house at Gibeah and consecrated his son Eleazar to guard the ark of the Lord.

first_reading.proposed: The men of Kiriath-jearim came and brought back the ark of the Lord. They brought it into Abinadab's house at Gibeah and consecrated his son Eleazar to guard the ark of the Lord.
first_reading.reason: Latin 'reduxerunt arcam Domini' = 'brought back the ark'; 'took up' reflects the Hebrew 'brought up', not the Vulgate's verb.

second_reading.note: 'reduxerunt arcam Domini' is brought back the ark; 'took up' renders the Hebrew verb, not reducere.

corrections.proposed_english: The men of Kiriath-jearim came and brought back the ark of the Lord. They brought it into Abinadab's house at Gibeah and consecrated his son Eleazar to guard the ark of the Lord.

corrections.latin: Et egressi sunt ad prædandum de castris Philisthinorum tres cunei. Unus cuneus pergebat contra viam Ephra ad terram Sual :
corrections.english: Three companies went out from the Philistine camp to plunder. One company took the road toward Ophrah, in the land of Shual.

first_reading.proposed: Three companies went out from the Philistine camp to plunder. One company took the road toward Ophrah, to the land of Shual.
first_reading.reason: Latin 'ad terram Sual' gives the direction of the march ('to the land of Shual'); 'in the land of Shual' makes it the location of Ophrah.

second_reading.note: 'pergebat ... ad terram Sual': ad with accusative gives the goal of the march; 'in the land of Shual' makes it Ophrah's location.

corrections.proposed_english: Three companies went out from the Philistine camp to plunder. One company took the road toward Ophrah, to the land of Shual.

corrections.latin: Egressa est autem statio Philisthiim, ut transcenderet in Machmas.
corrections.english: A Philistine outpost went out to the crossing at Michmash.

first_reading.proposed: A Philistine outpost went out to cross over into Michmash.
first_reading.reason: Latin 'ut transcenderet in Machmas' is a purpose clause, 'to cross over into Michmash'; 'to the crossing at Michmash' renders the Hebrew noun ('pass of Michmash').

second_reading.note: 'ut transcenderet in Machmas' is a purpose clause with a verb; 'to the crossing at Michmash' renders the Hebrew noun 'pass'.

corrections.proposed_english: A Philistine outpost went out to cross over into Michmash.

corrections.latin: Et factum est miraculum in castris per agros : sed et omnis populus stationis eorum qui ierant ad prædandum, obstupuit, et conturbata est terra : et accidit quasi miraculum a Deo.
corrections.english: A wonder occurred in the camp throughout the fields. All the people of the outpost and those who had gone out to plunder were stunned, and the earth was shaken. It happened like a wonder from God.

first_reading.proposed: A wonder occurred in the camp throughout the fields. All the people of their outpost who had gone out to plunder were stunned, and the earth was shaken. It happened like a wonder from God.
first_reading.reason: Latin 'omnis populus stationis eorum qui ierant ad prædandum' is one group (no 'et'); 'the outpost and those who had gone out to plunder' makes two groups, as in the Hebrew.

second_reading.note: 'omnis populus stationis eorum qui ierant ad praedandum' is one group with no 'et'; current 'the outpost and those who' makes two, as in the Hebrew.

corrections.proposed_english: A wonder occurred in the camp throughout the fields. All the people of their outpost who had gone out to plunder were stunned, and the earth was shaken. It happened like a wonder from God.

corrections.latin: Misit ergo Saul nuntios ad Isai, dicens : Mitte ad me David filium tuum, qui est in pascuis.
corrections.english: Saul sent messengers to Jesse, saying, “Send me your son David, who is with the flocks.”

first_reading.proposed: Saul sent messengers to Jesse, saying, “Send me your son David, who is in the pastures.”
first_reading.reason: Latin 'qui est in pascuis' = 'who is in the pastures'; 'with the flocks' renders the Hebrew ('with the sheep'), not the Vulgate.

second_reading.note: 'qui est in pascuis': pascua are pastures; 'with the flocks' renders the Hebrew 'with the sheep'.

corrections.proposed_english: Saul sent messengers to Jesse, saying, “Send me your son David, who is in the pastures.”

corrections.latin: Et revertentes filii Israël postquam persecuti fuerant Philisthæos, invaserunt castra eorum.
corrections.english: The Israelites returned from pursuing the Philistines and plundered their camp.

first_reading.proposed: The Israelites returned from pursuing the Philistines and fell upon their camp.
first_reading.reason: Latin 'invaserunt castra eorum' = 'fell upon/invaded their camp'; 'plundered' renders the Hebrew ('spoiled their tents'), not 'invaserunt'.

second_reading.note: 'invaserunt castra eorum': invadere is to fall upon or seize; 'plundered' is the Hebrew verb, not this Latin.

corrections.proposed_english: The Israelites returned from pursuing the Philistines and fell upon their camp.

corrections.latin: Ascenderunt autem Ziphæi ad Saul in Gabaa, dicentes : Nonne ecce David latitat apud nos in locis tutissimis silvæ, in colle Hachila, quæ est ad dexteram deserti ?
corrections.english: The Ziphites went up to Saul at Gibeah, saying, “Is David not hiding among us in the secure places of the forest, on the hill of Hachilah, south of the wilderness?

first_reading.proposed: The Ziphites went up to Saul at Gibeah, saying, “Is David not hiding among us in the secure places of the forest, on the hill of Hachilah, on the right of the wilderness?
first_reading.reason: Latin 'ad dexteram deserti' = 'on the right hand of the wilderness'; 'south of' is the modern rendering of the Hebrew idiom, not what the Latin says.

second_reading.note: 'ad dexteram deserti' says on the right of the desert; dextera has no sense 'south', which interprets the Hebrew idiom behind it.

corrections.proposed_english: The Ziphites went up to Saul at Gibeah, saying, “Is David not hiding among us in the secure places of the forest, on the hill of Hachilah, on the right of the wilderness?

corrections.latin: At illi surgentes abierunt in Ziph ante Saul : David autem et viri ejus erant in deserto Maon, in campestribus ad dexteram Jesimon.
corrections.english: They rose and went to Ziph ahead of Saul. David and his men were in the wilderness of Maon, in the plains south of Jeshimon.

first_reading.proposed: They rose and went to Ziph ahead of Saul. David and his men were in the wilderness of Maon, in the plains on the right of Jeshimon.
first_reading.reason: Latin 'ad dexteram Jesimon' = 'on the right hand of Jeshimon'; 'south of' interprets the Hebrew idiom rather than rendering the Latin.

second_reading.note: 'ad dexteram Jesimon' is on the right of Jeshimon; 'south of' interprets the Hebrew idiom, as at 23:19.

corrections.proposed_english: They rose and went to Ziph ahead of Saul. David and his men were in the wilderness of Maon, in the plains on the right of Jeshimon.

corrections.latin: Et nunc retribuet vobis quidem Dominus misericordiam et veritatem : sed et ego reddam gratiam, eo quod fecistis verbum istud.
corrections.english: Now may the Lord repay you with mercy and faithfulness. I too will repay your kindness, because you have done this.

first_reading.proposed: Now the Lord will indeed repay you with mercy and faithfulness. I too will repay your kindness, because you have done this.
first_reading.reason: Latin 'retribuet vobis quidem Dominus' is future indicative ('the Lord will indeed repay you'), parallel to 'et ego reddam'; the English turns it into a wish ('may the Lord repay'), as in the Hebrew.

second_reading.note: 'retribuet vobis quidem Dominus' is future indicative with 'quidem', parallel to 'reddam'; the wish 'may the Lord repay' follows the Hebrew.

corrections.proposed_english: Now the Lord will indeed repay you with mercy and faithfulness. I too will repay your kindness, because you have done this.

corrections.latin: Dixit quoque rex ad servos suos : Num ignoratis quoniam princeps et maximus cecidit hodie in Israël ?
corrections.english: The king also said to his servants, “Do you not know that a prince and a great man have fallen today in Israel?

first_reading.proposed: The king also said to his servants, “Do you not know that a prince and a great man has fallen today in Israel?
first_reading.reason: Latin 'princeps et maximus cecidit' is singular, one man (Abner); plural 'have fallen' reads as two persons. Should be 'has fallen'.

second_reading.note: 'princeps et maximus cecidit' is singular, one man (Abner); plural 'have fallen' wrongly suggests two persons.

corrections.proposed_english: The king also said to his servants, “Do you not know that a prince and a great man has fallen today in Israel?

corrections.latin: quoniam eum qui annuntiaverat mihi, et dixerat : Mortuus est Saul : qui putabat se prospera nuntiare, tenui, et occidi eum in Siceleg, cui oportebat mercedem dare pro nuntio.
corrections.english: the man who brought me news, saying, ‘Saul is dead,’ thought he was bringing good news. I seized and killed him at Ziklag, though he expected a reward for his report.

first_reading.proposed: the man who brought me news, saying, ‘Saul is dead,’ thought he was bringing good news. I seized and killed him at Ziklag, though he ought to have been given a reward for his report.
first_reading.reason: Latin 'cui oportebat mercedem dare pro nuntio' = 'to whom a reward ought to have been given for the news'; the English substitutes 'he expected a reward', which the Latin does not say.

second_reading.note: 'cui oportebat mercedem dare pro nuntio': oportebat is 'it was due', not 'he expected', which echoes the KJV.

corrections.proposed_english: the man who brought me news, saying, ‘Saul is dead,’ thought he was bringing good news. I seized and killed him at Ziklag, though he ought to have been given a reward for his report.

corrections.latin: Dixerunt autem ei servi sui : Quis est sermo quem fecisti ? propter infantem, cum adhuc viveret, jejunasti et flebas : mortuo autem puero, surrexisti, et comedisti panem.
corrections.english: His servants said to him, “What is this you have done? While the infant was still alive, you fasted and wept, but when the child died, you arose and ate bread.”

first_reading.proposed: His servants said to him, “What is this you have done? For the infant's sake, while he was still alive, you fasted and wept, but when the child died, you arose and ate bread.”
first_reading.reason: "propter infantem" (on account of / for the infant) is not rendered; the English keeps only the time clause "cum adhuc viveret".

second_reading.note: 'propter infantem ... jejunasti et flebas': the causal 'propter' is dropped; the current English keeps only the time clause 'cum adhuc viveret'.

corrections.proposed_english: His servants said to him, “What is this you have done? For the infant's sake, while he was still alive, you fasted and wept, but when the child died, you arose and ate bread.”

corrections.latin: Qui ait : Propter infantem, dum adhuc viveret, jejunavi et flevi : dicebam enim : Quis scit si forte donet eum mihi Dominus, et vivat infans ?
corrections.english: He said, “While the infant was still alive, I fasted and wept, for I said, ‘Who knows whether the Lord may grant him to me and the infant may live?’

first_reading.proposed: He said, “For the infant's sake, while he was still alive, I fasted and wept, for I said, ‘Who knows whether the Lord may grant him to me and the infant may live?’
first_reading.reason: "Propter infantem" (for the infant's sake) is omitted; only "dum adhuc viveret" is rendered.

second_reading.note: 'Propter infantem, dum adhuc viveret, jejunavi': the causal 'propter' is not rendered, as in 12:21.

corrections.proposed_english: He said, “For the infant's sake, while he was still alive, I fasted and wept, for I said, ‘Who knows whether the Lord may grant him to me and the infant may live?’

corrections.latin: Fugit autem Absalom. Et elevavit puer speculator oculos suos, et aspexit : et ecce populus multus veniebat per iter devium ex latere montis.
corrections.english: Absalom fled. The young watchman raised his eyes and looked, and a great crowd was coming by a winding road along the mountainside.

first_reading.proposed: Absalom fled. The young watchman raised his eyes and looked, and a great crowd was coming by an out-of-the-way road along the mountainside.
