first_reading.reason: "per iter devium" means by a by-way, a road off the main route (devius = out of the way), not a "winding" road.

second_reading.note: 'per iter devium': devius is off the main road, a byway; 'winding' is not a sense of the Latin word.

corrections.proposed_english: Absalom fled. The young watchman raised his eyes and looked, and a great crowd was coming by an out-of-the-way road along the mountainside.

corrections.latin: Heri venisti, et hodie compelleris nobiscum egredi ? ego autem vadam quo iturus sum : revertere, et reduc tecum fratres tuos, et Dominus faciet tecum misericordiam et veritatem, quia ostendisti gratiam et fidem.
corrections.english: You came yesterday, and today are you to be compelled to leave with us? I am going wherever I must go. Return and take your brothers back with you. May the Lord show you mercy and faithfulness, because you have shown kindness and fidelity.”

first_reading.proposed: You came yesterday, and today are you to be compelled to leave with us? I am going wherever I must go. Return and take your brothers back with you. The Lord will show you mercy and faithfulness, because you have shown kindness and fidelity.”
first_reading.reason: "Dominus faciet tecum misericordiam et veritatem" is future indicative, an assurance (the Lord will show), not the wish "May the Lord show".

second_reading.note: 'Dominus faciet tecum misericordiam et veritatem': faciet is future indicative, an assurance, not the wish 'May the Lord show'.

corrections.proposed_english: You came yesterday, and today are you to be compelled to leave with us? I am going wherever I must go. Return and take your brothers back with you. The Lord will show you mercy and faithfulness, because you have shown kindness and fidelity.”

corrections.latin: Et populum pauperem salvum facies : oculisque tuis excelsos humiliabis.
corrections.english: You will save an afflicted people and humble the lofty with Your eyes.

first_reading.proposed: You will save a poor people and humble the lofty with Your eyes.
first_reading.reason: "populum pauperem" is a poor people; "afflicted" is the Hebrew/KJV wording, not a sense of pauper.

second_reading.note: 'populum pauperem': pauper is poor; 'afflicted' is the Hebrew/KJV word and outside pauper's range.

corrections.proposed_english: You will save a poor people and humble the lofty with Your eyes.

corrections.latin: Et observa custodias Domini Dei tui, ut ambules in viis ejus : ut custodias cæremonias ejus, et præcepta ejus, et judicia, et testimonia, sicut scriptum est in lege Moysi : ut intelligas universa quæ facis, et quocumque te verteris :
corrections.english: Keep the observances of the Lord your God, walking in His ways and keeping His ceremonies, commandments, judgments, and testimonies, as written in the law of Moses, so that you may act wisely in everything you do and wherever you turn,

first_reading.proposed: Keep the observances of the Lord your God, walking in His ways and keeping His ceremonies, commandments, judgments, and testimonies, as written in the law of Moses, so that you may understand everything you do and wherever you turn,
first_reading.reason: "ut intelligas universa quæ facis" means that you may understand all you do; "act wisely in" replaces understanding with acting, nearer the Hebrew than the Latin.

second_reading.note: 'ut intelligas universa quae facis': intelligere is understand; 'act wisely in' follows the Hebrew verb, not the Latin.

corrections.proposed_english: Keep the observances of the Lord your God, walking in His ways and keeping His ceremonies, commandments, judgments, and testimonies, as written in the law of Moses, so that you may understand everything you do and wherever you turn,

corrections.latin: Et veniebant de cunctis populis ad audiendam sapientiam Salomonis, et ab universis regibus terræ qui audiebant sapientiam ejus.
corrections.english: People came from all nations to hear Solomon's wisdom, sent by all the kings of the earth who heard of his wisdom.

first_reading.proposed: People came from all nations to hear Solomon's wisdom, and from all the kings of the earth who heard of his wisdom.
first_reading.reason: "et ab universis regibus terræ" says only "and from all the kings of the earth"; "sent by" adds a verb the Latin lacks.

second_reading.note: 'et ab universis regibus terrae' is a second coordinate source; dropping 'et' and adding 'sent by' makes all the comers royal envoys.

corrections.proposed_english: People came from all nations to hear Solomon's wisdom, and from all the kings of the earth who heard of his wisdom.

corrections.latin: Et atrium majus rotundum trium ordinum de lapidibus sectis, et unius ordinis de dolata cedro : necnon et in atrio domus Domini interiori, et in porticu domus.
corrections.english: The great surrounding court had three courses of cut stones and one course of hewn cedar, as did the inner court of the Lord's house and the vestibule of the house.

first_reading.proposed: The great round court had three courses of cut stones and one course of hewn cedar, as did the inner court of the Lord's house and the vestibule of the house.
first_reading.reason: 'atrium majus rotundum' says the greater court was round; 'surrounding' is not a sense of 'rotundum' and reflects the Hebrew 'round about'.

second_reading.note: 'atrium majus rotundum': rotundum is round; 'surrounding' reflects the Hebrew 'round about', not this adjective.

corrections.proposed_english: The great round court had three courses of cut stones and one course of hewn cedar, as did the inner court of the Lord's house and the vestibule of the house.

corrections.latin: ut exaudias deprecationem servi tui et populi tui Israël, quodcumque oraverint in loco isto, et exaudies in loco habitaculi tui in cælo : et cum exaudieris, propitius eris.
corrections.english: Hear the supplication of Your servant and Your people Israel whenever they pray in this place. Hear in Your dwelling place in heaven, and when You hear, be merciful.

first_reading.proposed: Hear the supplication of Your servant and Your people Israel, whatever they pray for in this place. Hear in Your dwelling place in heaven, and when You hear, be merciful.
first_reading.reason: 'quodcumque oraverint' means 'whatsoever they shall pray for', the object of the prayer, not the temporal 'whenever they pray'.

second_reading.note: 'quodcumque oraverint' is whatever they pray for, the object of prayer; temporal 'whenever' would be 'quandocumque'.

corrections.proposed_english: Hear the supplication of Your servant and Your people Israel, whatever they pray for in this place. Hear in Your dwelling place in heaven, and when You hear, be merciful.

corrections.latin: Si fugerit populus tuus Israël inimicos suos (quia peccaturus est tibi), et agentes pœnitentiam, et confitentes nomini tuo, venerint, et oraverint, et deprecati te fuerint in domo hac :
corrections.english: If Your people Israel flee before their enemies because they have sinned against You, and they repent, acknowledge Your name, and come to pray and plead with You in this house,

first_reading.proposed: If Your people Israel flee before their enemies because they will sin against You, and they repent, acknowledge Your name, and come to pray and plead with You in this house,
first_reading.reason: 'quia peccaturus est tibi' is a future participle, 'because they will sin against You'; the English perfect 'have sinned' follows the Hebrew rather than this Latin.

second_reading.note: 'quia peccaturus est tibi' is a future periphrastic, 'because they will sin'; the perfect 'have sinned' follows the Hebrew.

corrections.proposed_english: If Your people Israel flee before their enemies because they will sin against You, and they repent, acknowledge Your name, and come to pray and plead with You in this house,

corrections.latin: Beati viri tui, et beati servi tui, qui stant coram te semper, et audiunt sapientiam tuam.
corrections.english: Happy are your men, and happy these servants of yours who stand before you continually and hear your wisdom.

first_reading.proposed: Happy are your men, and happy your servants who stand before you continually and hear your wisdom.
first_reading.reason: Latin has simply 'beati servi tui'; the demonstrative 'these servants of yours' is not in the Latin and reflects the Hebrew ('these your servants').

second_reading.note: 'beati servi tui' has no demonstrative; 'these servants of yours' adds the Hebrew 'these'.

corrections.proposed_english: Happy are your men, and happy your servants who stand before you continually and hear your wisdom.

corrections.latin: Delevitque Zambri omnem domum Baasa, juxta verbum Domini quod locutus fuerat ad Baasa in manu Jehu prophetæ,
corrections.english: Zimri destroyed the whole house of Baasha according to the word the Lord had spoken against Baasha through Jehu the prophet,

first_reading.proposed: Zimri destroyed the whole house of Baasha according to the word the Lord had spoken to Baasha through Jehu the prophet,
first_reading.reason: 'locutus fuerat ad Baasa' is 'had spoken to Baasha'; 'against Baasha' renders the Hebrew preposition, not the Latin 'ad' with a verb of speaking.

second_reading.note: 'locutus fuerat ad Baasa': loqui ad is speak to; 'against' renders the Hebrew preposition, not 'ad'.

corrections.proposed_english: Zimri destroyed the whole house of Baasha according to the word the Lord had spoken to Baasha through Jehu the prophet,

corrections.latin: Dixitque Elias ad eos : Apprehendite prophetas Baal, et ne unus quidem effugiat ex eis. Quos cum apprehendissent, duxit eos Elias ad torrentem Cison, et interfecit eos ibi.
corrections.english: Elijah said to them, “Seize Baal's prophets, and do not let even one of them escape.” When they seized them, Elijah led them down to the Kishon stream and killed them there.

first_reading.proposed: Elijah said to them, “Seize Baal's prophets, and do not let even one of them escape.” When they seized them, Elijah led them to the Kishon stream and killed them there.
first_reading.reason: 'duxit eos Elias ad torrentem Cison' is simply 'led them to the torrent'; 'down' is not in the Latin and comes from the Hebrew ('brought them down').

second_reading.note: 'duxit eos Elias ad torrentem Cison' is simply led them to the torrent; 'down' is added from the Hebrew verb.

corrections.proposed_english: Elijah said to them, “Seize Baal's prophets, and do not let even one of them escape.” When they seized them, Elijah led them to the Kishon stream and killed them there.

corrections.latin: Nonne vidisti humiliatum Achab coram me ? quia igitur humiliatus est mei causa, non inducam malum in diebus ejus, sed in diebus filii sui inferam malum domui ejus.
corrections.english: “Have you seen Ahab humbled before Me? Because he has humbled himself for My sake, I will not bring the calamity in his days; in his son's days I will bring calamity upon his house.”

first_reading.proposed: “Have you not seen Ahab humbled before Me? Because he has humbled himself for My sake, I will not bring the calamity in his days; in his son's days I will bring calamity upon his house.”
first_reading.reason: 'Nonne vidisti' is a negative question expecting yes, 'Have you not seen'; the English 'Have you seen' drops the negative, following the Hebrew form.

second_reading.note: 'Nonne vidisti' is a negative question expecting yes; 'Have you seen' drops the negative.

corrections.proposed_english: “Have you not seen Ahab humbled before Me? Because he has humbled himself for My sake, I will not bring the calamity in his days; in his son's days I will bring calamity upon his house.”

corrections.latin: Et ait Josaphat : Estne hic propheta Domini, ut deprecemur Dominum per eum ? Et respondit unus de servis regis Israël : Est hic Eliseus filius Saphat, qui fundebat aquam super manus Eliæ.
corrections.english: Jehoshaphat said, “Is there no prophet of the Lord here, through whom we may entreat the Lord?” One of the servants of the king of Israel answered, “Elisha son of Shaphat is here, who used to pour water over Elijah's hands.”

first_reading.proposed: Jehoshaphat said, “Is there a prophet of the Lord here, through whom we may entreat the Lord?” One of the servants of the king of Israel answered, “Elisha son of Shaphat is here, who used to pour water over Elijah's hands.”
first_reading.reason: 'Estne hic propheta Domini' is a plain positive question, 'Is there here a prophet of the Lord'; the negative 'Is there no prophet' follows the Hebrew form, not the Latin.

second_reading.note: 'Estne hic propheta Domini' is a plain question with enclitic -ne and no negative; 'Is there no prophet' adds the Hebrew's negation.

corrections.proposed_english: Jehoshaphat said, “Is there a prophet of the Lord here, through whom we may entreat the Lord?” One of the servants of the king of Israel answered, “Elisha son of Shaphat is here, who used to pour water over Elijah's hands.”

corrections.latin: Universi autem Moabitæ audientes quod ascendissent reges ut pugnarent adversum eos, convocaverunt omnes qui accincti erant balteo desuper, et steterunt in terminis.
corrections.english: All the Moabites heard that the kings had come up to fight against them. They summoned everyone old enough to wear a sword belt and took their stand at the borders.

first_reading.proposed: All the Moabites heard that the kings had come up to fight against them. They summoned everyone who was girded with a sword belt and took their stand at the borders.
first_reading.reason: 'omnes qui accincti erant balteo desuper' is 'all who were girded with a belt upon them'; 'old enough to wear' adds an age criterion the Latin does not state.

second_reading.note: 'omnes qui accincti erant balteo desuper': all who were girded with a belt; 'old enough to wear' adds the Hebrew's age criterion.

corrections.proposed_english: All the Moabites heard that the kings had come up to fight against them. They summoned everyone who was girded with a sword belt and took their stand at the borders.

corrections.latin: Profecta est igitur, et venit ad virum Dei in montem Carmeli : cumque vidisset eam vir Dei e contra, ait ad Giezi puerum suum : Ecce Sunamitis illa.
corrections.english: She set out and came to the man of God on Mount Carmel. When the man of God saw her from a distance, he said to his servant Gehazi, “Look, there is that Shunammite woman.

first_reading.proposed: She set out and came to the man of God on Mount Carmel. When the man of God saw her opposite him, he said to his servant Gehazi, “Look, there is that Shunammite woman.
first_reading.reason: 'cumque vidisset eam vir Dei e contra' is 'saw her over against him / coming toward him'; 'from a distance' renders the Hebrew ('afar off'), not 'e contra'.

second_reading.note: 'vidisset eam ... e contra' is over against, facing him; 'from a distance' is the Hebrew/KJV 'afar off', which the Vulgate elsewhere marks with 'longe' or 'procul'.

corrections.proposed_english: She set out and came to the man of God on Mount Carmel. When the man of God saw her opposite him, he said to his servant Gehazi, “Look, there is that Shunammite woman.

corrections.latin: Et Eliseus reversus est in Galgala. Erat autem fames in terra, et filii prophetarum habitabant coram eo. Dixitque uni de pueris suis : Pone ollam grandem, et coque pulmentum filiis prophetarum.
corrections.english: Elisha returned to Gilgal. There was a famine in the land, and the sons of the prophets were sitting before him. He said to one of his servants, “Set out the large pot and cook a stew for the sons of the prophets.”

first_reading.proposed: Elisha returned to Gilgal. There was a famine in the land, and the sons of the prophets were dwelling before him. He said to one of his servants, “Set out the large pot and cook a stew for the sons of the prophets.”
first_reading.reason: 'filii prophetarum habitabant coram eo' is 'dwelt before him'; 'were sitting before him' follows the Hebrew verb, not the Latin 'habitabant'.

second_reading.note: 'filii prophetarum habitabant coram eo': habitare is dwell; 'were sitting' follows the Hebrew verb's other sense.

corrections.proposed_english: Elisha returned to Gilgal. There was a famine in the land, and the sons of the prophets were dwelling before him. He said to one of his servants, “Set out the large pot and cook a stew for the sons of the prophets.”

corrections.latin: Et ascendit, et profectus est in Jezrahel : Joram enim ægrotabat ibi, et Ochozias rex Juda descenderat ad visitandum Joram.
corrections.english: He mounted his chariot and went to Jezreel, for Joram was ill there, and Ahaziah king of Judah had gone down to visit him.

first_reading.proposed: He went up and set out for Jezreel, for Joram was ill there, and Ahaziah king of Judah had gone down to visit him.
first_reading.reason: "Et ascendit, et profectus est" is simply 'he went up and set out'; "his chariot" is not in the Latin (it reflects the Hebrew 'rode').

second_reading.note: 'Et ascendit, et profectus est': absolute 'ascendit' can stay 'mounted', but 'his chariot' is not in the Latin; proposed 'went up' wrongly suggests an ascent.

corrections.proposed_english: He mounted and went to Jezreel, for Joram was ill there, and Ahaziah king of Judah had gone down to visit him.

corrections.latin: Si non pro sanguine Naboth, et pro sanguine filiorum ejus, quem vidi heri, ait Dominus, reddam tibi in agro isto, dicit Dominus. Nunc ergo tolle, et projice eum in agrum juxta verbum Domini.
corrections.english: ‘As surely as I saw the blood of Naboth and the blood of his sons yesterday, says the Lord, I will repay you in this field, says the Lord.’ Now take him and throw him into the field, according to the Lord's word.”

first_reading.proposed: ‘Surely for the blood of Naboth and for the blood of his sons, which I saw yesterday, says the Lord, I will repay you in this field, says the Lord.’ Now take him and throw him into the field, according to the Lord's word.”
first_reading.reason: Latin oath is "Si non pro sanguine Naboth... quem vidi heri... reddam tibi": 'surely I will repay you FOR the blood... which I saw'. English follows the Hebrew syntax ('As surely as I saw') and drops "pro".

second_reading.note: "Si non pro sanguine ... quem vidi heri ... reddam tibi": repayment is for the blood, which he saw; current drops "pro" and recasts the oath.

corrections.proposed_english: ‘Surely for the blood of Naboth and for the blood of his sons, which I saw yesterday, says the Lord, I will repay you in this field, says the Lord.’ Now take him and throw him into the field, according to the Lord's word.”

corrections.latin: Factum est autem, cum completum esset holocaustum, præcepit Jehu militibus et ducibus suis : Ingredimini, et percutite eos : nullus evadat. Percusseruntque eos in ore gladii, et projecerunt milites et duces : et ierunt in civitatem templi Baal,
corrections.english: When the burnt offering was completed, Jehu commanded his soldiers and officers, “Go in and strike them down; let none escape.” They struck them with the edge of the sword. The soldiers and officers threw them out and went into the citadel of Baal's temple.

first_reading.proposed: When the burnt offering was completed, Jehu commanded his soldiers and officers, “Go in and strike them down; let none escape.” They struck them with the edge of the sword. The soldiers and officers threw them out and went into the city of Baal's temple.
first_reading.reason: "in civitatem templi Baal" is 'into the city of the temple of Baal'; civitas does not mean 'citadel' (a modern rendering of the Hebrew).

second_reading.note: "in civitatem templi Baal": civitas is city, never citadel.

corrections.proposed_english: When the burnt offering was completed, Jehu commanded his soldiers and officers, “Go in and strike them down; let none escape.” They struck them with the edge of the sword. The soldiers and officers threw them out and went into the city of Baal's temple.

corrections.latin: Percussit autem Dominus regem, et fuit leprosus usque in diem mortis suæ, et habitabat in domo libera seorsum : Joatham vero filius regis gubernabat palatium, et judicabit populum terræ.
corrections.english: The Lord struck the king, and he was a leper until the day of his death. He lived apart in a separate house, while Jotham the king's son governed the palace and was to judge the people of the land.

first_reading.proposed: The Lord struck the king, and he was a leper until the day of his death. He lived apart in a free house, while Jotham the king's son governed the palace and judged the people of the land.
first_reading.reason: "in domo libera seorsum" is 'in a free house apart'; "libera" is not 'separate' (that reflects the Hebrew). "judicabat" (Clementine) is 'judged', not 'was to judge'.

second_reading.note: "in domo libera seorsum": libera is free, not separate; the card reads "judicabit" (future), so "was to judge" stands.

corrections.proposed_english: The Lord struck the king, and he was a leper until the day of his death. He lived apart in a free house, while Jotham the king's son governed the palace and was to judge the people of the land.

corrections.latin: Numquid non audisti quid ab initio fecerim ? ex diebus antiquis plasmavi illud, et nunc adduxi : eruntque in ruinam collium pugnantium civitates munitæ.
corrections.english: Have you not heard what I did from the beginning? From ancient days I shaped it, and now I have brought it about: fortified cities will become ruined heaps for those who fight.

first_reading.proposed: Have you not heard what I did from the beginning? From ancient days I shaped it, and now I have brought it about: fortified cities of fighting men will become ruined heaps.
first_reading.reason: "pugnantium civitates munitæ": pugnantium is genitive, 'fortified cities of fighting men', not ruins 'for those who fight'.

second_reading.note: "pugnantium civitates munitæ": pugnantium is genitive with civitates, not a dative "for those who fight".

corrections.proposed_english: Have you not heard what I did from the beginning? From ancient days I shaped it, and now I have brought it about: fortified cities of fighting men will become ruined heaps.

corrections.latin: Caleb autem frater Sua genuit Mahir, qui fuit pater Esthon.
corrections.english: Chelub, Shuhah's brother, fathered Mehir, who was Eshton's father.

first_reading.proposed: Caleb, Shuhah's brother, fathered Mehir, who was Eshton's father.
first_reading.reason: Latin names him "Caleb autem frater Sua"; English 'Chelub' is the Hebrew name form of modern versions, not the Vulgate's Caleb (rendered 'Caleb' elsewhere in the chapter).

second_reading.note: "Caleb autem frater Sua": the Latin name is Caleb; Chelub is the Hebrew text's different name.

corrections.proposed_english: Caleb, Shuhah's brother, fathered Mehir, who was Eshton's father.

corrections.latin: Fratres quoque eorum Levitæ, qui ordinati sunt in cunctum ministerium tabernaculi domus Domini.
corrections.english: Their brothers the Levites were appointed to all the service of the tabernacle of God's house.

first_reading.proposed: Their brothers the Levites were appointed to all the service of the tabernacle of the Lord's house.
first_reading.reason: Latin has 'tabernaculi domus Domini' (of the house of the Lord); 'God's house' follows the Hebrew wording, not this Latin.

second_reading.note: "tabernaculi domus Domini": Domini is the Lord's, not God's.

corrections.proposed_english: Their brothers the Levites were appointed to all the service of the tabernacle of the Lord's house.

corrections.latin: De filiis quoque Issachar viri eruditi, qui noverant singula tempora ad præcipiendum quid facere deberet Israël, principes ducenti : omnis autem reliqua tribus eorum consilium sequebatur.
corrections.english: Of the sons of Issachar, learned men who understood the times and knew what Israel should do: two hundred leaders. All the rest of their tribe followed their counsel.

first_reading.proposed: Of the sons of Issachar, learned men who understood the times so as to direct what Israel should do: two hundred leaders. All the rest of their tribe followed their counsel.
first_reading.reason: 'ad præcipiendum quid facere deberet Israël' means 'to direct/instruct what Israel should do'; English 'and knew what Israel should do' drops 'præcipiendum' (follows the Hebrew 'to know').

second_reading.note: "ad præcipiendum quid facere deberet Israël": purpose of directing, not "and knew"; præcipiendum was untranslated.

corrections.proposed_english: Of the sons of Issachar, learned men who understood the times so as to direct what Israel should do: two hundred leaders. All the rest of their tribe followed their counsel.

corrections.latin: Contristatusque est David, eo quod divisisset Dominus Ozam : vocavitque locum illum Divisio Ozæ, usque in præsentem diem.
corrections.english: David was grieved because the Lord had broken out against Uzzah. He called that place the Breach of Uzzah, as it is to the present day.

first_reading.proposed: David was grieved because the Lord had divided Uzzah. He called that place the Breach of Uzzah, as it is to the present day.
first_reading.reason: 'eo quod divisisset Dominus Ozam' = because the Lord had divided Oza (cf. 'Divisio Ozæ'); 'broken out against' renders the Hebrew idiom, not the Latin verb.

second_reading.note: "divisisset Dominus Ozam": transitive dividere with Oza as object; "broken out against" is the Hebrew idiom.

corrections.proposed_english: David was grieved because the Lord had divided Uzzah. He called that place the Breach of Uzzah, as it is to the present day.

corrections.latin: Cumque illi ascendissent in Baalpharasim, percussit eos ibi David, et dixit : Divisit Deus inimicos meos per manum meam, sicut dividuntur aquæ : et idcirco vocatum est nomen illius loci Baalpharasim.
corrections.english: They went up to Baal-perazim, and David struck them there. He said, “God has broken through my enemies by my hand, as waters break through.” Therefore that place was named Baal-perazim.

first_reading.proposed: They went up to Baal-perazim, and David struck them there. He said, “God has divided my enemies by my hand, as waters are divided.” Therefore that place was named Baal-perazim.
first_reading.reason: 'Divisit Deus inimicos meos ... sicut dividuntur aquæ' = God has divided my enemies as waters are divided (passive); 'broken through ... break through' follows the Hebrew sense.

second_reading.note: "Divisit Deus inimicos meos ... sicut dividuntur aquæ": passive dividuntur, waters are divided, not waters breaking through.

corrections.proposed_english: They went up to Baal-perazim, and David struck them there. He said, “God has divided my enemies by my hand, as waters are divided.” Therefore that place was named Baal-perazim.

corrections.latin: Fecit quoque sibi domos in civitate David : et ædificavit locum arcæ Dei, tetenditque ei tabernaculum.
corrections.english: David made houses for himself in the city of David. He prepared a place for the ark of God and pitched a tent for it.

first_reading.proposed: David made houses for himself in the city of David. He built a place for the ark of God and pitched a tent for it.
first_reading.reason: 'ædificavit locum arcæ Dei' = he built a place for the ark; 'prepared' follows the Hebrew, not the Latin 'ædificavit'.

second_reading.note: "ædificavit locum arcæ Dei": ædificavit is built; "prepared" follows the Hebrew.

corrections.proposed_english: David made houses for himself in the city of David. He built a place for the ark of God and pitched a tent for it.

corrections.latin: ne ut a principio, quia non eratis præsentes, percussit nos Dominus ; sic et nunc fiat, illicitum quid nobis agentibus.
corrections.english: lest what happened at first happen again: because you were not present, the Lord struck us, for we acted unlawfully.”

first_reading.proposed: lest, as at first the Lord struck us because you were not present, so it happen now also, should we do anything unlawful.”
first_reading.reason: 'sic et nunc fiat, illicitum quid nobis agentibus' is conditional on the present ('so it happen now too, if we do anything unlawful'); English turns it into a past cause, 'for we acted unlawfully'.

second_reading.note: "sic et nunc fiat, illicitum quid nobis agentibus": the ablative absolute belongs to the present danger, not a past cause "for we acted unlawfully".

corrections.proposed_english: lest, as at first the Lord struck us because you were not present, so it happen now also, should we do anything unlawful.”

corrections.latin: Porro quatuor millia janitores, et totidem psaltæ, canentes Domino in organis quæ fecerat ad canendum.
corrections.english: Four thousand were gatekeepers, and as many were musicians, making music to the Lord on the instruments he had made for praise.

first_reading.proposed: Four thousand were gatekeepers, and as many were musicians, making music to the Lord on the instruments he had made for playing.
first_reading.reason: 'in organis quæ fecerat ad canendum' = instruments he had made for singing/playing; 'for praise' reflects the Hebrew ('to praise'), not 'ad canendum'.

second_reading.note: "quæ fecerat ad canendum": canendum is singing/playing, not praise.

corrections.proposed_english: Four thousand were gatekeepers, and as many were musicians, making music to the Lord on the instruments he had made for playing.

corrections.latin: De filiis Asaph : Zachur, et Joseph, et Nathania, et Asarela, filii Asaph : sub manu Asaph prophetantis juxta regem.
corrections.english: Of the sons of Asaph: Zaccur, Joseph, Nethaniah, and Asarelah, the sons of Asaph, under Asaph, who prophesied under the king's direction.

first_reading.proposed: Of the sons of Asaph: Zaccur, Joseph, Nethaniah, and Asarelah, the sons of Asaph, under Asaph, who prophesied beside the king.
first_reading.reason: 'prophetantis juxta regem' = prophesying near/beside the king; 'under the king's direction' renders the Hebrew idiom, not the Latin 'juxta regem'.

second_reading.note: "prophetantis juxta regem": juxta with a person is beside/near; "under the king's direction" is the Hebrew idiom.

corrections.proposed_english: Of the sons of Asaph: Zaccur, Joseph, Nethaniah, and Asarelah, the sons of Asaph, under Asaph, who prophesied beside the king.

corrections.latin: Universi sub manu patris sui ad cantandum in templo Domini distributi erant, in cymbalis, et psalteriis, et citharis, in ministeria domus Domini juxta regem : Asaph videlicet, et Idithun, et Heman.
corrections.english: All were assigned under their father to sing in the Lord's temple with cymbals, harps, and lyres, for the services of the Lord's house, under the king's direction: Asaph, Jeduthun, and Heman.

first_reading.proposed: All were assigned under their father to sing in the Lord's temple with cymbals, harps, and lyres, for the services of the Lord's house, beside the king: Asaph, Jeduthun, and Heman.
first_reading.reason: 'in ministeria domus Domini juxta regem' = near/beside the king; 'under the king's direction' follows the Hebrew idiom rather than the Latin 'juxta regem'.

second_reading.note: "in ministeria domus Domini juxta regem": juxta regem is beside the king, not under his direction.

corrections.proposed_english: All were assigned under their father to sing in the Lord's temple with cymbals, harps, and lyres, for the services of the Lord's house, beside the king: Asaph, Jeduthun, and Heman.

corrections.latin: Venit ergo Salomon ab excelso Gabaon in Jerusalem coram tabernaculo fœderis, et regnavit super Israël.
corrections.english: Solomon came from the high place at Gibeon, from before the tabernacle of the covenant, to Jerusalem, and reigned over Israel.

first_reading.proposed: Solomon came from the high place at Gibeon to Jerusalem, before the tabernacle of the covenant, and reigned over Israel.
first_reading.reason: Latin 'ab excelso Gabaon in Jerusalem coram tabernaculo fœderis' has only 'coram' (before); 'from before the tabernacle' re-attaches the phrase to Gibeon, following the Hebrew/modern versions.

second_reading.note: "in Jerusalem coram tabernaculo fœderis": only coram, placed after Jerusalem; "from before" is the Hebrew, not this Latin.

corrections.proposed_english: Solomon came from the high place at Gibeon to Jerusalem, before the tabernacle of the covenant, and reigned over Israel.

corrections.latin: A die qua eduxi populum meum de terra Ægypti, non elegi civitatem de cunctis tribubus Israël ut ædificaretur in ea domus nomini meo, neque elegi quemquam alium virum ut esset dux in populo Israël :
corrections.english: ‘From the day I brought My people out of Egypt, I chose no city from all the tribes of Israel for a house to be built there for My name, nor did I choose any other man to lead My people Israel.

first_reading.proposed: ‘From the day I brought My people out of Egypt, I chose no city from all the tribes of Israel for a house to be built there for My name, nor did I choose any other man to be leader among the people of Israel.
first_reading.reason: Latin "ut esset dux in populo Israël" has no "meo"; "My people Israel" follows the Hebrew wording, not this Latin.

second_reading.note: "ut esset dux in populo Israël" has no meo, so "My" is added; "to lead" itself is sound and need not change.

corrections.proposed_english: ‘From the day I brought My people out of Egypt, I chose no city from all the tribes of Israel for a house to be built there for My name, nor did I choose any other man to lead the people of Israel.

corrections.latin: Si peccaverit quispiam in proximum suum, et jurare contra eum paratus venerit, seque maledicto constrinxerit coram altari in domo ista :
corrections.english: If someone sins against his neighbor and comes prepared to swear concerning him, binding himself with a curse before Your altar in this house,

first_reading.proposed: If someone sins against his neighbor and comes prepared to swear against him, binding himself with a curse before the altar in this house,
first_reading.reason: "jurare contra eum" is to swear against him, not "concerning him"; "coram altari" has no "tuo" ("Your" added).

second_reading.note: "jurare contra eum" is against him; "coram altari" has no tuo.

corrections.proposed_english: If someone sins against his neighbor and comes prepared to swear against him, binding himself with a curse before the altar in this house,

corrections.latin: Fecitque die octavo collectam, eo quod dedicasset altare septem diebus, et solemnitatem celebrasset diebus septem.
corrections.english: On the eighth day he held an assembly, for they had dedicated the altar for seven days and celebrated the festival for seven days.

first_reading.proposed: On the eighth day he held an assembly, for he had dedicated the altar for seven days and celebrated the festival for seven days.
first_reading.reason: "dedicasset ... celebrasset" are singular, continuing the subject of "fecit" (Solomon); "they had dedicated" follows the Hebrew plural.

second_reading.note: "dedicasset ... celebrasset" are singular, continuing the subject of "Fecitque"; "they" is the Hebrew plural.

corrections.proposed_english: On the eighth day he held an assembly, for he had dedicated the altar for seven days and celebrated the festival for seven days.

corrections.latin: Omnia quoque vasa convivii regis erant aurea, et vasa domus saltus Libani ex auro purissimo. Argentum enim in diebus illis pro nihilo reputabatur.
corrections.english: All the king's drinking vessels were gold, and the vessels of the House of the Forest of Lebanon were purest gold. Silver was considered nothing in those days.

first_reading.proposed: All the vessels of the king's table were gold, and the vessels of the House of the Forest of Lebanon were purest gold. Silver was considered nothing in those days.
first_reading.reason: "vasa convivii regis" are the vessels of the king's banquet/table; "drinking vessels" reflects the Hebrew, not the Latin "convivii".

second_reading.note: "vasa convivii regis": convivium is banquet/table, not drinking.

corrections.proposed_english: All the vessels of the king's table were gold, and the vessels of the House of the Forest of Lebanon were purest gold. Silver was considered nothing in those days.

corrections.latin: Reliqua autem operum Salomonis priorum et novissimorum scripta sunt in verbis Nathan prophetæ, et in libris Ahiæ Silonitis, in visione quoque Addo videntis contra Jeroboam filium Nabat.
corrections.english: The rest of Solomon's deeds, first and last, are written in the words of Nathan the prophet, the books of Ahijah the Shilonite, and the vision of Iddo the seer concerning Jeroboam son of Nebat.

first_reading.proposed: The rest of Solomon's deeds, first and last, are written in the words of Nathan the prophet, the books of Ahijah the Shilonite, and the vision of Iddo the seer against Jeroboam son of Nebat.
first_reading.reason: "contra Jeroboam" means against Jeroboam; "concerning" weakens the Latin preposition.

second_reading.note: "in visione ... contra Jeroboam": contra is against, not concerning.

corrections.proposed_english: The rest of Solomon's deeds, first and last, are written in the words of Nathan the prophet, the books of Ahijah the Shilonite, and the vision of Iddo the seer against Jeroboam son of Nebat.

corrections.latin: Cumque clausisset eas muris, posuit in eis principes, ciborumque horrea, hoc est, olei, et vini.
corrections.english: He enclosed them with walls and placed commanders and stores of food, oil, and wine in them.

first_reading.proposed: He enclosed them with walls and placed commanders and stores of provisions, that is, of oil and wine, in them.
first_reading.reason: "ciborumque horrea, hoc est, olei, et vini": the oil and wine explain the provisions ("hoc est"); the English turns them into a list of three separate things and drops "hoc est".

second_reading.note: "ciborumque horrea, hoc est, olei, et vini": hoc est was dropped; "food" for ciborum is sound and need not become "provisions".

corrections.proposed_english: He enclosed them with walls and placed commanders and stores of food, that is, of oil and wine, in them.

corrections.latin: Et ait rex Israël ad Josaphat : Est vir unus a quo possumus quærere Domini voluntatem : sed ego odi eum, quia non prophetat mihi bonum, sed malum omni tempore : est autem Michæas filius Jemla. Dixitque Josaphat : Ne loquaris, rex, hoc modo.
corrections.english: The king of Israel told Jehoshaphat, “There is one man through whom we can seek the Lord's will, but I hate him, because he never prophesies good for me, but always evil: Micaiah son of Imlah.” Jehoshaphat said, “The king should not speak like that.”

first_reading.proposed: The king of Israel told Jehoshaphat, “There is one man through whom we can seek the Lord's will, but I hate him, because he never prophesies good for me, but always evil: Micaiah son of Imlah.” Jehoshaphat said, “Do not speak like that, O king.”
first_reading.reason: "Ne loquaris, rex, hoc modo" is second-person address with vocative "rex" (Do not speak so, O king); the third-person "The king should not speak" follows the Hebrew form.

second_reading.note: "Ne loquaris, rex, hoc modo": second-person prohibition with vocative rex, not third person.

corrections.proposed_english: The king of Israel told Jehoshaphat, “There is one man through whom we can seek the Lord's will, but I hate him, because he never prophesies good for me, but always evil: Micaiah son of Imlah.” Jehoshaphat said, “Do not speak like that, O king.”

corrections.latin: e contrario agunt, et nituntur ejicere nos de possessione quam tradidisti nobis.
corrections.english: Yet these repay us by trying to drive us from the possession You gave us.

first_reading.proposed: Yet these do the contrary and strive to drive us from the possession You gave us.
first_reading.reason: "e contrario agunt, et nituntur ejicere nos" is "they act to the contrary and strive to cast us out"; "repay us" reflects the Hebrew verb, which the Latin does not have.

second_reading.note: "e contrario agunt, et nituntur ejicere nos": no verb of repaying; "e contrario agunt" was untranslated.

corrections.proposed_english: Yet these do the contrary and strive to drive us from the possession You gave us.

corrections.latin: Athalia enim impiissima, et filii ejus, destruxerunt domum Dei, et de universis quæ sanctificata fuerant in templo Domini, ornaverunt fanum Baalim.
corrections.english: For wicked Athaliah and her sons damaged God's house and adorned the shrine of the Baals with all the things consecrated in the Lord's temple.”

first_reading.proposed: For the most wicked Athaliah and her sons destroyed God's house and adorned the shrine of the Baals with all the things consecrated in the Lord's temple.”
first_reading.reason: "destruxerunt domum Dei" is destroyed/pulled down, softened to "damaged"; the superlative "impiissima" (most wicked) is reduced to "wicked".

second_reading.note: "impiissima" is superlative and "destruxerunt domum Dei" is destroyed, stronger than "damaged".

corrections.proposed_english: For the most wicked Athaliah and her sons destroyed God's house and adorned the shrine of the Baals with all the things consecrated in the Lord's temple.”

corrections.latin: Ezechias autem etiam hæc addidit : Implestis manus vestras Domino : accedite, et offerte victimas et laudes in domo Domini. Obtulit ergo universa multitudo hostias, et laudes, et holocausta, mente devota.
corrections.english: Hezekiah added, “You have filled your hands for the Lord. Come and offer sacrifices and thank offerings in the Lord's house.” The whole multitude offered sacrifices, thank offerings, and burnt offerings with devoted hearts.

first_reading.proposed: Hezekiah added, “You have filled your hands for the Lord. Come and offer sacrifices and praises in the Lord's house.” The whole multitude offered sacrifices, praises, and burnt offerings with devoted hearts.
first_reading.reason: "victimas et laudes ... hostias, et laudes": Latin "laudes" is praises; "thank offerings" (twice) reflects the Hebrew term rather than the Latin word.

second_reading.note: "victimas et laudes ... hostias, et laudes": laudes is praises; "thank offerings" is the Hebrew term.

corrections.proposed_english: Hezekiah added, “You have filled your hands for the Lord. Come and offer sacrifices and praises in the Lord's house.” The whole multitude offered sacrifices, praises, and burnt offerings with devoted hearts.

corrections.latin: post quem Jahiel, et Azarias, et Nahath, et Asaël, et Jerimoth, Jozabad quoque, et Eliel, et Jesmachias, et Mahath, et Banaias, præpositi sub manibus Choneniæ et Semei fratris ejus, ex imperio Ezechiæ regis et Azariæ pontificis domus Dei, ad quos omnia pertinebant.
corrections.english: Under them were Jehiel, Azaziah, Nahath, Asahel, Jerimoth, Jozabad, Eliel, Ismachiah, Mahath, and Benaiah, overseers under Conaniah and his brother Shimei, by order of King Hezekiah and Azariah, chief priest of God's house, who had charge of everything.

first_reading.proposed: Under them were Jehiel, Azariah, Nahath, Asahel, Jerimoth, Jozabad, Eliel, Ismachiah, Mahath, and Benaiah, overseers under Conaniah and his brother Shimei, by order of King Hezekiah and Azariah, chief priest of God's house, who had charge of everything.
first_reading.reason: The Latin's second name is "Azarias" (Azariah); the English "Azaziah" is the Hebrew text's name, not a modern form of the Latin one.

second_reading.note: "Jahiel, et Azarias, et Nahath": the Latin name is Azarias (Azariah); Azaziah is the Hebrew text's name.

corrections.proposed_english: Under them were Jehiel, Azariah, Nahath, Asahel, Jerimoth, Jozabad, Eliel, Ismachiah, Mahath, and Benaiah, overseers under Conaniah and his brother Shimei, by order of King Hezekiah and Azariah, chief priest of God's house, who had charge of everything.

corrections.latin: Porro instauravit altare Domini, et immolavit super illud victimas, et pacifica, et laudem : præcepitque Judæ ut serviret Domino Deo Israël.
corrections.english: He restored the Lord's altar and sacrificed victims, peace offerings, and thank offerings upon it. He commanded Judah to serve the Lord God of Israel.

first_reading.proposed: He restored the Lord's altar and sacrificed victims, peace offerings, and praise upon it. He commanded Judah to serve the Lord God of Israel.
first_reading.reason: "victimas, et pacifica, et laudem": Latin "laudem" is praise (a sacrifice of praise); "thank offerings" reflects the Hebrew term rather than the Latin word.

second_reading.note: "victimas, et pacifica, et laudem": laudem is singular praise, not thank offerings.

corrections.proposed_english: He restored the Lord's altar and sacrificed victims, peace offerings, and praise upon it. He commanded Judah to serve the Lord God of Israel.

corrections.latin: Et non est reveritus faciem Domini, sicut reveritus est Manasses pater ejus, et multo majora deliquit.
corrections.english: He did not humble himself before the Lord as his father Manasseh had done, and committed far greater offenses.

first_reading.proposed: He did not revere the face of the Lord as his father Manasseh had done, and committed far greater offenses.
first_reading.reason: "non est reveritus faciem Domini, sicut reveritus est Manasses" means he did not revere the Lord's face; "humble himself before the Lord" follows the Hebrew verb, not the Latin.

second_reading.note: "non est reveritus faciem Domini": revereri is to revere/stand in awe; "humble himself" is the Hebrew verb (Challoner follows it too).

corrections.proposed_english: He did not revere the face of the Lord as his father Manasseh had done, and committed far greater offenses.

corrections.latin: Et destinaverunt aliqui de populo, et abierunt ad regem : et dedit illis potestatem ut facerent justitiam gentium.
corrections.english: Some of the people were appointed and went to the king, and he gave them authority to practice the customs of the nations.

first_reading.proposed: Some of the people resolved on this and went to the king, and he gave them authority to practice the customs of the nations.
first_reading.reason: "destinaverunt aliqui de populo" is active: some of the people determined/resolved (to do this). The English passive "were appointed" makes them chosen by others.

second_reading.note: "destinaverunt aliqui de populo" is active, they themselves determined; "were appointed" makes others choose them.

corrections.proposed_english: Some of the people resolved on this and went to the king, and he gave them authority to practice the customs of the nations.

corrections.latin: Et dixit Mathathias : Væ mihi ! ut quid natus sum videre contritionem populi mei, et contritionem civitatis sanctæ, et sedere illic, cum datur in manibus inimicorum ?
corrections.english: Mattathias said, “Woe to me! Why was I born to see the crushing of my people and the crushing of the holy city, and to sit here while it is given into the hands of enemies?

first_reading.proposed: Mattathias said, “Woe to me! Why was I born to see the crushing of my people and the crushing of the holy city, and to sit there while it is given into the hands of enemies?
first_reading.reason: "sedere illic" is "to sit there" (in the holy city); English has "here".

second_reading.note: "sedere illic": illic is there (the holy city), not here.

corrections.proposed_english: Mattathias said, “Woe to me! Why was I born to see the crushing of my people and the crushing of the holy city, and to sit there while it is given into the hands of enemies?

corrections.latin: et obtinuerunt legem de manibus gentium, et de manibus regum, et non dederant cornu peccatori. · Translation note. Cornu, horn, is preserved in the image horn of strength. Strength makes the military force of the image readable, without substituting a different action.
corrections.english: They rescued the law from the hands of the nations and from the hands of the kings, and did not give the sinner a horn of strength.

first_reading.proposed: They rescued the law from the hands of the nations and from the hands of the kings, and did not give a horn to the sinner.
first_reading.reason: "non dederant cornu peccatori": the Latin has only "cornu", a horn. "of strength" is an explanatory addition not in the Latin (acknowledged in the note).

second_reading.note: "non dederant cornu peccatori": only cornu; "of strength" is an added gloss.

corrections.proposed_english: They rescued the law from the hands of the nations and from the hands of the kings, and did not give a horn to the sinner.

corrections.latin: Et statuit Judas, et fratres ejus, et universa ecclesia Israël, ut agatur dies dedicationis altaris in temporibus suis ab anno in annum per dies octo a quinta et vigesima die mensis Casleu, cum lætitia et gaudio.
corrections.english: Judas, his brothers, and the whole assembly of Israel decreed that the days of the altar's dedication should be observed in their season, year by year for eight days, from the twenty-fifth day of the month of Casleu, with joy and gladness.

first_reading.proposed: Judas, his brothers, and the whole assembly of Israel decreed that the day of the altar's dedication should be observed in its season, year by year for eight days, from the twenty-fifth day of the month of Casleu, with joy and gladness.
first_reading.reason: "ut agatur dies dedicationis altaris": singular verb, so "the day of the dedication ... should be kept"; English has plural "the days ... in their season" (as the Greek).

second_reading.note: "ut agatur dies dedicationis altaris": singular verb and subject; plural "the days" follows the Greek.

corrections.proposed_english: Judas, his brothers, and the whole assembly of Israel decreed that the day of the altar's dedication should be observed in its season, year by year for eight days, from the twenty-fifth day of the month of Casleu, with joy and gladness.

corrections.latin: Et irridens sprevit eos, et polluit : et locutus est superbe,
corrections.english: He mocked and despised them, treated them with contempt, and spoke arrogantly.

first_reading.proposed: He mocked and despised them, defiled them, and spoke arrogantly.
first_reading.reason: "et polluit" means he defiled/polluted (them); "treated them with contempt" merely repeats "sprevit" and loses the defilement.

second_reading.note: "sprevit eos, et polluit": polluit is defiled, not a second verb of contempt.

corrections.proposed_english: He mocked and despised them, defiled them, and spoke arrogantly.

corrections.latin: exclamaverunt autem et hi qui erant ex parte Judæ etiam ipsi, et commota est terra a voce exercituum : et commissum est prælium a mane usque ad vesperam.
corrections.english: Those on Judas's side also sounded their trumpets, and the earth shook at the sound of the armies. Battle was joined from morning until evening.

first_reading.proposed: Those on Judas's side also cried out, and the earth shook at the sound of the armies. Battle was joined from morning until evening.
first_reading.reason: "exclamaverunt autem et hi ... etiam ipsi": they too cried out. The Latin has no trumpets here; "sounded their trumpets" matches the Greek, not this Latin.

second_reading.note: "exclamaverunt autem et hi ... etiam ipsi": they cried out; trumpets are the Greek reading, absent from this Latin.

corrections.proposed_english: Those on Judas's side also cried out, and the earth shook at the sound of the armies. Battle was joined from morning until evening.

corrections.latin: Ipse vero Timotheus incidit in partes Dosithei et Sosipatris : et multis precibus postulabat ut vivus dimitteretur, eo quod multorum ex Judæis parentes haberet ac fratres, quos morte ejus decipi eveniret.
corrections.english: Timothy himself fell into the hands of Dositheus's and Sosipater's troops. With many entreaties he asked to be released alive, because he held the parents and brothers of many Jews, who would come to harm through his death.

first_reading.proposed: Timothy himself fell into the hands of Dositheus's and Sosipater's troops. With many entreaties he asked to be released alive, because he held the parents and brothers of many Jews, who would be deceived through his death.
first_reading.reason: "quos morte ejus decipi eveniret": decipi means to be deceived or cheated (of their hope), not to "come to harm".

second_reading.note: "quos morte ejus decipi eveniret": decipi is to be deceived or cheated; "come to harm" is not a sense of the verb.

corrections.proposed_english: Timothy himself fell into the hands of Dositheus's and Sosipater's troops. With many entreaties he asked to be released alive, because he held the parents and brothers of many Jews, who would be deceived through his death.

corrections.latin: Hi sunt autem provinciæ filii, qui ascenderunt de captivitate, quam transtulerat Nabuchodonosor rex Babylonis in Babylonem, et reversi sunt in Jerusalem et Judam, unusquisque in civitatem suam.
corrections.english: These are the people of the province who came up from the captivity into which Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon had carried them in Babylon. They returned to Jerusalem and Judah, each to his own city.

first_reading.proposed: These are the people of the province who came up from the captivity that Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon had carried away to Babylon. They returned to Jerusalem and Judah, each to his own city.
first_reading.reason: "quam transtulerat ... in Babylonem": in with the accusative is motion, "had carried away to Babylon"; the English "had carried them in Babylon" makes it a location and reads as a slip.

second_reading.note: "quam transtulerat ... in Babylonem": accusative of motion, to Babylon; "carried them in Babylon" is a slip.

corrections.proposed_english: These are the people of the province who came up from the captivity that Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon had carried away to Babylon. They returned to Jerusalem and Judah, each to his own city.

corrections.latin: et Hasabiam, et cum eo Isaiam de filiis Merari, fratresque ejus, et filios ejus viginti :
corrections.english: and Hashabiah, and with him Jeshaiah from the descendants of Merari, with his kinsmen and their sons, twenty.

first_reading.proposed: and Hashabiah, and with him Jeshaiah from the descendants of Merari, with his kinsmen and his sons, twenty.
first_reading.reason: "fratresque ejus, et filios ejus" is "his brothers and his sons"; English "their sons" follows the Hebrew pronoun, not the Latin singular "ejus".

second_reading.note: "fratresque ejus, et filios ejus": both ejus are singular, his sons, not their sons.

corrections.proposed_english: and Hashabiah, and with him Jeshaiah from the descendants of Merari, with his kinsmen and his sons, twenty.

corrections.latin: Et surrexit Eliasib sacerdos magnus, et fratres ejus sacerdotes, et ædificaverunt portam gregis : ipsi sanctificaverunt eam, et statuerunt valvas ejus, et usque ad turrim centum cubitorum sanctificaverunt eam, usque ad turrim Hananeel.
corrections.english: Eliashib the high priest and his fellow priests rose and built the Sheep Gate. They consecrated it and set up its doors, and consecrated the wall as far as the tower of a hundred cubits, as far as the Tower of Hananel.

first_reading.proposed: Eliashib the high priest and his fellow priests rose and built the Sheep Gate. They consecrated it and set up its doors, and consecrated it as far as the tower of a hundred cubits, as far as the Tower of Hananel.
first_reading.reason: "usque ad turrim centum cubitorum sanctificaverunt eam": "eam" is the same "it" (portam) as before; English supplies "the wall", a noun the Latin does not have.

second_reading.note: "usque ad turrim centum cubitorum sanctificaverunt eam": feminine eam is still portam; "the wall" (murus) is not its antecedent.

corrections.proposed_english: Eliashib the high priest and his fellow priests rose and built the Sheep Gate. They consecrated it and set up its doors, and consecrated it as far as the tower of a hundred cubits, as far as the Tower of Hananel.

corrections.latin: Post eum in monte ædificavit Baruch filius Zachai mensuram secundam, ab angulo usque ad portam domus Eliasib sacerdotis magni.
corrections.english: After him Baruch son of Zabbai built a second section on the hill, from the corner to the entrance of the house of Eliashib the high priest.

first_reading.proposed: After him Baruch son of Zaccai built a second section on the hill, from the corner to the entrance of the house of Eliashib the high priest.
first_reading.reason: Latin "Baruch filius Zachai" is Zaccai; English "Zabbai" is the Hebrew written reading, not the name the Vulgate gives.

second_reading.note: "Baruch filius Zachai": the Latin name is Zaccai; Zabbai is the Hebrew written reading.

corrections.proposed_english: After him Baruch son of Zaccai built a second section on the hill, from the corner to the entrance of the house of Eliashib the high priest.

corrections.latin: Et alii dicebant : Mutuo sumamus pecunias in tributa regis, demusque agros nostros et vineas :
corrections.english: Still others said, “Let us borrow money for the king's taxes and give our fields and vineyards as security.

first_reading.proposed: Still others said, “Let us borrow money for the king's taxes and give up our fields and vineyards.
first_reading.reason: "demusque agros nostros et vineas" is simply "and let us give our fields and vineyards"; "as security" is an interpretive addition with no Latin behind it.

second_reading.note: "demusque agros nostros et vineas": "as security" is added; plain "give" renders demus, so "give up" is not needed either.

corrections.proposed_english: Still others said, “Let us borrow money for the king's taxes and give our fields and vineyards.

corrections.latin: Stetit autem Esdras scriba super gradum ligneum, quem fecerat ad loquendum : et steterunt juxta eum Mathathias, et Semeia, et Ania, et Uria, et Helcia, et Maasia, ad dexteram ejus : et ad sinistram, Phadaia, Misaël, et Melchia, et Hasum, et Hasbadana, Zacharia, et Mosollam.
corrections.english: Ezra the scribe stood on a wooden platform he had made for speaking. Beside him on his right stood Mattithiah, Shema, Anaiah, Uriah, Hilkiah, and Maaseiah; on his left were Pedaiah, Mishael, Malchijah, Hashum, Hashbaddanah, Zechariah, and Meshullam.

first_reading.proposed: Ezra the scribe stood on a wooden platform he had made for speaking. Beside him on his right stood Mattithiah, Shemaiah, Anaiah, Uriah, Hilkiah, and Maaseiah; on his left were Pedaiah, Mishael, Malchijah, Hashum, Hashbaddanah, Zechariah, and Meshullam.
first_reading.reason: Latin "Semeia" is the name Shemaiah (as rendered elsewhere in this book); English "Shema" is the Hebrew form of the name here, not the Vulgate's.

second_reading.note: "Mathathias, et Semeia, et Ania": Semeia is Shemaiah; Shema is the Hebrew text's name here.

corrections.proposed_english: Ezra the scribe stood on a wooden platform he had made for speaking. Beside him on his right stood Mattithiah, Shemaiah, Anaiah, Uriah, Hilkiah, and Maaseiah; on his left were Pedaiah, Mishael, Malchijah, Hashum, Hashbaddanah, Zechariah, and Meshullam.

corrections.latin: Et dixerunt Levitæ Josue, et Cedmihel, Bonni, Hasebnia, Serebia, Odaia, Sebnia, Phathathia : Surgite, benedicite Domino Deo vestro ab æterno usque in æternum : et benedicant nomini gloriæ tuæ excelso in omni benedictione et laude.
corrections.english: The Levites Jeshua, Kadmiel, Bunni, Hashabneiah, Sherebiah, Hodiah, Shebaniah, and Pethahiah said, “Rise and bless the Lord your God from everlasting to everlasting. Let them bless Your glorious name, exalted above every blessing and praise.

first_reading.proposed: The Levites Jeshua, Kadmiel, Bunni, Hashabneiah, Sherebiah, Hodiah, Shebaniah, and Pethahiah said, “Rise and bless the Lord your God from everlasting to everlasting. Let them bless Your glorious and exalted name with every blessing and praise.
first_reading.reason: "benedicant nomini gloriæ tuæ excelso in omni benedictione et laude": "excelso" qualifies the name, and "in omni" is "with all"; "exalted above every blessing" is the Hebrew sense, not the Latin.

second_reading.note: "nomini gloriæ tuæ excelso in omni benedictione et laude": excelso qualifies the name and "in omni" is with every, not above every.

corrections.proposed_english: The Levites Jeshua, Kadmiel, Bunni, Hashabneiah, Sherebiah, Hodiah, Shebaniah, and Pethahiah said, “Rise and bless the Lord your God from everlasting to everlasting. Let them bless Your glorious and exalted name with every blessing and praise.

corrections.latin: Tu ipse, Domine, solus, tu fecisti cælum, et cælum cælorum, et omnem exercitum eorum : terram, et universa quæ in ea sunt : maria, et omnia quæ in eis sunt : et tu vivificas omnia hæc, et exercitus cæli te adorat.
corrections.english: You alone are the Lord. You made heaven, the heaven of heavens, and all their host; the earth and everything upon it; the seas and everything in them. You give life to all these, and the host of heaven worships You.

first_reading.proposed: You Yourself, Lord, You alone made heaven, the heaven of heavens, and all their host; the earth and everything upon it; the seas and everything in them. You give life to all these, and the host of heaven worships You.
first_reading.reason: "Tu ipse, Domine, solus, tu fecisti cælum": "Domine" is vocative and "solus" goes with the making; "You alone are the Lord" is the Hebrew statement, not in the Latin.

second_reading.note: "Tu ipse, Domine, solus, tu fecisti cælum": Domine is vocative, so "You alone are the Lord" asserts what the Latin does not.

corrections.proposed_english: You Yourself, Lord, You alone made heaven, the heaven of heavens, and all their host; the earth and everything upon it; the seas and everything in them. You give life to all these, and the host of heaven worships You.

corrections.latin: debet indui vestibus regiis, et imponi super equum, qui de sella regis est, et accipere regium diadema super caput suum :
corrections.english: ought to be dressed in royal garments, placed upon a horse from the king's own stable, and receive the royal diadem upon his head.

first_reading.proposed: ought to be dressed in royal garments, placed upon a horse the king himself rides, and receive the royal diadem upon his head.
first_reading.reason: "equum, qui de sella regis est" is the horse "of the king's saddle", one the king himself rides; "sella" is saddle or seat, not "stable".

second_reading.note: "equum, qui de sella regis est": sella is saddle/seat, the king's own mount, not his stable.

corrections.proposed_english: ought to be dressed in royal garments, placed upon a horse the king himself rides, and receive the royal diadem upon his head.

corrections.latin: Obtenebrentur stellæ caligine ejus ; expectet lucem, et non videat, nec ortum surgentis auroræ.
corrections.english: Let its stars be darkened with gloom. Let it await light and not see it, nor the rising of the dawn,

first_reading.proposed: Let the stars be darkened with its gloom. Let it await light and not see it, nor the rising of the dawn,
first_reading.reason: "stellæ caligine ejus": ejus qualifies caligine ("with its gloom"), not stellæ; the English moves the possessive to the stars ("its stars ... with gloom").

second_reading.note: "stellæ caligine ejus": ejus follows and qualifies caligine, its gloom, not its stars.

corrections.proposed_english: Let the stars be darkened with its gloom. Let it await light and not see it, nor the rising of the dawn,

corrections.latin: Sed cum lapidibus regionum pactum tuum, et bestiæ terræ pacificæ erunt tibi.
corrections.english: For your covenant shall be with the stones of the fields, and the beasts of the earth shall be at peace with you.

first_reading.proposed: But your covenant shall be with the stones of the lands, and the beasts of the earth shall be at peace with you.
first_reading.reason: "Sed cum lapidibus regionum" = "But ... with the stones of the lands"; "For ... stones of the fields" follows the Hebrew wording, not the Latin Sed / regionum.

second_reading.note: "Sed cum lapidibus regionum": Sed is But, and regionum is of the lands/regions, not fields.

corrections.proposed_english: But your covenant shall be with the stones of the lands, and the beasts of the earth shall be at peace with you.

corrections.latin: Et scies quod pacem habeat tabernaculum tuum ; et visitans speciem tuam, non peccabis.
corrections.english: You shall know that your tent is at peace; when you inspect your property, you shall not go wrong.

first_reading.proposed: You shall know that your tent is at peace; when you visit your beauty, you shall not sin.
first_reading.reason: "visitans speciem tuam, non peccabis" = "visiting your beauty, you shall not sin"; "inspect your property ... not go wrong" reflects the Hebrew (fold/miss nothing), not speciem / peccabis.

second_reading.note: "visitans speciem tuam, non peccabis": species is beauty/appearance, not property; peccabis is plainly sin.

corrections.proposed_english: You shall know that your tent is at peace; when you visit your beauty, you shall not sin.

corrections.latin: [Usquequo loqueris talia, et spiritus multiplex sermones oris tui ?
corrections.english: How long will you speak such things, the words of your mouth a mighty wind?

first_reading.proposed: How long will you speak such things, the words of your mouth a manifold wind?
first_reading.reason: "spiritus multiplex" = a manifold (many-sided) wind/spirit; "mighty wind" follows the Hebrew (and DR "strong wind"), not multiplex.

second_reading.note: "spiritus multiplex": multiplex is manifold, not mighty; "mighty/strong" is the Hebrew word.

corrections.proposed_english: How long will you speak such things, the words of your mouth a manifold wind?

corrections.latin: Si absorbuerit eum de loco suo, negabit eum, et dicet : Non novi te.
corrections.english: If his place swallows him up, it shall deny him and say: I do not know you.

first_reading.proposed: If one swallows him up from his place, it shall deny him and say: I do not know you.
first_reading.reason: "Si absorbuerit eum de loco suo": he is swallowed up out of his place (de loco suo, separation); the English makes the place the swallower and drops "from".

second_reading.note: "Si absorbuerit eum de loco suo": de loco suo is separation, from his place; the place is not the subject of absorbuerit.

corrections.proposed_english: If one swallows him up from his place, it shall deny him and say: I do not know you.

corrections.latin: et scias quia nihil impium fecerim, cum sit nemo qui de manu tua possit eruere ?
corrections.english: though You know that I have done nothing wicked and there is no one who can rescue me from Your hand?

first_reading.proposed: and know that I have done nothing wicked, while there is no one who can rescue me from Your hand?
first_reading.reason: "et scias quia nihil impium fecerim" continues ut quæras ... scruteris ("that You should seek ... and know"); the English turns it into a concession ("though You know"), as in the Hebrew.

second_reading.note: "et scias quia nihil impium fecerim, cum sit nemo": scias is a coordinated subjunctive, not a concession; cum sit is whereas.

corrections.proposed_english: and know that I have done nothing wicked, while there is no one who can rescue me from Your hand?

corrections.latin: Qui immutat cor principum populi terræ, et decipit eos ut frustra incedant per invium :
corrections.english: He changes the heart of the earth's rulers and misleads them to walk in vain through a trackless place.

first_reading.proposed: He changes the heart of the rulers of the people of the earth and misleads them to walk in vain through a trackless place.
first_reading.reason: "principum populi terræ" = the princes of the people of the earth; "populi" is left untranslated ("the earth's rulers").

second_reading.note: "principum populi terræ": populi was left untranslated.

corrections.proposed_english: He changes the heart of the rulers of the people of the earth and misleads them to walk in vain through a trackless place.

corrections.latin: Quis potest facere mundum de immundo conceptum semine ? nonne tu qui solus es ?
corrections.english: Who can make clean one conceived from unclean seed? Is it not You, who alone can do so?

first_reading.proposed: Who can make clean one conceived from unclean seed? Is it not You, who alone are?
first_reading.reason: "nonne tu qui solus es?" = "is it not You who alone are?"; the English adds "can do so", which the Latin lacks, changing es (are) into an ability.

second_reading.note: "nonne tu qui solus es?": es is are; "can do so" is supplied without Latin support.

corrections.proposed_english: Who can make clean one conceived from unclean seed? Is it not You, who alone are?

corrections.latin: Numquid habebunt finem verba ventosa ? aut aliquid tibi molestum est, si loquaris ?
corrections.english: Will windy words have an end? Or does something trouble you, that you must speak?

first_reading.proposed: Will windy words have an end? Or is it any trouble to you to speak?
first_reading.reason: "aut aliquid tibi molestum est, si loquaris?" = "or is anything burdensome to you if you speak?"; the English reverses it (a trouble that makes him speak), as in the Hebrew.

second_reading.note: "aliquid tibi molestum est, si loquaris": speaking is the supposed trouble (si loquaris), not a trouble that compels speech.

corrections.proposed_english: Will windy words have an end? Or is it any trouble to you to speak?

corrections.latin: Nubes latibulum ejus, nec nostra considerat, et circa cardines cæli perambulat.
corrections.english: Clouds are His hiding place; He does not consider our affairs, but walks around the vault of heaven.

first_reading.proposed: Clouds are His hiding place; He does not consider our affairs, but walks around the poles of heaven.
first_reading.reason: "circa cardines cæli" = about the hinges/poles of heaven; "vault of heaven" reflects the Hebrew (circle/vault), not cardines.

second_reading.note: "circa cardines cæli": cardines are hinges/poles, not a vault.

corrections.proposed_english: Clouds are His hiding place; He does not consider our affairs, but walks around the poles of heaven.

corrections.latin: Suscipe ex ore illius legem, et pone sermones ejus in corde tuo.
corrections.english: Receive instruction from His mouth and place His words in your heart.

first_reading.proposed: Receive the law from His mouth and place His words in your heart.
first_reading.reason: "Suscipe ex ore illius legem": legem = law; "instruction" follows the Hebrew torah sense rather than the Latin lex.

second_reading.note: "Suscipe ex ore illius legem": legem is law; "instruction" follows the Hebrew.

corrections.proposed_english: Receive the law from His mouth and place His words in your heart.

corrections.latin: Ponam coram eo judicium, et os meum replebo increpationibus :
corrections.english: I would set my case before Him and fill my mouth with arguments,

first_reading.proposed: I would set my case before Him and fill my mouth with reproofs,
first_reading.reason: "os meum replebo increpationibus": increpatio = rebuke, reproof; "arguments" follows the Hebrew/KJV wording, not increpationibus.

second_reading.note: "os meum replebo increpationibus": increpatio is rebuke or reproof, not argument.

corrections.proposed_english: I would set my case before Him and fill my mouth with reproofs,

corrections.latin: Comparatus sum luto, et assimilatus sum favillæ et cineri.
corrections.english: I have been likened to mud and made like dust and ashes.

first_reading.proposed: I have been likened to mud and made like embers and ashes.
first_reading.reason: "favillæ et cineri" = embers (hot ash) and ashes; "dust and ashes" follows the Hebrew pairing, not favillæ.

second_reading.note: "favillæ et cineri": favilla is embers or hot ash, not dust.

corrections.proposed_english: I have been likened to mud and made like embers and ashes.

corrections.latin: (quia ab infantia mea crevit mecum miseratio, et de utero matris meæ egressa est mecum) ;
corrections.english: though compassion grew with me from my infancy and came out with me from my mother's womb,

first_reading.proposed: for compassion grew with me from my infancy and came out with me from my mother's womb,
first_reading.reason: "quia ab infantia mea crevit mecum miseratio": quia = for/because, giving the reason he did not eat alone; the English makes it concessive ("though").

second_reading.note: "quia ab infantia mea crevit mecum miseratio": quia is causal, for, not concessive though.

corrections.proposed_english: for compassion grew with me from my infancy and came out with me from my mother's womb,

corrections.latin: et fulgurare lumine suo desuper, cardines quoque maris operiet.
corrections.english: and flash with His light from above, He will also cover the depths of the sea.

first_reading.proposed: and flash with His light from above, He will also cover the ends of the sea.
first_reading.reason: "cardines quoque maris operiet": cardines = hinges, poles, extremities ("the ends of the sea"); "depths" reflects the Hebrew (roots/bottom of the sea), not cardines.

second_reading.note: "cardines quoque maris operiet": cardines are hinges, poles or limits, not depths.

corrections.proposed_english: and flash with His light from above, He will also cover the ends of the sea.

corrections.latin: Misit de summo, et accepit me ; et assumpsit me de aquis multis.
corrections.english: He reached down from on high and took me; He drew me out of many waters.

first_reading.proposed: He sent from on high and took me; He drew me out of many waters.
first_reading.reason: "Misit de summo" is "He sent from on high"; "reached down" is not what misit says and follows modern versions of the Hebrew.

second_reading.note: "Misit de summo": misit without an object is sent; "reached down" imports the Hebrew-based reading.

corrections.proposed_english: He sent from on high and took me; He drew me out of many waters.

corrections.latin: magnificans salutes regis ejus, et faciens misericordiam christo suo David, et semini ejus usque in sæculum.]
corrections.english: He magnifies the victories of His king and shows mercy to His anointed, David, and to his descendants forever.

first_reading.proposed: He magnifies the deliverances of His king and shows mercy to His anointed, David, and to his descendants forever.
first_reading.reason: "salutes regis ejus" means the salvations/deliverances of His king; "victories" is not a sense of salus and follows modern versions of the Hebrew.

second_reading.note: "magnificans salutes regis ejus": salus is deliverance/salvation, not victory.

corrections.proposed_english: He magnifies the deliverances of His king and shows mercy to His anointed, David, and to his descendants forever.

corrections.latin: Exsultent et lætentur qui volunt justitiam meam ; et dicant semper : Magnificetur Dominus, qui volunt pacem servi ejus.
corrections.english: Let those who desire my vindication rejoice and be glad, and let those who desire His servant's peace always say, “May the Lord be magnified.”

first_reading.proposed: Let those who desire my righteousness rejoice and be glad, and let those who desire His servant's peace always say, “May the Lord be magnified.”
first_reading.reason: "qui volunt justitiam meam": justitia is righteousness/justice (so rendered elsewhere in these psalms); "vindication" is not a sense of the word and follows modern versions of the Hebrew.

second_reading.note: "qui volunt justitiam meam": justitia is righteousness/justice; vindication is the modern Hebrew-based rendering.

corrections.proposed_english: Let those who desire my righteousness rejoice and be glad, and let those who desire His servant's peace always say, “May the Lord be magnified.”

corrections.latin: Et dicet homo : Si utique est fructus justo, utique est Deus judicans eos in terra.]
corrections.english: A person will say, “Surely there is fruit for the just; surely there is a God who judges them upon the earth.”

first_reading.proposed: A person will say, “If indeed there is fruit for the just, surely there is a God who judges them upon the earth.”
first_reading.reason: "Si utique est fructus justo" is conditional ("If indeed there is fruit for the just"); the English drops "Si" and makes it a flat assertion, as in versions of the Hebrew.

second_reading.note: "Si utique est fructus justo, utique est Deus": Si makes the first clause conditional; current drops it.

corrections.proposed_english: A person will say, “If indeed there is fruit for the just, surely there is a God who judges them upon the earth.”

corrections.latin: Dux itineris fuisti in conspectu ejus ; plantasti radices ejus, et implevit terram.
corrections.english: You were its guide along the way. You planted its roots, and it filled the land.

first_reading.proposed: You were the guide of the journey before it. You planted its roots, and it filled the land.
first_reading.reason: "in conspectu ejus" (in its sight, before it) is not rendered; "Dux itineris fuisti in conspectu ejus" = You were guide of the journey before it.

second_reading.note: 'in conspectu ejus' is left untranslated in the current English; 'Dux itineris ... in conspectu ejus' needs 'before it'.

corrections.proposed_english: You were the guide of the journey before it. You planted its roots, and it filled the land.

corrections.latin: Memor ero Rahab et Babylonis, scientium me ; ecce alienigenæ, et Tyrus, et populus Æthiopum, hi fuerunt illic.
corrections.english: I will remember Rahab and Babylon among those who know Me. Look, foreigners and Tyre and the people of Ethiopia—these were there.

first_reading.proposed: I will remember Rahab and Babylon, who know Me. Look, foreigners and Tyre and the people of Ethiopia—these were there.
first_reading.reason: "scientium me" is a genitive agreeing with Rahab and Babylon ("who know me"); "among those who know Me" follows the Hebrew construction, not the Latin.

second_reading.note: Genitive 'scientium me' agrees with 'Rahab et Babylonis' after 'Memor ero'; 'among those who know Me' is a different construction.

corrections.proposed_english: I will remember Rahab and Babylon, who know Me. Look, foreigners and Tyre and the people of Ethiopia—these were there.

corrections.latin: Et exaltent eum in ecclesia plebis, et in cathedra seniorum laudent eum.
corrections.english: Let them exalt Him in the assembly of the people and praise Him in the council of elders.

first_reading.proposed: Let them exalt Him in the assembly of the people and praise Him in the seat of the elders.
first_reading.reason: "in cathedra seniorum" is "in the seat (chair) of the elders"; "cathedra" does not mean "council".

second_reading.note: 'cathedra seniorum' is the seat or chair of the elders; 'council' is not a sense of cathedra.

corrections.proposed_english: Let them exalt Him in the assembly of the people and praise Him in the seat of the elders.

corrections.latin: qui convertit petram in stagna aquarum, et rupem in fontes aquarum.
corrections.english: who turned the rock into pools of water and the flint into springs of water.

first_reading.proposed: who turned the rock into pools of water and the crag into springs of water.
first_reading.reason: "rupem" is a crag or cliff of rock; "flint" is the Hebrew/KJV wording, not the Latin.

second_reading.note: 'rupem' is a cliff or crag of rock; 'flint' is not a meaning of rupes.

corrections.proposed_english: who turned the rock into pools of water and the crag into springs of water.
