corrections.latin: convertimini ad correptionem meam. En proferam vobis spiritum meum, et ostendam vobis verba mea.
corrections.english: Turn at my correction. Look, I will pour out my spirit for you and make my words known to you.

first_reading.proposed: Turn at my correction. Look, I will bring forth my spirit for you and make my words known to you.
first_reading.reason: Latin "proferam vobis spiritum meum" = I will bring forth/utter my spirit to you (cf. "profert verba sua" in 1:21). "pour out" is the Hebrew/KJV wording, not a sense of proferre.

second_reading.note: 'proferam ... spiritum meum' is bring forth or utter; proferre does not mean 'pour out'.

corrections.proposed_english: Turn at my correction. Look, I will bring forth my spirit for you and make my words known to you.

corrections.latin: vita enim sunt invenientibus ea, et universæ carni sanitas.
corrections.english: for they are life to those who find them and health to all their flesh.

first_reading.proposed: for they are life to those who find them and health to all flesh.
first_reading.reason: Latin "universæ carni sanitas" has no possessive: "health to all flesh". "their flesh" follows the Hebrew/KJV wording, not the Latin.

second_reading.note: 'universæ carni sanitas' has no possessive; 'their' is added and closes off the plain sense 'all flesh'.

corrections.proposed_english: for they are life to those who find them and health to all flesh.

corrections.latin: Sapientes abscondunt scientiam ; os autem stulti confusioni proximum est.
corrections.english: The wise store up knowledge, but the mouth of a fool is close to ruin.

first_reading.proposed: The wise store up knowledge, but the mouth of a fool is close to shame.
first_reading.reason: Latin "confusioni proximum est" = next to confusion/shame (cf. "filius confusionis" rendered "son of shame" at 10:5). "ruin" follows the Hebrew, not the Latin.

second_reading.note: 'confusioni proximum' is next to confusion or shame; confusio does not mean 'ruin'.

corrections.proposed_english: The wise store up knowledge, but the mouth of a fool is close to shame.

corrections.latin: Exsultatio juvenum fortitudo eorum, et dignitas senum canities.
corrections.english: The pride of the young is their strength, and the dignity of the old is gray hair.

first_reading.proposed: The joy of the young is their strength, and the dignity of the old is gray hair.
first_reading.reason: Latin "Exsultatio juvenum" = the exultation/joy of the young; "pride" reflects the Hebrew/modern-version "glory" rather than exsultatio.

second_reading.note: 'Exsultatio juvenum' is exultation or joy; 'pride' gives a different notion, closer to 'gloria'.

corrections.proposed_english: The joy of the young is their strength, and the dignity of the old is gray hair.

corrections.latin: Omnia hæc tractavi in corde meo, ut curiose intelligerem. Sunt justi atque sapientes, et opera eorum in manu Dei ; et tamen nescit homo utrum amore an odio dignus sit.
corrections.english: I considered all these things in my heart, to understand them carefully. The just and the wise and their works are in the hand of God, yet a person does not know whether he is worthy of love or hatred.

first_reading.proposed: I considered all these things in my heart, to understand them carefully. There are just and wise people, and their works are in the hand of God, yet a person does not know whether he is worthy of love or hatred.
first_reading.reason: Latin "Sunt justi atque sapientes, et opera eorum in manu Dei": there are just and wise men, and their works are in God's hand. English puts the just and wise themselves in God's hand, as Hebrew/KJV.

second_reading.note: 'Sunt justi atque sapientes, et opera eorum in manu Dei': an existential clause, then only the works are placed in God's hand.

corrections.proposed_english: I considered all these things in my heart, to understand them carefully. There are just and wise people, and their works are in the hand of God, yet a person does not know whether he is worthy of love or hatred.

corrections.latin: excelsa quoque timebunt, et formidabunt in via. Florebit amygdalus, impinguabitur locusta, et dissipabitur capparis, quoniam ibit homo in domum æternitatis suæ, et circuibunt in platea plangentes.
corrections.english: They will also fear heights and be afraid on the road. The almond tree will blossom, the locust will grow fat, and the caper will scatter, because the human being will go to the house of his eternity and the mourners will go around in the street.

first_reading.proposed: They will also fear heights and be afraid on the road. The almond tree will blossom, the locust will grow fat, and the caper will be scattered, because the human being will go to the house of his eternity and the mourners will go around in the street.
first_reading.reason: Latin "dissipabitur capparis" is passive: the caper will be scattered/destroyed. English "will scatter" makes it active.

second_reading.note: 'dissipabitur capparis' is passive, the caper will be scattered or destroyed; 'will scatter' reads as the caper acting.

corrections.proposed_english: They will also fear heights and be afraid on the road. The almond tree will blossom, the locust will grow fat, and the caper will be scattered, because the human being will go to the house of his eternity and the mourners will go around in the street.

corrections.latin: Quis est iste qui dixit ut fieret, Domino non jubente ?
corrections.english: Mem. Who is this who spoke and it came to pass, without the Lord commanding it?

first_reading.proposed: Mem. Who is this who said that a thing should be done, without the Lord commanding it?
first_reading.reason: 'qui dixit ut fieret' is a command clause (who said that it should be done); 'who spoke and it came to pass' renders the Hebrew, asserting a fulfilment the Latin does not state.

second_reading.note: 'dixit ut fieret', parallel to 'Domino non jubente', is a command that something be done, not a statement that it came to pass.

corrections.proposed_english: Mem. Who is this who said that a thing should be done, without the Lord commanding it?

corrections.latin: Creavit enim ut essent omnia, et sanabiles fecit nationes orbis terrarum : et non est in illis medicamentum exterminii, nec inferorum regnum in terra.
corrections.english: For He created all things to exist, and made the kinds of things throughout the world capable of health. There is no deadly poison in them, nor is the dominion of the realm of the dead upon the earth.

first_reading.proposed: For He created all things to exist, and made the nations of the world capable of health. There is no deadly poison in them, nor is the dominion of the realm of the dead upon the earth.
first_reading.reason: 'nationes orbis terrarum' is 'the nations of the world'; 'the kinds of things throughout the world' follows the Greek (geneseis), not the Latin.

second_reading.note: 'nationes orbis terrarum' is the nations of the world; 'the kinds of things throughout the world' gives the Greek reading, not this Latin.

corrections.proposed_english: For He created all things to exist, and made the nations of the world capable of health. There is no deadly poison in them, nor is the dominion of the realm of the dead upon the earth.

corrections.latin: Qui de luce vigilaverit ad illam non laborabit ; assidentem enim illam foribus suis inveniet.
corrections.english: Whoever rises early to seek her will not labor in vain, for he will find her sitting at his doors.

first_reading.proposed: Whoever rises early to seek her will not labor, for he will find her sitting at his doors.
first_reading.reason: 'non laborabit' is simply 'will not labor' (he is spared toil, finding her at his door); 'in vain' is added and shifts the sense to labor that succeeds.

second_reading.note: 'non laborabit' says he will have no toil; 'in vain' is added and turns it into labor that succeeds.

corrections.proposed_english: Whoever rises early to seek her will not labor, for he will find her sitting at his doors.

corrections.latin: Et cum sit una, omnia potest ; et in se permanens omnia innovat : et per nationes in animas sanctas se transfert ; amicos Dei et prophetas constituit.
corrections.english: Although she is one, she can do all things, and remaining in herself, she renews all things. Through the generations she passes into holy souls and makes friends of God and prophets.

first_reading.proposed: Although she is one, she can do all things, and remaining in herself, she renews all things. Through the nations she passes into holy souls and makes friends of God and prophets.
first_reading.reason: 'per nationes' is 'through the nations'; 'through the generations' renders the Greek (kata geneas), not the Latin shown.

second_reading.note: 'per nationes' is through the nations; 'generations' renders the Greek, not the Latin word shown.

corrections.proposed_english: Although she is one, she can do all things, and remaining in herself, she renews all things. Through the nations she passes into holy souls and makes friends of God and prophets.

corrections.latin: honora patrem tuum, et gemitus matris tuæ ne obliviscaris :
corrections.english: honor your father, and do not forget your mother's birth pangs.

first_reading.proposed: honor your father, and do not forget your mother's groans.
first_reading.reason: Latin 'gemitus matris tuæ' means your mother's groans/groanings; 'birth pangs' renders the Greek (odinas), not the Latin word.

second_reading.note: 'gemitus matris tuæ' is your mother's groans; 'birth pangs' is a different word, from the Greek.

corrections.proposed_english: honor your father, and do not forget your mother's groans.

corrections.latin: Et qui se jungit fornicariis erit nequam : putredo et vermes hæreditabunt illum : et extolletur in exemplum majus, et tolletur de numero anima ejus.]
corrections.english: The one who joins himself to prostitutes will become worthless. Rot and worms will inherit him; he will be held up as a great example, and his soul will be removed from the number of the living.

first_reading.proposed: The one who joins himself to prostitutes will become worthless. Rot and worms will inherit him; he will be held up as a great example, and his soul will be removed from the number.
first_reading.reason: Latin 'tolletur de numero anima ejus' says only 'his soul will be taken from the number'; 'of the living' is an explanatory addition with no Latin behind it.

second_reading.note: 'tolletur de numero anima ejus' leaves 'numero' unqualified; 'of the living' is an addition choosing one of several possible senses.

corrections.proposed_english: The one who joins himself to prostitutes will become worthless. Rot and worms will inherit him; he will be held up as a great example, and his soul will be removed from the number.

corrections.latin: Lingua tertia mulieres viratas ejecit, et privavit illas laboribus suis.
corrections.english: A third tongue has driven out married women and deprived them of their labors.

first_reading.proposed: A third tongue has driven out valiant women and deprived them of their labors.
first_reading.reason: Latin 'mulieres viratas': viratus means manly, valiant (Douay 'valiant women'), not 'married'; the English narrows it to marital status.

second_reading.note: 'mulieres viratas': viratus is manly, of manly spirit, hence valiant; it does not mean 'married'.

corrections.proposed_english: A third tongue has driven out valiant women and deprived them of their labors.

corrections.latin: Sapientiam omnium antiquorum exquiret sapiens, et in prophetis vacabit.
corrections.english: This passage continues Latin 38:39 in the preceding comparison chapter. A wise man will seek out the wisdom of all the ancients and devote his leisure to the prophets.

first_reading.proposed: A wise man will seek out the wisdom of all the ancients and devote his leisure to the prophets.
first_reading.reason: The English opens with an editorial sentence, 'This passage continues Latin 38:39 in the preceding comparison chapter.', which renders nothing in the Latin 'Sapientiam omnium antiquorum exquiret sapiens, et in prophetis vacabit'.

second_reading.note: The editorial opening sentence renders nothing in 'Sapientiam omnium antiquorum exquiret sapiens, et in prophetis vacabit' and must go.

corrections.proposed_english: A wise man will seek out the wisdom of all the ancients and devote his leisure to the prophets.

corrections.latin: a socio et amico de injustitia, et de loco in quo habitas :
corrections.english: before a companion and a friend, of injustice, and before the place where you dwell,

first_reading.proposed: before a companion and a friend, of injustice, and of the place where you dwell,
first_reading.reason: Latin 'de loco in quo habitas' uses 'de', the list's marker for the thing one is ashamed of; 'before the place' renders it as if 'a loco', the Greek sense, making the place a witness.

second_reading.note: 'de loco in quo habitas' uses 'de', the list's marker for the matter of shame, where 'a' marks the witness; 'before the place' reverses that.

corrections.proposed_english: before a companion and a friend, of injustice, and of the place where you dwell,

corrections.latin: de furto, de veritate Dei, et testamento : de discubitu in panibus, et ab obfuscatione dati et accepti : · Translation note. This continues the shame list from 41:21. The prepositional shifts in the Latin are difficult; “before God’s truth and covenant” gives the witnesses before whom shame is felt.
corrections.english: of theft; before God's truth and covenant; of reclining upon the bread, and of obscuring what is given and received;

first_reading.proposed: of theft; of God's truth and covenant; of reclining upon the bread, and of obscuring what is given and received;
first_reading.reason: Latin 'de veritate Dei, et testamento' is 'of/concerning God's truth and the covenant' (the matter of shame); 'before God's truth and covenant' turns them into witnesses, as in the Greek, against the Latin 'de'.

second_reading.note: 'de veritate Dei, et testamento' is of or concerning God's truth and covenant; 'before' would need 'a', as the Greek has.

corrections.proposed_english: of theft; of God's truth and covenant; of reclining upon the bread, and of obscuring what is given and received;

corrections.latin: Tunc exclamaverunt filii Aaron, in tubis productilibus sonuerunt : et auditam fecerunt vocem magnam in memoriam coram Deo.
corrections.english: Then Aaron's sons cried aloud and sounded long trumpets, and made a great sound heard as a remembrance before God.

first_reading.proposed: Then Aaron's sons cried aloud and sounded beaten trumpets, and made a great sound heard as a remembrance before God.
first_reading.reason: "in tubis productilibus": productilis means beaten or hammered out (of metal), not long; the trumpets are of beaten work.

second_reading.note: 'tubis productilibus': productilis is drawn out by hammering, of beaten metal; it does not mean 'long'.

corrections.proposed_english: Then Aaron's sons cried aloud and sounded beaten trumpets, and made a great sound heard as a remembrance before God.

corrections.latin: [Et venite, et arguite me, dicit Dominus. Si fuerint peccata vestra ut coccinum, quasi nix dealbabuntur ; et si fuerint rubra quasi vermiculus, velut lana alba erunt.
corrections.english: Come, then, and argue your case with Me, says the Lord. If your sins are like scarlet, they will be made white as snow; if they are red as crimson, they will be white as wool.

first_reading.proposed: Come, then, and accuse Me, says the Lord. If your sins are like scarlet, they will be made white as snow; if they are red as crimson, they will be white as wool.
first_reading.reason: "arguite me": me is the direct object of arguere (accuse, reprove me). "Argue your case with Me" follows the Hebrew-style "reason together", not the Latin.

second_reading.note: 'arguite me' has 'me' as direct object of arguere, accuse or reprove me; 'argue your case with Me' softens it toward the Hebrew.

corrections.proposed_english: Come, then, and accuse Me, says the Lord. If your sins are like scarlet, they will be made white as snow; if they are red as crimson, they will be white as wool.

corrections.latin: Et judicabit gentes, et arguet populos multos ; et conflabunt gladios suos in vomeres, et lanceas suas in falces. Non levabit gens contra gentem gladium, nec exercebuntur ultra ad prælium.
corrections.english: He will judge the nations and settle disputes for many peoples. They will beat their swords into plowshares and their spears into pruning hooks. Nation will not lift a sword against nation, nor will they train for battle any longer.

first_reading.proposed: He will judge the nations and rebuke many peoples. They will beat their swords into plowshares and their spears into pruning hooks. Nation will not lift a sword against nation, nor will they train for battle any longer.
first_reading.reason: "arguet populos multos" means He will rebuke or reprove many peoples; "settle disputes for many peoples" is a modern rendering of the Hebrew, not of arguet.

second_reading.note: 'arguet populos multos' is He will rebuke or reprove many peoples; 'settle disputes for' is not a sense of arguere with an accusative.

corrections.proposed_english: He will judge the nations and rebuke many peoples. They will beat their swords into plowshares and their spears into pruning hooks. Nation will not lift a sword against nation, nor will they train for battle any longer.

corrections.latin: principem super quinquaginta, et honorabilem vultu et consiliarium, et sapientem de architectis, et prudentem eloquii mystici.
corrections.english: the captain of fifty, the man held in honor, the counselor, the skilled architect, and the one versed in mysterious speech.

first_reading.proposed: the captain of fifty, the man honorable in countenance, the counselor, the skilled architect, and the one versed in mysterious speech.
first_reading.reason: "honorabilem vultu" is honorable in countenance; the English "the man held in honor" leaves vultu untranslated.

second_reading.note: 'honorabilem vultu' is honorable in countenance; the current English drops 'vultu'.

corrections.proposed_english: the captain of fifty, the man honorable in countenance, the counselor, the skilled architect, and the one versed in mysterious speech.

corrections.latin: Agnitio vultus eorum respondit eis ; et peccatum suum quasi Sodoma prædicaverunt, nec absconderunt. Væ animæ eorum, quoniam reddita sunt eis mala !
corrections.english: The expression of their faces testifies against them, and they have proclaimed their sin like Sodom, without hiding it. Woe to their souls, for evils have been repaid to them!

first_reading.proposed: The expression of their faces has answered them, and they have proclaimed their sin like Sodom, without hiding it. Woe to their souls, for evils have been repaid to them!
first_reading.reason: "respondit eis" is has answered them; "testifies against them" is the Hebrew/KJV sense (witness against), not what respondere with the dative says.

second_reading.note: 'respondit eis' is perfect, has answered them; 'testifies against them' gives the Hebrew idiom and a present tense.

corrections.proposed_english: The expression of their faces has answered them, and they have proclaimed their sin like Sodom, without hiding it. Woe to their souls, for evils have been repaid to them!

corrections.latin: sed caput Syriæ Damascus, et caput Damasci Rasin ; et adhuc sexaginta et quinque anni, et desinet Ephraim esse populus ;
corrections.english: For the head of Syria is Damascus, and the head of Damascus is Rezin; within sixty-five years Ephraim will cease to be a people.

first_reading.proposed: But the head of Syria is Damascus, and the head of Damascus is Rezin; within sixty-five years Ephraim will cease to be a people.
first_reading.reason: "sed caput Syriæ": sed is adversative (but), contrasting with "Non stabit" in 7:7; "For" renders the Hebrew conjunction, not the Latin.

second_reading.note: 'sed caput Syriæ' is adversative, 'but'; 'For' turns the contrast into a reason.

corrections.proposed_english: But the head of Syria is Damascus, and the head of Damascus is Rezin; within sixty-five years Ephraim will cease to be a people.

corrections.latin: Quia antequam sciat puer reprobare malum et eligere bonum, derelinquetur terra quam tu detestaris a facie duorum regum suorum.
corrections.english: For before the child knows how to reject evil and choose good, the land that you dread will be abandoned by its two kings.

first_reading.proposed: For before the child knows how to reject evil and choose good, the land that you detest will be abandoned by its two kings.
first_reading.reason: "quam tu detestaris" is which you detest/abhor; "dread" follows modern renderings of the Hebrew, not detestari.

second_reading.note: 'quam tu detestaris' is which you detest or abhor; detestari does not mean 'dread'.

corrections.proposed_english: For before the child knows how to reject evil and choose good, the land that you detest will be abandoned by its two kings.

corrections.latin: Et dixit Dominus ad me : Sume tibi librum grandem, et scribe in eo stylo hominis : Velociter spolia detrahe, cito prædare.
corrections.english: The Lord said to me: Take a large scroll and write in it with an ordinary man's pen: Strip the spoils quickly; plunder swiftly.

first_reading.proposed: The Lord said to me: Take a large scroll and write in it with a man's pen: Strip the spoils quickly; plunder swiftly.
first_reading.reason: "stylo hominis" is simply with a man's pen; "ordinary" is an interpretive addition not in the Latin.

second_reading.note: 'stylo hominis' is simply a man's pen; 'ordinary' is an interpretive word with nothing in the Latin behind it.

corrections.proposed_english: The Lord said to me: Take a large scroll and write in it with a man's pen: Strip the spoils quickly; plunder swiftly.

corrections.latin: quia antequam sciat puer vocare patrem suum et matrem suam, auferetur fortitudo Damasci, et spolia Samariæ, coram rege Assyriorum.
corrections.english: For before the child knows how to call his father and his mother, the wealth of Damascus and the spoils of Samaria will be carried away before the king of the Assyrians.

first_reading.proposed: For before the child knows how to call his father and his mother, the strength of Damascus and the spoils of Samaria will be carried away before the king of the Assyrians.
first_reading.reason: "fortitudo Damasci" is the strength of Damascus (so Douay-Rheims); "wealth" follows modern renderings of the Hebrew.

second_reading.note: 'fortitudo Damasci' is the strength of Damascus; fortitudo does not mean 'wealth'.

corrections.proposed_english: For before the child knows how to call his father and his mother, the strength of Damascus and the spoils of Samaria will be carried away before the king of the Assyrians.

corrections.latin: Et invenit quasi nidum manus mea fortitudinem populorum ; et sicut colliguntur ova quæ derelicta sunt, sic universam terram ego congregavi ; et non fuit qui moveret pennam, et aperiret os, et ganniret.
corrections.english: My hand found the wealth of peoples as though it were a nest. As abandoned eggs are gathered, so I gathered the whole earth; no one moved a wing or opened a mouth or chirped.

first_reading.reason: "fortitudinem populorum" is the strength of the peoples; "wealth" follows modern renderings of the Hebrew, not fortitudo.

second_reading.note: 'fortitudinem populorum' is the strength of the peoples; fortitudo does not mean 'wealth'.

corrections.proposed_english: My hand found the strength of peoples as though it were a nest. As abandoned eggs are gathered, so I gathered the whole earth; no one moved a wing or opened a mouth or chirped.

corrections.latin: et replebit eum spiritus timoris Domini. Non secundum visionem oculorum judicabit, neque secundum auditum aurium arguet ;

corrections.proposed_english: and the spirit of the fear of the Lord will fill him. He will not judge according to what his eyes see or reprove according to what his ears hear,

corrections.proposed_english: but he will judge the poor with righteousness and reprove fairly for the meek of the earth. He will strike the earth with the rod of his mouth and kill the wicked with the breath of his lips.

corrections.latin: Et dicet habitator insulæ hujus in die illa : Ecce hæc erat spes nostra, ad quos confugimus in auxilium, ut liberarent nos a facie regis Assyriorum : et quomodo effugere poterimus nos ?]

corrections.proposed_english: On that day the inhabitant of this island will say: Behold, this was our hope, those to whom we fled for help to deliver us from the king of the Assyrians! How shall we ourselves escape?

corrections.latin: Domine, exaltetur manus tua, et non videant ; videant, et confundantur zelantes populi ; et ignis hostes tuos devoret.
corrections.english: Lord, let Your hand be exalted, though they do not see. Let the jealous peoples see and be put to shame, and let fire devour Your enemies.

corrections.proposed_english: Lord, let Your hand be exalted, and let them not see. Let the jealous peoples see and be put to shame, and let fire devour Your enemies.

corrections.latin: An potius tenebit fortitudinem meam ? faciet pacem mihi, pacem faciet mihi.
corrections.english: Or will it rather take hold of My strength? Let it make peace with Me; let it make peace with Me.

first_reading.proposed: Or will it rather take hold of My strength? It will make peace with Me; it will make peace with Me.
first_reading.reason: "faciet pacem mihi, pacem faciet mihi": faciet is future indicative (it will make peace); the jussive "Let it make peace" follows renderings of the Hebrew, not the Latin mood.

second_reading.note: 'faciet pacem mihi, pacem faciet mihi' is future indicative, like 'tenebit'; 'Let it make peace' is a jussive the Latin lacks.

corrections.proposed_english: Or will it rather take hold of My strength? It will make peace with Me; it will make peace with Me.

corrections.latin: Laxati sunt funiculi tui, et non prævalebunt ; sic erit malus tuus ut dilatare signum non queas. Tunc dividentur spolia prædarum multarum ; claudi diripient rapinam.

first_reading.reason: "dilatare signum": signum is a standard or ensign (rendered signal elsewhere), not a sail; "sail" follows modern renderings of the Hebrew.

second_reading.note: 'dilatare signum': signum is a standard, flag or ensign; it does not mean 'sail'.

corrections.proposed_english: Your ropes have slackened and will not hold firm; your mast will be in such a state that you cannot spread the ensign. Then the spoils of much plunder will be divided; the lame will seize the booty.

corrections.latin: Nolite audire Ezechiam ; hæc enim dicit rex Assyriorum : Facite mecum benedictionem, et egredimini ad me, et comedite unusquisque vineam suam, et unusquisque ficum suam, et bibite unusquisque aquam cisternæ suæ,
corrections.english: Do not listen to Hezekiah, for thus says the king of the Assyrians: Make peace with me and come out to me. Let each of you eat from his own vine and his own fig tree, and drink the water of his own cistern,

first_reading.reason: "Facite mecum benedictionem" is literally make a blessing with me; "Make peace with me" is the modern interpretation of the Hebrew idiom, not what benedictionem says.

second_reading.note: 'Facite mecum benedictionem' is make a blessing with me; 'peace' interprets the Hebrew idiom and is not what benedictio means.

corrections.proposed_english: Do not listen to Hezekiah, for thus says the king of the Assyrians: Make a blessing with me and come out to me. Let each of you eat from his own vine and his own fig tree, and drink the water of his own cistern,

corrections.latin: In manu servorum tuorum exprobrasti Domino, et dixisti : In multitudine quadrigarum mearum ego ascendi altitudinem montium juga Libani ; et succidam excelsa cedrorum ejus, et electas abietes illius, et introibo altitudinem summitatis ejus, saltum Carmeli ejus.
corrections.english: Through your servants you have taunted the Lord and said, “With my many chariots I have climbed the mountain heights, the ridges of Lebanon. I will cut down its lofty cedars and choice cypresses, and enter its highest summit, the forest of its Carmel.

first_reading.reason: 'electas abietes' are 'choice firs'; abies is the fir, not the cypress (cupressus). 'Cypresses' is the modern versions' rendering of the Hebrew tree name.

second_reading.note: 'electas abietes': abies is the fir; cypress would be cupressus.

corrections.proposed_english: Through your servants you have taunted the Lord and said, “With my many chariots I have climbed the mountain heights, the ridges of Lebanon. I will cut down its lofty cedars and choice firs, and enter its highest summit, the forest of its Carmel.

corrections.latin: Cum fureres adversum me, superbia tua ascendit in aures meas. Ponam ergo circulum in naribus tuis, et frenum in labiis tuis, et reducam te in viam per quem venisti.]
corrections.english: When you raged against Me, your pride rose into My ears. Therefore I will put My ring in your nostrils and My bridle on your lips, and lead you back by the road on which you came.

corrections.proposed_english: When you raged against Me, your pride rose into My ears. Therefore I will put a ring in your nostrils and a bridle on your lips, and lead you back by the road on which you came.

corrections.latin: Forte lignum et imputribile elegit ; artifex sapiens quærit quomodo statuat simulacrum, quod non moveatur.
corrections.english: Perhaps he has chosen wood that will not rot; a skilled artisan seeks how to set up an idol that will not move.

second_reading.note: 'Forte lignum et imputribile': forte is the neuter adjective 'strong' joined by 'et' to imputribile, not the adverb 'perhaps'.

corrections.proposed_english: He has chosen strong wood that will not rot; a skilled artisan seeks how to set up an idol that will not move.

corrections.english: Their trunk has scarcely been planted or sown or rooted in the earth when He suddenly blows upon them and they wither; a whirlwind will carry them away like stubble.

first_reading.proposed: Indeed their trunk has been neither planted nor sown nor rooted in the earth; He suddenly blows upon them and they wither; a whirlwind will carry them away like stubble.

second_reading.note: 'Et quidem neque plantatus, neque satus, neque radicatus' is a flat threefold denial; 'scarcely ... when' is a different, temporal construction.

corrections.proposed_english: Indeed their trunk has been neither planted nor sown nor rooted in the earth; He suddenly blows upon them and they wither; a whirlwind will carry them away like stubble.

corrections.proposed_english: He gives strength to the weary and multiplies might and power for those who are not.

corrections.latin: Dabo in solitudinem cedrum, et spinam, et myrtum, et lignum olivæ ; ponam in deserto abietem, ulmum, et buxum simul :

first_reading.proposed: I will put cedar, thorn tree, myrtle, and olive tree in the wilderness; I will place fir, elm, and box tree together in the desert,
first_reading.reason: 'abietem' is the fir, not the cypress (cupressus); 'cypress' is the modern versions' rendering of the Hebrew tree name.

second_reading.note: 'abietem' is the fir; cypress would be cupressus.

corrections.proposed_english: I will put cedar, thorn tree, myrtle, and olive tree in the wilderness; I will place fir, elm, and box tree together in the desert,

corrections.latin: Sublevetur desertum et civitates ejus. In domibus habitabit Cedar : laudate, habitatores petræ ; de vertice montium clamabunt.

corrections.proposed_english: Let the desert and its cities be lifted up. Kedar will dwell in houses. Sing praise, inhabitants of the rock; they will cry out from the mountain tops.

corrections.latin: Ecce omnes participes ejus confundentur, fabri enim sunt ex hominibus ; convenient omnes, stabunt et pavebunt, et confundentur simul.

corrections.proposed_english: Look, all who share in it will be confounded, for its craftsmen are only human beings. They will all gather and stand; they will be afraid and confounded together.

corrections.latin: Laudate, cæli, quoniam misericordiam fecit Dominus ; jubilate, extrema terræ ; resonate, montes, laudationem, saltus et omne lignum ejus, quoniam redemit Dominus Jacob, et Israël gloriabitur.]
corrections.english: Sing praise, heavens, for the Lord has shown mercy. Shout for joy, depths of the earth; mountains, ring out with praise, forest and all its trees, for the Lord has redeemed Jacob, and Israel will glory.

corrections.proposed_english: Sing praise, heavens, for the Lord has shown mercy. Shout for joy, ends of the earth; mountains, ring out with praise, forest and all its trees, for the Lord has redeemed Jacob, and Israel will glory.

second_reading.note: 'super Deum Israël constabiliti sunt' is are established or made firm upon; 'lean upon' is the Hebrew verb's sense.

corrections.proposed_english: For they are called after the holy city and are established upon the God of Israel; the Lord of hosts is His name.

corrections.latin: Quæ audisti, vide omnia ; vos autem, num annuntiastis ? Audita feci tibi nova ex tunc, et conservata sunt quæ nescis.

corrections.proposed_english: Look at all that you have heard. But have you announced it? From that time I have made new things heard by you, things kept in reserve that you do not know.

corrections.latin: Et dixit mihi : Servus meus es tu Israël, quia in te gloriabor.

corrections.english: But I said, “I have labored for nothing; without cause and in vain I have spent my strength. Yet my judgment is with the Lord, and my work with my God.”

corrections.proposed_english: But I said, “I have labored for nothing; without cause and in vain I have spent my strength. Therefore my judgment is with the Lord, and my work with my God.”

corrections.latin: Hæc dicit Dominus : Quis est hic liber repudii matris vestræ, quo dimisi eam ? aut quis est creditor meus, cui vendidi vos ? Ecce in iniquitatibus vestris venditi estis, et in sceleribus vestris dimisi matrem vestram.
corrections.english: Thus says the Lord: Where is your mother's certificate of divorce by which I sent her away? Or who is My creditor to whom I sold you? Look, you were sold because of your iniquities, and because of your crimes I sent your mother away.

corrections.proposed_english: Thus says the Lord: What is this certificate of divorce of your mother by which I sent her away? Or who is My creditor to whom I sold you? Look, you were sold because of your iniquities, and because of your crimes I sent your mother away.

corrections.latin: Consurge, consurge, induere fortitudinem, brachium Domini ! consurge sicut in diebus antiquis, in generationibus sæculorum. Numquid non tu percussisti superbum, vulnerasti draconem ?

corrections.proposed_english: Arise, arise, clothe yourself with strength, arm of the Lord! Arise as in ancient days, in generations long past. Was it not You who struck the proud one and wounded the dragon?

corrections.latin: Consurge , consurge, induere fortitudine tua, Sion ! induere vestimentis gloriæ tuæ, Jerusalem, civitas Sancti, quia non adjiciet ultra ut pertranseat per te incircumcisus et immundus.
corrections.english: Awake, awake, clothe yourself with your strength, Zion! Put on your glorious garments, Jerusalem, city of the Holy One, for the uncircumcised and unclean will no longer pass through you.

first_reading.proposed: Arise, arise, clothe yourself with your strength, Zion! Put on your glorious garments, Jerusalem, city of the Holy One, for the uncircumcised and unclean will no longer pass through you.
first_reading.reason: 'Consurge, consurge' means 'Arise, arise'; 'Awake, awake' is the Hebrew/KJV wording, not the sense of consurgere.

second_reading.note: 'Consurge, consurge' is arise, arise; 'Awake' is the Hebrew verb's sense, not that of consurgere.

corrections.proposed_english: Arise, arise, clothe yourself with your strength, Zion! Put on your glorious garments, Jerusalem, city of the Holy One, for the uncircumcised and unclean will no longer pass through you.

corrections.latin: Iste asperget gentes multas ; super ipsum continebunt reges os suum : quia quibus non est narratum de eo viderunt, et qui non audierunt contemplati sunt.]
corrections.english: He will sprinkle many nations; kings will shut their mouths because of him. For those to whom nothing was told about him have seen, and those who have not heard have understood.

first_reading.proposed: He will sprinkle many nations; kings will shut their mouths because of him. For those to whom nothing was told about him have seen, and those who have not heard have beheld.
first_reading.reason: 'contemplati sunt' means 'have beheld, gazed upon'; 'understood' renders the Hebrew verb, not contemplari.

second_reading.note: 'contemplati sunt', parallel to 'viderunt', is have gazed upon or beheld; 'understood' is the Hebrew verb's sense.

corrections.proposed_english: He will sprinkle many nations; kings will shut their mouths because of him. For those to whom nothing was told about him have seen, and those who have not heard have beheld.

second_reading.note: 'saliunca' is a low shrub and 'abies' the fir; 'in signum' is for or as a sign, not 'through'; but 'nominatus' can properly mean renowned.

corrections.proposed_english: In place of the shrub the fir will rise, and in place of nettles the myrtle will grow. The Lord will be renowned as an everlasting sign that will not be taken away.

corrections.proposed_english: The Lord God, who gathers the dispersed of Israel, says: I will yet gather to him his gathered ones.

corrections.latin: Tunc videbis, et afflues ; mirabitur et dilatabitur cor tuum : quando conversa fuerit ad te multitudo maris ; fortitudo gentium venerit tibi.
corrections.english: Then you will see and overflow; your heart will marvel and expand, when the multitude of the sea turns to you and the wealth of nations comes to you.

first_reading.proposed: Then you will see and overflow; your heart will marvel and expand, when the multitude of the sea turns to you and the strength of nations comes to you.
first_reading.reason: 'fortitudo gentium' is 'the strength of nations'; 'wealth' renders the Hebrew noun, not fortitudo.

second_reading.note: 'fortitudo gentium' is the strength of nations; fortitudo does not mean 'wealth'.

corrections.proposed_english: Then you will see and overflow; your heart will marvel and expand, when the multitude of the sea turns to you and the strength of nations comes to you.

corrections.latin: Et aperientur portæ tuæ jugiter ; die ac nocte non claudentur, ut afferatur ad te fortitudo gentium, et reges earum adducantur.
corrections.english: Your gates will be continually open, not shut by day or night, so that the wealth of nations may be brought to you and their kings led in.

first_reading.proposed: Your gates will be continually open, not shut by day or night, so that the strength of nations may be brought to you and their kings led in.
first_reading.reason: 'fortitudo gentium' is 'the strength of nations'; 'wealth' renders the Hebrew noun, not fortitudo.

second_reading.note: 'fortitudo gentium' is the strength of nations; fortitudo does not mean 'wealth'.

corrections.proposed_english: Your gates will be continually open, not shut by day or night, so that the strength of nations may be brought to you and their kings led in.

corrections.latin: Gloria Libani ad te veniet, abies, et buxus, et pinus simul ad ornandum locum sanctificationis meæ ; et locum pedum meorum glorificabo.
corrections.english: Lebanon's glory will come to you, cypress, box tree, and pine together, to adorn the place of My sanctuary; I will glorify the place of My feet.

first_reading.proposed: Lebanon's glory will come to you, fir, box tree, and pine together, to adorn the place of My sanctuary; I will glorify the place of My feet.
first_reading.reason: 'abies' is the fir, not the cypress (cupressus); 'cypress' is the modern versions' rendering of the Hebrew tree name.

second_reading.note: 'abies' is the fir; cypress would be cupressus.

corrections.proposed_english: Lebanon's glory will come to you, fir, box tree, and pine together, to adorn the place of My sanctuary; I will glorify the place of My feet.

corrections.latin: Vos autem sacerdotes Domini vocabimini : Ministri Dei nostri, dicetur vobis, fortitudinem gentium comedetis, et in gloria earum superbietis.
corrections.english: But you will be called priests of the Lord; they will call you ministers of our God. You will consume the wealth of nations and boast in their glory.

first_reading.proposed: But you will be called priests of the Lord; they will call you ministers of our God. You will consume the strength of nations and boast in their glory.
first_reading.reason: 'fortitudinem gentium' is 'the strength of nations'; 'wealth' renders the Hebrew noun, not fortitudo.

second_reading.note: 'fortitudinem gentium' is strength; fortitudo has no sense 'wealth', which comes from the Hebrew noun.

corrections.proposed_english: But you will be called priests of the Lord; they will call you ministers of our God. You will consume the strength of nations and boast in their glory.

corrections.latin: Quia ego Dominus diligens judicium, et odio habens rapinam in holocausto ; et dabo opus eorum in veritate, et fœdus perpetuum feriam eis.
corrections.english: For I am the Lord who loves judgment and hates robbery in a burnt offering. I will give them their recompense in truth and make an everlasting covenant with them.

first_reading.proposed: For I am the Lord who loves judgment and hates robbery in a burnt offering. I will give their work in truth and make an everlasting covenant with them.
first_reading.reason: 'dabo opus eorum in veritate' is 'I will give their work in truth'; 'their recompense' follows the Hebrew ('their wage'), not the Latin 'opus'.

second_reading.note: 'dabo opus eorum in veritate': opus is 'work', not 'recompense'; the current follows the Hebrew.

corrections.proposed_english: For I am the Lord who loves judgment and hates robbery in a burnt offering. I will give their work in truth and make an everlasting covenant with them.

corrections.latin: sicut exustio ignis tabescerent, aquæ arderent igni : ut notum fieret nomen tuum inimicis tuis ; a facie tua gentes turbarentur.
corrections.english: melt as at fire's burning, and waters would boil in the fire, so that Your name might become known to Your enemies and nations tremble before You!

first_reading.proposed: They would melt as at fire's burning, and waters would boil in the fire, so that Your name might become known to Your enemies and nations tremble before You!
first_reading.reason: English opens with a subjectless fragment, 'melt as at fire's burning', because the preceding Vg 64:1 is missing; 'tabescerent' is 'they would melt'.

second_reading.note: 'tabescerent' is a finite third plural; bare 'melt' leaves a subjectless fragment on the card. Minor: nothing asserted changes.

corrections.proposed_english: They would melt as at fire's burning, and waters would boil in the fire, so that Your name might become known to Your enemies and nations tremble before You!

corrections.latin: Quis audivit umquam tale ? et quis vidit huic simile ? numquid parturiet terra in die una, aut parietur gens simul, quia parturivit et peperit Sion filios suos ?
corrections.english: Who has ever heard such a thing, or seen anything like it? Will the earth bring forth in one day, or a nation be born at once? Yet Zion was in labor and bore her children.

first_reading.proposed: Who has ever heard such a thing, or seen anything like it? Will the earth bring forth in one day, or a nation be born at once? For Zion was in labor and bore her children.
first_reading.reason: 'quia parturivit et peperit Sion' is causal, 'because/for Zion has been in labor and borne'; adversative 'Yet' is not a sense of quia.

second_reading.note: 'quia parturivit et peperit Sion' is causal; adversative 'Yet' is not a sense of quia.

corrections.proposed_english: Who has ever heard such a thing, or seen anything like it? Will the earth bring forth in one day, or a nation be born at once? For Zion was in labor and bore her children.

corrections.latin: Quam vilis facta es nimis, iterans vias tuas ! et ab Ægypto confunderis, sicut confusa es ab Assur.
corrections.english: How utterly contemptible you have become, changing your ways again and again! You will be put to shame by Egypt, just as you were put to shame by Assyria.

first_reading.proposed: How utterly contemptible you have become, repeating your ways again and again! You will be put to shame by Egypt, just as you were put to shame by Assyria.
first_reading.reason: 'iterans vias tuas' is 'repeating, going over your ways again'; 'changing your ways' is the Hebrew/KJV sense ('to change thy way'), not that of iterare.

second_reading.note: 'iterans vias tuas' is going over your ways again; 'changing' is the Hebrew sense, not that of iterare.

corrections.proposed_english: How utterly contemptible you have become, repeating your ways again and again! You will be put to shame by Egypt, just as you were put to shame by Assyria.

corrections.latin: Si reverteris, Israël, ait Dominus, ad me convertere : si abstuleris offendicula tua a facie mea, non commoveberis.
corrections.english: “If you return, Israel, says the Lord, return to Me. If you remove your abominations from My presence, you will not be shaken.

first_reading.proposed: “If you return, Israel, says the Lord, return to Me. If you remove your stumbling blocks from My presence, you will not be shaken.
first_reading.reason: 'offendicula tua' is 'your stumbling blocks' (so rendered at Isaiah 57:14); 'abominations' is the Hebrew/KJV word.

second_reading.note: 'offendicula tua' are stumbling blocks; 'abominations' renders the Hebrew noun.

corrections.proposed_english: “If you return, Israel, says the Lord, return to Me. If you remove your stumbling blocks from My presence, you will not be shaken.

corrections.latin: Dicite gentibus : Ecce auditum est in Jerusalem custodes venire de terra longinqua, et dare super civitates Juda vocem suam :
corrections.english: Tell the nations: Look, it has been heard in Jerusalem that besiegers are coming from a distant land and raising their voices against the cities of Judah.

first_reading.proposed: Tell the nations: Look, it has been heard in Jerusalem that guards are coming from a distant land and raising their voices against the cities of Judah.
first_reading.reason: 'custodes' is 'guards, keepers', the same word as 'custodes agrorum' ('keepers of fields') in 4:17; 'besiegers' follows modern renderings of the Hebrew and loses the Latin link.

second_reading.note: 'custodes venire' is guards or watchers coming; 'besiegers' is not a sense of custos.

corrections.proposed_english: Tell the nations: Look, it has been heard in Jerusalem that guards are coming from a distant land and raising their voices against the cities of Judah.

corrections.latin: Prophetæ fuerunt in ventum locuti, et responsum non fuit in eis : hæc ergo evenient illis.
corrections.english: The prophets have spoken into the wind, and no divine answer was in them. So let these things happen to them!’

first_reading.proposed: The prophets have spoken into the wind, and no divine answer was in them. So these things will happen to them!’
first_reading.reason: "hæc ergo evenient illis" is future indicative, 'these things therefore will befall them'; the English turns the statement into a wish ('let these things happen').

second_reading.note: 'hæc ergo evenient illis' is future indicative, a statement, not a wish.

corrections.proposed_english: The prophets have spoken into the wind, and no divine answer was in them. So these things will happen to them!’

corrections.latin: Me ergo non timebitis, ait Dominus, et a facie mea non dolebitis ? qui posui arenam terminum mari, præceptum sempiternum quod non præteribit : et commovebuntur, et non poterunt ; et intumescent fluctus ejus, et non transibunt illud.
corrections.english: Will you not fear Me, then, says the Lord, and tremble before Me? I set the sand as the sea's boundary, an everlasting decree that it cannot cross. Its waves will churn but be powerless; they will swell but not cross it.

first_reading.proposed: Will you not fear Me, then, says the Lord, and grieve before Me? I set the sand as the sea's boundary, an everlasting decree that it cannot cross. Its waves will churn but be powerless; they will swell but not cross it.
first_reading.reason: "a facie mea non dolebitis" = 'will you not be pained/grieve before Me'; 'tremble' renders the Hebrew verb, not Latin 'dolere'.

second_reading.note: 'non dolebitis' is grieve or be pained; 'tremble' renders the Hebrew verb, not dolere.

corrections.proposed_english: Will you not fear Me, then, says the Lord, and grieve before Me? I set the sand as the sea's boundary, an everlasting decree that it cannot cross. Its waves will churn but be powerless; they will swell but not cross it.

corrections.latin: Sicut decipula plena avibus, sic domus eorum plenæ dolo : ideo magnificati sunt et ditati.
corrections.english: Like a cage full of birds, their houses are full of deceit; therefore they have become great and rich.

first_reading.proposed: Like a trap full of birds, their houses are full of deceit; therefore they have become great and rich.
first_reading.reason: "decipula" is a snare or trap (as in v.26's fowlers); 'cage' is the Hebrew/KJV word, not the Latin.

second_reading.note: 'decipula' is a snare or trap; 'cage' is the Hebrew/KJV word.

corrections.proposed_english: Like a trap full of birds, their houses are full of deceit; therefore they have become great and rich.

corrections.latin: Propterea hæc dicit Dominus : Ecce ego dabo in populum istum ruinas : et ruent in eis patres et filii simul ; vicinus et proximus peribunt.
corrections.english: Therefore thus says the Lord: Look, I will set stumbling blocks before this people; fathers and sons together will stumble over them, and neighbor and friend will perish.

first_reading.proposed: Therefore thus says the Lord: Look, I will bring ruin upon this people; fathers and sons together will fall in it, and neighbor and friend will perish.
first_reading.reason: "dabo in populum istum ruinas: et ruent in eis" = 'I will bring ruins upon this people, and they shall fall in them'; 'stumbling blocks … stumble over' follows the Hebrew.

second_reading.note: 'dabo in populum istum ruinas, et ruent in eis' speaks of ruin and falling; 'stumbling blocks ... stumble over' follows the Hebrew.

corrections.proposed_english: Therefore thus says the Lord: Look, I will bring ruin upon this people; fathers and sons together will fall in it, and neighbor and friend will perish.

corrections.latin: quia fecerunt filii Juda malum in oculis meis, dicit Dominus. Posuerunt offendicula sua in domo in qua invocatum est nomen meum, ut polluerent eam :
corrections.english: For the children of Judah have done evil in My eyes, says the Lord. They have placed their abominations in the house upon which My name has been invoked, to defile it.

first_reading.proposed: For the children of Judah have done evil in My eyes, says the Lord. They have placed their stumbling blocks in the house upon which My name has been invoked, to defile it.
first_reading.reason: "offendicula sua" = 'their stumbling blocks'; 'abominations' is the Hebrew/Douay word, not what this Latin says.

second_reading.note: 'offendicula sua' are stumbling blocks, as at 4:1; 'abominations' is the Hebrew word, though Douay has it here.

corrections.proposed_english: For the children of Judah have done evil in My eyes, says the Lord. They have placed their stumbling blocks in the house upon which My name has been invoked, to defile it.

corrections.latin: Non est his similis pars Jacob : qui enim formavit omnia, ipse est, et Israël virga hæreditatis ejus : Dominus exercituum nomen illi.
corrections.english: Jacob's portion is not like these, for He is the One who formed all things, and Israel is the tribe of His inheritance. The Lord of hosts is His name.

first_reading.proposed: Jacob's portion is not like these, for He is the One who formed all things, and Israel is the rod of His inheritance. The Lord of hosts is His name.
first_reading.reason: "virga hæreditatis ejus" = 'the rod of His inheritance'; 'tribe' is the sense of the Hebrew word, not of Latin 'virga'.

second_reading.note: 'virga hæreditatis ejus' is rod; 'tribe' is a sense of the Hebrew noun, not of virga.

corrections.proposed_english: Jacob's portion is not like these, for He is the One who formed all things, and Israel is the rod of His inheritance. The Lord of hosts is His name.

corrections.latin: Dic regi et dominatrici : Humiliamini, sedete, quoniam descendit de capite vestro corona gloriæ vestræ.
corrections.english: Say to the king and the queen mother: Humble yourselves and sit down, for your glorious crown has fallen from your head.

first_reading.proposed: Say to the king and the queen: Humble yourselves and sit down, for your glorious crown has fallen from your head.
first_reading.reason: "dominatrici" = 'her who rules', the queen/lady ruler; 'queen mother' imports the Hebrew term, the Latin has nothing for 'mother'.

second_reading.note: 'dominatrici' is the ruling lady; nothing in the Latin says 'mother'.

corrections.proposed_english: Say to the king and the queen: Humble yourselves and sit down, for your glorious crown has fallen from your head.

corrections.latin: Perdix fovit quæ non peperit : fecit divitias, et non in judicio : in dimidio dierum suorum derelinquet eas, et in novissimo suo erit insipiens.
corrections.english: A partridge broods over what it did not hatch; a man acquires riches unjustly. In the midst of his days he will leave them, and at his end he will be a fool.”

first_reading.proposed: A partridge broods over what it did not lay; a man acquires riches unjustly. In the midst of his days he will leave them, and at his end he will be a fool.”
first_reading.reason: "fovit quæ non peperit" = 'has brooded what she did not bring forth (lay)'; 'did not hatch' misrenders 'peperit' and blurs the image.

second_reading.note: 'fovit quæ non peperit': peperit is 'bore, laid', not 'hatched'.

corrections.proposed_english: A partridge broods over what it did not lay; a man acquires riches unjustly. In the midst of his days he will leave them, and at his end he will be a fool.”

corrections.latin: Tu autem, Domine, scis omne consilium eorum adversum me in mortem : ne propitieris iniquitati eorum, et peccatum eorum a facie tua non deleatur : fiant corruentes in conspectu tuo ; in tempore furoris tui abutere eis.]
corrections.english: But You, Lord, know all their plans to put me to death. Do not forgive their iniquity or wipe their sin from Your sight. Let them fall before You; deal with them in the time of Your fury.

first_reading.proposed: But You, Lord, know all their plans to put me to death. Do not forgive their iniquity or wipe their sin from Your sight. Let them fall before You; destroy them in the time of Your fury.
first_reading.reason: "abutere eis" = 'use them up, consume/destroy them' (Douay 'destroy them'); the neutral 'deal with them' is the Hebrew wording, weaker than the Latin.

second_reading.note: 'abutere eis' (use hard, ill-treat) is stronger than neutral 'deal with them', but 'destroy' overshoots abuti; 'deal harshly' covers it.

corrections.proposed_english: But You, Lord, know all their plans to put me to death. Do not forgive their iniquity or wipe their sin from Your sight. Let them fall before You; deal harshly with them in the time of Your fury.

corrections.latin: Et sanctificabo super te, interficientem virum et arma ejus : et succident electas cedros tuas, et præcipitabunt in ignem.
corrections.english: I will consecrate destroyers against you, each man with his weapons. They will cut down your choice cedars and throw them into the fire.

first_reading.proposed: I will consecrate against you a slayer and his weapons. They will cut down your choice cedars and throw them into the fire.
first_reading.reason: "interficientem virum et arma ejus" is singular, 'a man who slays, and his weapons'; 'destroyers, each man with his weapons' reproduces the Hebrew construction.

second_reading.note: 'interficientem virum et arma ejus' is singular, a slaying man and his weapons; plural with 'each man' is the Hebrew construction.

corrections.proposed_english: I will consecrate against you a slayer and his weapons. They will cut down your choice cedars and throw them into the fire.

corrections.latin: Væ qui ædificat domum suam in injustitia, et cœnacula sua non in judicio : amicum suum opprimet frustra, et mercedem ejus non reddet ei :
corrections.english: Woe to the one who builds his house in injustice and his upper rooms without justice, who forces his friend to work for nothing and does not pay his wages;

first_reading.proposed: Woe to the one who builds his house in injustice and his upper rooms without justice, who oppresses his friend without cause and does not pay his wages;
first_reading.reason: "amicum suum opprimet frustra" = 'he will oppress his friend without cause'; 'forces his friend to work for nothing' is the Hebrew sense, not the Latin.

second_reading.note: 'opprimet' is oppress, not 'force to work'; but 'for nothing' already renders 'frustra' soundly, so only the verb needs changing.

corrections.proposed_english: Woe to the one who builds his house in injustice and his upper rooms without justice, who oppresses his friend for nothing and does not pay his wages;

corrections.latin: cum diceret : Revertimini unusquisque a via sua mala, et a pessimis cogitationibus vestris, et habitabitis in terra quam dedit Dominus vobis et patribus vestris, a sæculo et usque in sæculum :
corrections.english: when He said: Turn back, each of you, from your evil way and your most wicked thoughts, and dwell in the land that the Lord gave you and your fathers from ages past and forever.

first_reading.proposed: when He said: Turn back, each of you, from your evil way and your most wicked thoughts, and you will dwell in the land that the Lord gave you and your fathers from ages past and forever.
first_reading.reason: "et habitabitis in terra" is future indicative, a promise ('and you shall dwell'); the English makes it a further imperative ('and dwell'), as the Hebrew has.

second_reading.note: 'et habitabitis' is future indicative, a promise, not a second imperative.

corrections.proposed_english: when He said: Turn back, each of you, from your evil way and your most wicked thoughts, and you will dwell in the land that the Lord gave you and your fathers from ages past and forever.

corrections.latin: Propterea habitabunt dracones cum faunis ficariis, et habitabunt in ea struthiones : et non inhabitabitur ultra usque in sempiternum, nec exstruetur usque ad generationem et generationem.
corrections.english: Therefore dragons will dwell there with wild fauns, and ostriches will inhabit her. She will never again be inhabited or rebuilt, from generation to generation.

first_reading.proposed: Therefore dragons will dwell there with fig fauns, and ostriches will inhabit her. She will never again be inhabited or rebuilt, from generation to generation.
first_reading.reason: "faunis ficariis" = 'fig fauns' (ficarius, 'of figs'); 'wild' is not a sense of 'ficariis'.

second_reading.note: 'faunis ficariis' is fig fauns; 'wild' is not a sense of ficarius.

corrections.proposed_english: Therefore dragons will dwell there with fig fauns, and ostriches will inhabit her. She will never again be inhabited or rebuilt, from generation to generation.

corrections.latin: Ecce quasi leo ascendet, de superbia Jordanis ad pulchritudinem robustam, quia subito currere faciam eum ad illam. Et quis erit electus, quem præponam ei ? quis est enim similis mei ? et quis sustinebit me ? et quis est iste pastor, qui resistat vultui meo ?
corrections.english: Behold, like a lion he will come up from the luxuriant growth of the Jordan against the strong and beautiful place, for I will suddenly make him run against it. Who is the chosen one I will appoint over it? For who is like Me? Who can withstand Me? And who is the shepherd who can resist Me to My face?

first_reading.proposed: Behold, like a lion he will come up from the swelling of the Jordan against the strong and beautiful place, for I will suddenly make him run against it. Who is the chosen one I will appoint over it? For who is like Me? Who can withstand Me? And who is the shepherd who can resist Me to My face?
first_reading.reason: "de superbia Jordanis" = 'from the pride/swelling of the Jordan' (so rendered at 12:5); 'luxuriant growth' is a modern reading of the Hebrew, not of Latin 'superbia'.

second_reading.note: 'de superbia Jordanis' is the pride or swelling of the Jordan; 'luxuriant growth' renders a modern reading of the Hebrew.

corrections.proposed_english: Behold, like a lion he will come up from the swelling of the Jordan against the strong and beautiful place, for I will suddenly make him run against it. Who is the chosen one I will appoint over it? For who is like Me? Who can withstand Me? And who is the shepherd who can resist Me to My face?

corrections.latin: Relinque pupillos tuos : ego faciam eos vivere : et viduæ tuæ in me sperabunt.
corrections.english: Leave your orphans; I will keep them alive, and let your widows trust in Me.

first_reading.proposed: Leave your orphans; I will keep them alive, and your widows will trust in Me.
first_reading.reason: "viduæ tuæ in me sperabunt" is future indicative, 'your widows will hope in Me'; the English makes it a jussive ('let your widows trust'), as the Hebrew has.

second_reading.note: 'viduæ tuæ in me sperabunt' is future indicative, not jussive.

corrections.proposed_english: Leave your orphans; I will keep them alive, and your widows will trust in Me.

corrections.latin: Ecce quasi leo ascendet de superbia Jordanis ad pulchritudinem robustam, quia subito currere faciam eum ad illam. Et quis erit electus, quem præponam ei ? quis enim similis mei ? et quis sustinebit me ? et quis est iste pastor, qui resistat vultui meo ?
corrections.english: Behold, like a lion he will come up from the luxuriant growth of the Jordan against the strong and beautiful place, for I will suddenly make him run against it. Who is the chosen one I will appoint over it? For who is like Me? Who can withstand Me? And who is the shepherd who can resist Me to My face?

first_reading.proposed: Behold, like a lion he will come up from the swelling of the Jordan against the strong and beautiful place, for I will suddenly make him run against it. Who is the chosen one I will appoint over it? For who is like Me? Who can withstand Me? And who is the shepherd who can resist Me to My face?
first_reading.reason: "de superbia Jordanis" = 'from the pride/swelling of the Jordan' (so rendered at 12:5); 'luxuriant growth' is a modern reading of the Hebrew, not of Latin 'superbia'.

second_reading.note: 'de superbia Jordanis' is the pride or swelling of the Jordan; 'luxuriant growth' renders a modern reading of the Hebrew.

corrections.proposed_english: Behold, like a lion he will come up from the swelling of the Jordan against the strong and beautiful place, for I will suddenly make him run against it. Who is the chosen one I will appoint over it? For who is like Me? Who can withstand Me? And who is the shepherd who can resist Me to My face?

corrections.latin: Fugite, salvate animas vestras, et eritis quasi myricæ in deserto :
corrections.english: Flee, save your lives, and be like tamarisks in the wilderness.

first_reading.proposed: Flee, save your lives, and you will be like tamarisks in the wilderness.
first_reading.reason: "et eritis quasi myricæ" is future indicative, 'and you shall be like tamarisks'; the English turns the prediction into a command ('and be like').

second_reading.note: 'et eritis quasi myricæ' is future indicative, a prediction, not a command.

corrections.proposed_english: Flee, save your lives, and you will be like tamarisks in the wilderness.

corrections.latin: postquam egressus est Jechonias rex, et domina, et eunuchi, et principes Juda et Jerusalem, et faber et inclusor, de Jerusalem,
corrections.english: after King Jeconiah, the queen mother, the eunuchs, the rulers of Judah and Jerusalem, the craftsmen, and the metalworkers had left Jerusalem,

first_reading.proposed: after King Jeconiah, the queen, the eunuchs, the rulers of Judah and Jerusalem, the craftsmen, and the metalworkers had left Jerusalem,
first_reading.reason: Latin 'domina' is 'the lady/queen'; 'queen mother' adds 'mother', an interpretation drawn from the Hebrew, not in the Latin.

second_reading.note: 'domina' is the lady or queen; 'mother' is not in the Latin.

corrections.proposed_english: after King Jeconiah, the queen, the eunuchs, the rulers of Judah and Jerusalem, the craftsmen, and the metalworkers had left Jerusalem,

corrections.latin: propter malitiam filiorum Israël et filiorum Juda, quam fecerunt ad iracundiam me provocantes, ipsi et reges eorum, principes eorum, et sacerdotes eorum, et prophetæ eorum, viri Juda et habitatores Jerusalem.
corrections.english: because of all the wickedness the children of Israel and the children of Judah have committed to provoke Me to anger: they, their kings, their rulers, their priests, their prophets, the men of Judah, and the inhabitants of Jerusalem.

first_reading.proposed: because of the wickedness the children of Israel and the children of Judah have committed to provoke Me to anger: they, their kings, their rulers, their priests, their prophets, the men of Judah, and the inhabitants of Jerusalem.
first_reading.reason: Latin has 'propter malitiam' with no 'omnem'; the English adds 'all' (as in the Hebrew).

second_reading.note: 'propter malitiam' has no 'omnem' on the card; 'all' is added.

corrections.proposed_english: because of the wickedness the children of Israel and the children of Judah have committed to provoke Me to anger: they, their kings, their rulers, their priests, their prophets, the men of Judah, and the inhabitants of Jerusalem.

corrections.latin: Hæc dicit Dominus : Adhuc audietur in loco isto quem vos dicitis esse desertum, eo quod non sit homo nec jumentum in civitatibus Juda, et foris Jerusalem, quæ desolatæ sunt, absque homine, et absque habitatore, et absque pecore,
corrections.english: Thus says the Lord: Again there will be heard in this place, which you call desolate because neither human nor animal remains, in the cities of Judah and the streets of Jerusalem, deserted, without human being, inhabitant, or livestock,

first_reading.proposed: Thus says the Lord: Again there will be heard in this place, which you call desolate because neither human nor animal remains, in the cities of Judah and outside Jerusalem, deserted, without human being, inhabitant, or livestock,
first_reading.reason: Latin 'foris Jerusalem' means 'outside Jerusalem'; 'the streets of Jerusalem' follows the Hebrew, not the Latin.

second_reading.note: 'foris Jerusalem' is outside Jerusalem; 'streets' is the Hebrew noun.

corrections.proposed_english: Thus says the Lord: Again there will be heard in this place, which you call desolate because neither human nor animal remains, in the cities of Judah and outside Jerusalem, deserted, without human being, inhabitant, or livestock,

corrections.latin: sed in pace morieris : et secundum combustiones patrum tuorum, regum priorum qui fuerunt ante te, sic comburent te : et : Væ domine, plangent te : quia verbum ego locutus sum, dicit Dominus.
corrections.english: but will die in peace. As at the funeral burnings of your fathers, the earlier kings who preceded you, so they will burn for you and lament you, saying, “Alas, my lord!” For I have spoken the word, says the Lord.’”

first_reading.proposed: but will die in peace. As at the funeral burnings of your fathers, the earlier kings who preceded you, so they will burn you and lament you, saying, “Alas, my lord!” For I have spoken the word, says the Lord.’”
first_reading.reason: Latin 'sic comburent te' is 'so they will burn you' (accusative); 'burn for you' follows the Hebrew/KJV sense (burning spices for him), not the Latin.

second_reading.note: 'sic comburent te' has accusative te, 'they will burn you'; 'burn for you' is the Hebrew sense.

corrections.proposed_english: but will die in peace. As at the funeral burnings of your fathers, the earlier kings who preceded you, so they will burn you and lament you, saying, “Alas, my lord!” For I have spoken the word, says the Lord.’”

corrections.latin: Et dixit Jeremias ad Sedeciam : Hæc dicit Dominus exercituum, Deus Israël : Si profectus exieris ad principes regis Babylonis, vivet anima tua, et civitas hæc non succendetur igni : et salvus eris tu, et domus tua.
corrections.english: Jeremiah said to Zedekiah, “Thus says the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel: If you go out and surrender to the officers of the king of Babylon, you will live, and this city will not be burned with fire. You and your household will be safe.

first_reading.proposed: Jeremiah said to Zedekiah, “Thus says the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel: If you set out and go out to the officers of the king of Babylon, you will live, and this city will not be burned with fire. You and your household will be safe.
first_reading.reason: 'Si profectus exieris ad principes' is 'if you set out and go forth to the princes'; 'surrender' is not in the Latin (an interpretive gloss from modern versions), and 'profectus' is left unrendered.

second_reading.note: 'Si profectus exieris ad principes' has no 'surrender'; profectus is 'having set out'.

corrections.proposed_english: Jeremiah said to Zedekiah, “Thus says the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel: If you set out and go out to the officers of the king of Babylon, you will live, and this city will not be burned with fire. You and your household will be safe.

corrections.latin: sed facientes faciemus omne verbum quod egredietur de ore nostro, ut sacrificemus reginæ cæli, et libemus ei libamina, sicut fecimus nos et patres nostri, reges nostri et principes nostri, in urbibus Juda, et in plateis Jerusalem : et saturati sumus panibus, et bene nobis erat, malumque non vidimus.
corrections.english: We will certainly do everything that has gone forth from our mouth: sacrifice to the queen of heaven and pour out drink offerings to her, just as we, our fathers, our kings, and our rulers did in the cities of Judah and the streets of Jerusalem. Then we had bread in plenty, all went well with us, and we saw no calamity.

first_reading.proposed: We will certainly do everything that will go forth from our mouth: sacrifice to the queen of heaven and pour out drink offerings to her, just as we, our fathers, our kings, and our rulers did in the cities of Judah and the streets of Jerusalem. Then we had bread in plenty, all went well with us, and we saw no calamity.
first_reading.reason: 'quod egredietur de ore nostro' is future ('that will go forth'); the English 'has gone forth' makes it a past vow, as in the Hebrew-based versions.

second_reading.note: 'quod egredietur de ore nostro' is future, 'will go forth', not past.

corrections.proposed_english: We will certainly do everything that will go forth from our mouth: sacrifice to the queen of heaven and pour out drink offerings to her, just as we, our fathers, our kings, and our rulers did in the cities of Judah and the streets of Jerusalem. Then we had bread in plenty, all went well with us, and we saw no calamity.

corrections.latin: Et tu, fili hominis, ecce data sunt super te vincula, et ligabunt te in eis, et non egredieris de medio eorum.
corrections.english: As for you, son of man, behold, bonds have been placed upon you, and they will bind you with them, and you will not go out among them.

first_reading.proposed: As for you, son of man, behold, bonds have been placed upon you, and they will bind you with them, and you will not go out from the midst of them.
first_reading.reason: 'non egredieris de medio eorum' is 'you will not go out from the midst of them'; 'go out among them' follows the Hebrew sense, not the Latin 'de medio'.

second_reading.note: 'de medio eorum' is from the midst of them; 'among them' reverses the direction, following the Hebrew.

corrections.proposed_english: As for you, son of man, behold, bonds have been placed upon you, and they will bind you with them, and you will not go out from the midst of them.

corrections.latin: Propterea hæc dicit Dominus Deus : Quia longe feci eos in gentibus, et quia dispersi eos in terris : ero eis in sanctificationem modicam in terris ad quas venerunt.
corrections.english: Therefore thus says the Lord God: Though I have sent them far away among the nations and scattered them through the lands, I will be a little sanctuary for them in the lands to which they have come.

first_reading.proposed: Therefore thus says the Lord God: Because I have sent them far away among the nations and because I have scattered them through the lands, I will be a little sanctuary for them in the lands to which they have come.
first_reading.reason: Latin 'Quia longe feci eos ... et quia dispersi eos' is causal ('because ... and because'); concessive 'Though' follows modern versions of the Hebrew, not the Latin.

second_reading.note: 'Quia longe feci eos ... et quia dispersi eos' is causal; concessive 'Though' is not a sense of quia.

corrections.proposed_english: Therefore thus says the Lord God: Because I have sent them far away among the nations and because I have scattered them through the lands, I will be a little sanctuary for them in the lands to which they have come.

corrections.latin: Et si fuerint tres viri isti in medio ejus, Noë, Daniel, et Job, ipsi justitia sua liberabunt animas suas, ait Dominus exercituum.
corrections.english: Even if these three men, Noah, Daniel, and Job, were within it, they would deliver only their own souls by their righteousness, says the Lord of hosts.

first_reading.proposed: Even if these three men, Noah, Daniel, and Job, were within it, they themselves would deliver their own souls by their righteousness, says the Lord of hosts.
first_reading.reason: "only" is added: the Latin has "ipsi justitia sua liberabunt animas suas" (they themselves shall deliver their souls), with no "soli" here (contrast 14:16, 18); 14:20 renders the same phrase without "only".

second_reading.note: 'ipsi ... liberabunt animas suas' has no 'soli' here, unlike 14:16 and 18; 'only' is added and 'ipsi' left unrendered.

corrections.proposed_english: Even if these three men, Noah, Daniel, and Job, were within it, they themselves would deliver their own souls by their righteousness, says the Lord of hosts.

corrections.latin: Et vestivi te discoloribus, et calceavi te janthino, et cinxi te bysso, et indui te subtilibus :
corrections.english: I clothed you in embroidered garments, put violet-colored shoes on you, girded you with fine linen, and dressed you in delicate fabrics.

first_reading.proposed: I clothed you in many-colored garments, put violet-colored shoes on you, girded you with fine linen, and dressed you in delicate fabrics.
first_reading.reason: "discoloribus" means garments of varied colours (cf. "multicoloribus" 16:13, rendered "multicolored"); "embroidered" is the Hebrew/KJV sense, not what the Latin word says.

second_reading.note: 'discoloribus' is of varied colours; 'embroidered' is the Hebrew/KJV sense, not that of discolor.

corrections.proposed_english: I clothed you in many-colored garments, put violet-colored shoes on you, girded you with fine linen, and dressed you in delicate fabrics.

corrections.latin: Ecce ego extendam manum meam super te, et auferam justificationem tuam, et dabo te in animas odientium te filiarum Palæstinarum, quæ erubescunt in via tua scelerata.
corrections.english: Behold, I will stretch out My hand against you and take away your rightful provision. I will deliver you to the will of those who hate you, the daughters of the Philistines, who blush at your criminal way.

first_reading.proposed: Behold, I will stretch out My hand against you and take away your justification. I will deliver you to the will of those who hate you, the daughters of the Philistines, who blush at your criminal way.
first_reading.reason: "auferam justificationem tuam" = I will take away your justification; "rightful provision" renders the Hebrew sense (allotted portion), not the Latin word.

second_reading.note: 'justificationem tuam' is justification or ordinance; 'rightful provision' renders the Hebrew 'allotted portion'.

corrections.proposed_english: Behold, I will stretch out My hand against you and take away your justification. I will deliver you to the will of those who hate you, the daughters of the Philistines, who blush at your criminal way.

corrections.latin: sed quasi mulier adultera, quæ super virum suum inducit alienos.
corrections.english: but like an adulterous wife who brings in strangers in place of her husband.

first_reading.proposed: but like an adulterous wife who brings in strangers over and above her husband.
first_reading.reason: "super virum suum inducit alienos": super = over, in addition to her husband; "in place of" follows the Hebrew/KJV ("instead of"), a sense "super" does not have.

second_reading.note: 'super virum suum' is over or besides her husband; super does not mean 'in place of'.

corrections.proposed_english: but like an adulterous wife who brings in strangers over and above her husband.

corrections.latin: Et facta est aquila altera grandis, magnis alis, multisque plumis : et ecce vinea ista quasi mittens radices suas ad eam, palmites suos extendit ad illam, ut irrigaret eam de areolis germinis sui.
corrections.english: There was another great eagle, with great wings and many feathers; and behold, this vine, as though sending its roots toward him, stretched out its shoots toward him from the beds in which it grew, so that he might water it.

first_reading.proposed: There was another great eagle, with great wings and many feathers; and behold, this vine, as though sending its roots toward him, stretched out its shoots toward him, so that he might water it from the beds in which it grew.
first_reading.reason: "ut irrigaret eam de areolis germinis sui": "de areolis" belongs to the purpose clause (water it from the beds of its growth); the English attaches it to "extendit" instead.

second_reading.note: Word order joins 'de areolis germinis sui' to 'ut irrigaret eam', not to 'extendit'.

corrections.proposed_english: There was another great eagle, with great wings and many feathers; and behold, this vine, as though sending its roots toward him, stretched out its shoots toward him, so that he might water it from the beds in which it grew.

corrections.latin: Ad dexteram ejus facta est divinatio super Jerusalem, ut ponat arietes, ut aperiat os in cæde, ut elevet vocem in ululatu, ut ponat arietes contra portas, ut comportet aggerem, ut ædificet munitiones.
corrections.english: In his right hand the divination pointed to Jerusalem: to place battering rams, to open the mouth for slaughter, to raise the voice in a war cry, to place battering rams against the gates, to heap up a ramp, and to build siege works.
