first_reading.proposed: On his right the divination pointed to Jerusalem: to place battering rams, to open the mouth for slaughter, to raise the voice in a war cry, to place battering rams against the gates, to heap up a ramp, and to build siege works.
first_reading.reason: "Ad dexteram ejus" = at/on his right (the right-hand road); "In his right hand" is the Hebrew sense (lot held in the hand), not what the Latin says.

second_reading.note: 'Ad dexteram ejus' is at or on his right; 'in his right hand' would be 'in dextera' and follows the Hebrew.

corrections.proposed_english: On his right the divination pointed to Jerusalem: to place battering rams, to open the mouth for slaughter, to raise the voice in a war cry, to place battering rams against the gates, to heap up a ramp, and to build siege works.

corrections.latin: Et descendent de sedibus suis omnes principes maris, et auferent exuvias suas, et vestimenta sua varia abjicient, et induentur stupore : in terra sedebunt, et attoniti super repentino casu tuo admirabuntur :
corrections.english: All the princes of the sea will descend from their thrones, remove their robes, and cast off their embroidered garments; they will clothe themselves in astonishment. They will sit on the ground, stunned and amazed at your sudden fall.

first_reading.proposed: All the princes of the sea will descend from their thrones, remove their robes, and cast off their many-colored garments; they will clothe themselves in astonishment. They will sit on the ground, stunned and amazed at your sudden fall.
first_reading.reason: "vestimenta sua varia" = their variegated, many-coloured garments (cf. "veste varia" 23:12, rendered "varied garments"); "embroidered" is the Hebrew/KJV sense, not the Latin word.

second_reading.note: 'vestimenta sua varia' is variegated, many-coloured garments; varius does not mean embroidered.

corrections.proposed_english: All the princes of the sea will descend from their thrones, remove their robes, and cast off their many-colored garments; they will clothe themselves in astonishment. They will sit on the ground, stunned and amazed at your sudden fall.

corrections.latin: et detraxero te cum his qui descendunt in lacum ad populum sempiternum ; et collocavero te in terra novissima sicut solitudines veteres, cum his qui deducuntur in lacum, ut non habiteris ; porro cum dedero gloriam in terra viventium :
corrections.english: when I bring you down with those descending into the pit, to the people of ages past, and settle you in the lowest land, like ancient wastelands, with those brought down to the pit, so that you may not be inhabited—yet when I set glory in the land of the living—

first_reading.proposed: when I bring you down with those descending into the pit, to the everlasting people, and settle you in the lowest land, like ancient wastelands, with those brought down to the pit, so that you may not be inhabited—yet when I set glory in the land of the living—
first_reading.reason: "ad populum sempiternum" = to the everlasting people; "people of ages past" follows the Hebrew/KJV ("people of old time"), not "sempiternum".

second_reading.note: 'ad populum sempiternum' is the everlasting people; sempiternus cannot mean 'of ages past'.

corrections.proposed_english: when I bring you down with those descending into the pit, to the everlasting people, and settle you in the lowest land, like ancient wastelands, with those brought down to the pit, so that you may not be inhabited—yet when I set glory in the land of the living—

corrections.latin: Byssus varia de Ægypto texta est tibi in velum ut poneretur in malo : hyacinthus et purpura de insulis Elisa facta sunt operimentum tuum.
corrections.english: Embroidered fine linen from Egypt was woven for your sail, to be placed on the mast; blue and purple from the islands of Elishah formed your covering.

first_reading.proposed: Many-colored fine linen from Egypt was woven for your sail, to be placed on the mast; blue and purple from the islands of Elishah formed your covering.
first_reading.reason: "Byssus varia" = variegated, many-coloured fine linen; "Embroidered" is the Hebrew/KJV sense ("broidered work"), not what "varia" means.

second_reading.note: 'Byssus varia' is variegated fine linen; 'embroidered' is the Hebrew/KJV sense.

corrections.proposed_english: Many-colored fine linen from Egypt was woven for your sail, to be placed on the mast; blue and purple from the islands of Elishah formed your covering.

corrections.latin: Manus autem Domini facta fuerat ad me vespere, antequam veniret qui fugerat : aperuitque os meum donec veniret ad me mane : et aperto ore meo, non silui amplius.
corrections.english: The Lord's hand had come upon me in the evening before the escaped man arrived, and He opened my mouth before he came to me in the morning. My mouth was opened, and I was silent no longer.

first_reading.proposed: The Lord's hand had come upon me in the evening before the escaped man arrived, and He opened my mouth until he came to me in the morning. My mouth was opened, and I was silent no longer.
first_reading.reason: "aperuitque os meum donec veniret ad me mane": "donec" means until, not before ("antequam" is used earlier in the verse).

second_reading.note: 'donec veniret ad me mane' is 'until he came'; 'before' is antequam, used earlier in the verse.

corrections.proposed_english: The Lord's hand had come upon me in the evening before the escaped man arrived, and He opened my mouth until he came to me in the morning. My mouth was opened, and I was silent no longer.

corrections.latin: Et insurrexistis super me ore vestro, et derogastis adversum me verba vestra : ego audivi.
corrections.english: You rose against Me with your mouth and multiplied your disparaging words against Me. I heard.

first_reading.proposed: You rose against Me with your mouth and spoke your disparaging words against Me. I heard.
first_reading.reason: "derogastis adversum me verba vestra" = you spoke your words in detraction against me; "multiplied" comes from the Hebrew/KJV ("multiplied your words"), not from the Latin.

second_reading.note: 'derogastis adversum me verba vestra' is detraction only; nothing in the Latin says 'multiplied'.

corrections.proposed_english: You rose against Me with your mouth and spoke your disparaging words against Me. I heard.

corrections.latin: Et ascendes super populum meum Israël quasi nubes, ut operias terram. In novissimis diebus eris, et adducam te super terram meam : ut sciant gentes me cum sanctificatus fuero in te in oculis eorum, o Gog !]
corrections.english: You will come up against My people Israel like a cloud to cover the land. It will be in the last days, and I will bring you against My land, so that the nations may know Me when I manifest My holiness in you before their eyes, O Gog.

first_reading.proposed: You will come up against My people Israel like a cloud to cover the land. You will be in the last days, and I will bring you against My land, so that the nations may know Me when I manifest My holiness in you before their eyes, O Gog.
first_reading.reason: 'In novissimis diebus eris' is second person, 'you will be in the last days'; the English makes it impersonal ('It will be').

second_reading.note: 'eris' is second person singular, 'you will be', not impersonal 'it will be'.

corrections.proposed_english: You will come up against My people Israel like a cloud to cover the land. You will be in the last days, and I will bring you against My land, so that the nations may know Me when I manifest My holiness in you before their eyes, O Gog.

corrections.latin: [Hæc dicit Dominus Deus : Tu ergo ille es, de quo locutus sum in diebus antiquis in manu servorum meorum prophetarum Israël, qui prophetaverunt in diebus illorum temporum, ut adducerem te super eos.
corrections.english: Thus says the Lord God: Are you, then, the one of whom I spoke in ancient days through My servants the prophets of Israel, who prophesied in the days of those times that I would bring you against them?

first_reading.proposed: Thus says the Lord God: You, then, are the one of whom I spoke in ancient days through My servants the prophets of Israel, who prophesied in the days of those times that I would bring you against them.
first_reading.reason: 'Tu ergo ille es, de quo locutus sum' is a statement in the Clementine; the English turns it into a question, as in the Hebrew.

second_reading.note: 'Tu ergo ille es, de quo locutus sum' stands as a statement in the Clementine; the question follows the Hebrew.

corrections.proposed_english: Thus says the Lord God: You, then, are the one of whom I spoke in ancient days through My servants the prophets of Israel, who prophesied in the days of those times that I would bring you against them.

corrections.latin: Et mensus est vestibulum portæ octo cubitorum, et frontem ejus duobus cubitis : vestibulum autem portæ erat intrinsecus.
corrections.english: He measured the gate's vestibule: eight cubits, and its pier: two cubits. The gate's vestibule was on the inside.

first_reading.proposed: He measured the gate's vestibule: eight cubits, and its front: two cubits. The gate's vestibule was on the inside.
first_reading.reason: 'frontem ejus' means its front; 'pier' renders the Hebrew term (jamb/pilaster), not 'frons'. The same 'pier' for 'frons/frontes' recurs throughout chapter 40 (e.g. units 62, 66, 68, 73, 76, 78, 81-89, 100).

second_reading.note: 'frontem ejus' is its front; frons does not mean pier, which renders the Hebrew term.

corrections.proposed_english: He measured the gate's vestibule: eight cubits, and its front: two cubits. The gate's vestibule was on the inside.

corrections.latin: Et introduxit me in atrium interius ad portam australem : et mensus est portam juxta mensuras superiores.
corrections.english: He brought me into the inner court through the south gate and measured the gate according to the previous measurements.

first_reading.proposed: He brought me into the inner court at the south gate and measured the gate according to the previous measurements.
first_reading.reason: 'ad portam australem' is 'to/at the south gate'; 'through' follows the Hebrew preposition, not the Latin 'ad'.

second_reading.note: 'ad portam australem' is to or at the south gate; ad is not 'through'.

corrections.proposed_english: He brought me into the inner court at the south gate and measured the gate according to the previous measurements.

corrections.latin: Et introduxit me in templum, et mensus est frontes : sex cubitos latitudinis hinc, et sex cubitos latitudinis inde, latitudinem tabernaculi.
corrections.english: He brought me into the temple and measured the piers: six cubits wide on this side and six cubits wide on that, the width of the tabernacle.

first_reading.proposed: He brought me into the temple and measured the fronts: six cubits wide on this side and six cubits wide on that, the width of the tabernacle.
first_reading.reason: 'frontes' means fronts; 'piers' renders the Hebrew term (jambs/pilasters), not the Latin. Same in unit 3 ('in fronte portæ'), continuing the usage of chapter 40.

second_reading.note: 'mensus est frontes' is fronts; 'piers' renders the Hebrew term.

corrections.proposed_english: He brought me into the temple and measured the fronts: six cubits wide on this side and six cubits wide on that, the width of the tabernacle.

corrections.latin: Faciem hominis juxta palmam ex hac parte, et faciem leonis juxta palmam ex alia parte : expressam per omnem domum in circuitu.
corrections.english: a human face toward the palm tree on this side and a lion's face toward the palm tree on the other side, depicted throughout the house all around.

first_reading.proposed: a human face beside the palm tree on this side and a lion's face beside the palm tree on the other side, depicted throughout the house all around.
first_reading.reason: 'juxta palmam' is 'beside/next to the palm tree', not 'toward' it (twice).

second_reading.note: 'juxta palmam' (twice) is beside the palm, not toward it.

corrections.proposed_english: a human face beside the palm tree on this side and a lion's face beside the palm tree on the other side, depicted throughout the house all around.

corrections.latin: Et primitiva omnium primogenitorum, et omnia libamenta ex omnibus quæ offeruntur, sacerdotum erunt : et primitiva ciborum vestrorum dabitis sacerdoti, ut reponat benedictionem domui tuæ.
corrections.english: The first of all firstfruits and all libations from everything offered will belong to the priests. You will give the first of your food to the priest, so that he may lay a blessing upon your house.

first_reading.proposed: The firstfruits of all the firstborn and all libations from everything offered will belong to the priests. You will give the first of your food to the priest, so that he may lay a blessing upon your house.
first_reading.reason: 'primitiva omnium primogenitorum' is 'the firstfruits of all the firstborn'; 'the first of all firstfruits' follows the Hebrew, not the Latin 'primogenitorum'.

second_reading.note: 'primitiva omnium primogenitorum' is of all the firstborn; 'of all firstfruits' follows the Hebrew.

corrections.proposed_english: The firstfruits of all the firstborn and all libations from everything offered will belong to the priests. You will give the first of your food to the priest, so that he may lay a blessing upon your house.

corrections.latin: Et erit ex omni parte sanctificatum quingentos per quingentos, quadrifariam per circuitum, et quinquaginta cubitis in suburbana ejus per gyrum.
corrections.english: Within it there will be a holy area of five hundred by five hundred, square on every side, with fifty cubits of open ground around it.

first_reading.proposed: There will be a holy area of five hundred by five hundred on every side, square all around, with fifty cubits of open ground around it.
first_reading.reason: 'Et erit ex omni parte sanctificatum … quadrifariam per circuitum': no 'Within it' in the Latin (that is the Hebrew 'of this'); 'ex omni parte' and 'per circuitum' are both to be kept.

second_reading.note: 'Et erit ex omni parte sanctificatum' has no 'Within it'; 'ex omni parte' is 'on every side', beside 'quadrifariam per circuitum'.

corrections.proposed_english: There will be a holy area of five hundred by five hundred on every side, square all around, with fifty cubits of open ground around it.

corrections.latin: De terra erit ei possessio in Israël, et non depopulabuntur ultra principes populum meum : sed terram dabunt domui Israël secundum tribus eorum.
corrections.english: This land will be his possession in Israel, and My princes will no longer plunder My people, but will give the land to the house of Israel according to their tribes.

first_reading.proposed: This land will be his possession in Israel, and the princes will no longer plunder My people, but will give the land to the house of Israel according to their tribes.
first_reading.reason: Latin has 'principes' without a possessive; 'My princes' follows the Hebrew.

second_reading.note: 'principes' has no possessive; 'My' is added from the Hebrew.

corrections.proposed_english: This land will be his possession in Israel, and the princes will no longer plunder My people, but will give the land to the house of Israel according to their tribes.

corrections.latin: Et in nundinis, et in solemnitatibus, erit sacrificium ephi per vitulum, et ephi per arietem : agnis autem erit sacrificium sicut invenerit manus ejus, et olei hin per singula ephi.
corrections.english: At the appointed gatherings and solemn feasts the grain offering will be an ephah for the bull and an ephah for the ram; for the lambs the offering will be as much as his hand can supply, and a hin of oil for every ephah.

first_reading.proposed: At the fairs and solemn feasts the grain offering will be an ephah for the bull and an ephah for the ram; for the lambs the offering will be as much as his hand can supply, and a hin of oil for every ephah.
first_reading.reason: 'in nundinis' means at the fairs (market days); 'appointed gatherings' is not what 'nundinae' means and echoes the Hebrew.

second_reading.note: 'in nundinis' is at the fairs or market days; 'appointed gatherings' echoes the Hebrew, not nundinae.

corrections.proposed_english: At the fairs and solemn feasts the grain offering will be an ephah for the bull and an ephah for the ram; for the lambs the offering will be as much as his hand can supply, and a hin of oil for every ephah.

corrections.latin: Porro plaga orientalis de medio Auran, et de medio Damasci, et de medio Galaad, et de medio terræ Israël, Jordanis disterminans ad mare orientale. Metiemini etiam plagam orientalem.
corrections.english: On the eastern side, between Hauran and Damascus, between Gilead and the land of Israel, the Jordan forms the boundary to the eastern sea. You will also measure the eastern side.

first_reading.proposed: On the eastern side, from the midst of Hauran, from the midst of Damascus, from the midst of Gilead, and from the midst of the land of Israel, the Jordan forms the boundary to the eastern sea. You will also measure the eastern side.
first_reading.reason: 'de medio Auran, et de medio Damasci, et de medio Galaad, et de medio terræ Israël' is four times 'from the midst of'; the paired 'between … and …' follows the Hebrew.

second_reading.note: 'de medio' four times is 'from the midst of'; paired 'between ... and' is the Hebrew construction.

corrections.proposed_english: On the eastern side, from the midst of Hauran, from the midst of Damascus, from the midst of Gilead, and from the midst of the land of Israel, the Jordan forms the boundary to the eastern sea. You will also measure the eastern side.

corrections.latin: Quod autem reliquum fuerit in longitudine secundum primitias sanctuarii, decem millia in orientem, et decem millia in occidentem, erunt sicut primitiæ sanctuarii : et erunt fruges ejus in panes his qui serviunt civitati.
corrections.english: What remains in length alongside the holy firstfruits, ten thousand to the east and ten thousand to the west, will lie alongside the holy firstfruits. Its produce will provide bread for those who serve the city.

first_reading.proposed: What remains in length alongside the holy firstfruits, ten thousand to the east and ten thousand to the west, will be like the holy firstfruits. Its produce will provide bread for those who serve the city.
first_reading.reason: 'erunt sicut primitiæ sanctuarii' is 'will be as/like the firstfruits of the sanctuary'; 'will lie alongside' follows the Hebrew, not 'sicut'.

second_reading.note: 'erunt sicut primitiæ sanctuarii' is 'will be as'; sicut is not 'alongside', which rendered 'secundum' earlier.

corrections.proposed_english: What remains in length alongside the holy firstfruits, ten thousand to the east and ten thousand to the west, will be like the holy firstfruits. Its produce will provide bread for those who serve the city.

corrections.latin: vidi in visione mea, cum essem in Susis castro, quod est in Ælam regione : vidi autem in visione esse me super portam Ulai.
corrections.english: saw in my vision that I was in the citadel of Susa, in the province of Elam. In the vision I saw myself above the gate of Ulai.

first_reading.proposed: saw in my vision, when I was in the citadel of Susa, in the province of Elam. In the vision I saw myself above the gate of Ulai.
first_reading.reason: 'cum essem in Susis castro' is 'when I was in the citadel of Susa' (his location while seeing); 'that I was' makes it the content of the vision, as in the Hebrew.

second_reading.note: 'cum essem in Susis castro' is temporal, 'when I was'; 'that I was' turns his location into the content of the vision.

corrections.proposed_english: saw in my vision, when I was in the citadel of Susa, in the province of Elam. In the vision I saw myself above the gate of Ulai.

corrections.latin: Et magnificatum est usque ad fortitudinem cæli : et dejecit de fortitudine, et de stellis, et conculcavit eas.
corrections.english: It grew great as far as the host of heaven and cast down some of the host and of the stars and trampled them.

first_reading.proposed: It grew great as far as the strength of heaven and cast down some of the strength and of the stars and trampled them.
first_reading.reason: 'fortitudinem cæli … de fortitudine' is 'the strength of heaven … of the strength'; 'host' renders the Hebrew word, not 'fortitudo'.

second_reading.note: 'fortitudinem cæli … de fortitudine' means strength; 'host' is not a sense of 'fortitudo' and follows the Hebrew.

corrections.proposed_english: It grew great as far as the strength of heaven and cast down some of the strength and of the stars and trampled them.

corrections.latin: Et usque ad principem fortitudinis magnificatum est : et ab eo tulit juge sacrificium, et dejecit locum sanctificationis ejus.
corrections.english: It grew great even against the prince of the host. It took the continual sacrifice away from him and cast down the place of his sanctuary.

first_reading.proposed: It grew great even against the prince of the strength. It took the continual sacrifice away from him and cast down the place of his sanctuary.
first_reading.reason: 'principem fortitudinis' is 'the prince of the strength'; 'host' follows the Hebrew, not 'fortitudo'.

second_reading.note: 'principem fortitudinis' is 'prince of the strength'; 'host' follows the Hebrew, not 'fortitudo'.

corrections.proposed_english: It grew great even against the prince of the strength. It took the continual sacrifice away from him and cast down the place of his sanctuary.

corrections.latin: Et audivi unum de sanctis loquentem : et dixit unus sanctus alteri nescio cui loquenti : Usquequo visio, et juge sacrificium, et peccatum desolationis quæ facta est : et sanctuarium, et fortitudo conculcabitur ?
corrections.english: I heard one of the holy ones speaking, and one holy one said to another who was speaking—I do not know who—‘How long will the vision last, concerning the continual sacrifice and the sin of desolation that has occurred? How long will the sanctuary and the host be trampled?’

first_reading.proposed: I heard one of the holy ones speaking, and one holy one said to another who was speaking—I do not know who—‘How long will the vision last, concerning the continual sacrifice and the sin of desolation that has occurred? How long will the sanctuary and the strength be trampled?’
first_reading.reason: 'sanctuarium, et fortitudo conculcabitur': 'fortitudo' is 'the strength'; 'host' follows the Hebrew.

second_reading.note: 'sanctuarium, et fortitudo conculcabitur': 'fortitudo' is strength; 'host' follows the Hebrew.

corrections.proposed_english: I heard one of the holy ones speaking, and one holy one said to another who was speaking—I do not know who—‘How long will the vision last, concerning the continual sacrifice and the sin of desolation that has occurred? How long will the sanctuary and the strength be trampled?’

corrections.latin: Nunc ergo exaudi, Deus noster, orationem servi tui, et preces ejus : et ostende faciem tuam super sanctuarium tuum, quod desertum est propter temetipsum.
corrections.english: Now, therefore, our God, hear the prayer and supplications of Your servant, and for Your own sake let Your face shine upon Your desolate sanctuary.

first_reading.proposed: Now, therefore, our God, hear the prayer and supplications of Your servant, and for Your own sake show Your face upon Your desolate sanctuary.
first_reading.reason: 'ostende faciem tuam super sanctuarium' is 'show Your face upon'; 'let Your face shine' is the Hebrew idiom, not 'ostende'.

second_reading.note: 'ostende faciem tuam' is 'show Your face'; 'let shine' would need 'illumina' and follows the Hebrew idiom.

corrections.proposed_english: Now, therefore, our God, hear the prayer and supplications of Your servant, and for Your own sake show Your face upon Your desolate sanctuary.

corrections.latin: Exaudi, Domine ; placare Domine : attende et fac : ne moreris propter temetipsum, Deus meus, quia nomen tuum invocatum est super civitatem et super populum tuum.
corrections.english: Hear, Lord; forgive, Lord; attend and act. Do not delay, for Your own sake, my God, because Your name is invoked over Your city and Your people.”

first_reading.proposed: Hear, Lord; be appeased, Lord; attend and act. Do not delay, for Your own sake, my God, because Your name is invoked over Your city and Your people.”
first_reading.reason: 'placare, Domine' is 'be appeased, Lord'; 'forgive' follows the Hebrew, not the Latin verb.

second_reading.note: 'placare' is passive imperative, 'be appeased'; 'forgive' renders the Hebrew verb instead.

corrections.proposed_english: Hear, Lord; be appeased, Lord; attend and act. Do not delay, for Your own sake, my God, because Your name is invoked over Your city and Your people.”

corrections.latin: Septuaginta hebdomades abbreviatæ sunt super populum tuum et super urbem sanctam tuam, ut consummetur prævaricatio, et finem accipiat peccatum, et deleatur iniquitas, et adducatur justitia sempiterna, et impleatur visio et prophetia, et ungatur Sanctus sanctorum.
corrections.english: Seventy weeks have been shortened for your people and your holy city, so that transgression may be brought to completion, sin come to an end, iniquity be wiped away, everlasting justice be brought in, vision and prophecy be fulfilled, and the Holy of Holies be anointed.

first_reading.proposed: Seventy weeks have been shortened for your people and your holy city, so that transgression may be brought to completion, sin come to an end, iniquity be wiped away, everlasting justice be brought in, vision and prophecy be fulfilled, and the Holy One of holy ones be anointed.
first_reading.reason: 'ungatur Sanctus sanctorum' is masculine, a person ('the Saint of saints'); 'the Holy of Holies' suggests the place (Sanctum sanctorum) and matches the Hebrew rather than this Latin.

second_reading.note: Masculine 'Sanctus sanctorum' denotes a person; 'Holy of Holies' reads as the neuter 'Sanctum sanctorum', the place.

corrections.proposed_english: Seventy weeks have been shortened for your people and your holy city, so that transgression may be brought to completion, sin come to an end, iniquity be wiped away, everlasting justice be brought in, vision and prophecy be fulfilled, and the Holy One of holy ones be anointed.

corrections.latin: Filii autem ejus provocabuntur, et congregabunt multitudinem exercituum plurimorum : et veniet properans, et inundans : et revertetur, et concitabitur, et congredietur cum robore ejus.
corrections.english: His sons will be provoked and gather a multitude of very great armies. He will come swiftly, sweeping in like a flood; he will return, be stirred up, and engage his stronghold.

first_reading.proposed: His sons will be provoked and gather a multitude of very great armies. He will come swiftly, sweeping in like a flood; he will return, be stirred up, and engage his forces.
first_reading.reason: 'congredietur cum robore ejus' is 'will join battle with his strength/forces'; 'stronghold' follows the Hebrew ('fortress'), not 'robur'.

second_reading.note: 'congredietur cum robore ejus' is 'with his strength/forces'; 'stronghold' is not what 'robur' means here and follows the Hebrew.

corrections.proposed_english: His sons will be provoked and gather a multitude of very great armies. He will come swiftly, sweeping in like a flood; he will return, be stirred up, and engage his forces.

corrections.latin: Et faciet juxta voluntatem suam rex, et elevabitur, et magnificabitur adversus omnem deum : et adversus Deum deorum loquetur magnifica, et dirigetur, donec compleatur iracundia : perpetrata quippe est definitio.
corrections.english: The king will do as he wills. He will exalt himself and magnify himself against every god; against the God of gods he will speak monstrous things. He will prosper until wrath is completed, for the determination has been made.

first_reading.proposed: The king will do as he wills. He will exalt himself and magnify himself against every god; against the God of gods he will speak great things. He will prosper until wrath is completed, for the determination has been made.
first_reading.reason: 'loquetur magnifica' is 'will speak great (boastful) things'; 'monstrous' is not a sense of 'magnifica'.

second_reading.note: 'loquetur magnifica' is 'will speak great (grand) things'; 'monstrous' lies outside the range of 'magnificus'.

corrections.proposed_english: The king will do as he wills. He will exalt himself and magnify himself against every god; against the God of gods he will speak great things. He will prosper until wrath is completed, for the determination has been made.

corrections.latin: Et percutiam cum eis fœdus in die illa, cum bestia agri, et cum volucre cæli, et cum reptili terræ ; et arcum, et gladium, et bellum conteram de terra, et dormire eos faciam fiducialiter.
corrections.english: On that day I will make a covenant for them with the wild beast, the bird of the sky, and the creeping creature of the earth. I will break bow and sword and warfare from the land and make them sleep in safety.

first_reading.proposed: On that day I will make a covenant with them, with the wild beast, the bird of the sky, and the creeping creature of the earth. I will break bow and sword and warfare from the land and make them sleep in safety.
first_reading.reason: Latin 'percutiam cum eis fœdus' is 'I will make a covenant with them'; English 'for them' follows the Hebrew, not 'cum eis'.

second_reading.note: 'percutiam cum eis fœdus' is a covenant 'with them'; 'for them' follows the Hebrew.

corrections.proposed_english: On that day I will make a covenant with them, with the wild beast, the bird of the sky, and the creeping creature of the earth. I will break bow and sword and warfare from the land and make them sleep in safety.

corrections.latin: Cum sanare vellem Israël, revelata est iniquitas Ephraim, et malitia Samariæ, quia operati sunt mendacium ; et fur ingressus est spolians, latrunculus foris.
corrections.english: When I wished to heal Israel, Ephraim's iniquity and Samaria's wickedness were uncovered, for they practiced deceit. A thief entered to plunder, a robber band outside.

first_reading.proposed: When I wished to heal Israel, Ephraim's iniquity and Samaria's wickedness were uncovered, for they practiced deceit. A thief entered to plunder, a robber outside.
first_reading.reason: 'latrunculus foris' is singular, 'a robber outside'; 'robber band' adds a collective sense taken from the Hebrew, not in the Latin.

second_reading.note: 'latrunculus' is singular, parallel to 'fur'; 'band' is added from the Hebrew collective.

corrections.proposed_english: When I wished to heal Israel, Ephraim's iniquity and Samaria's wickedness were uncovered, for they practiced deceit. A thief entered to plunder, a robber outside.

corrections.latin: In funiculis Adam traham eos, in vinculis caritatis ; et ero eis quasi exaltans jugum super maxillas eorum, et declinavi ad eum ut vesceretur.
corrections.english: With human cords I will draw them, with bonds of love. I will be to them like one lifting the yoke over their jaws, and I bent down to him so that he might eat.

first_reading.proposed: With the cords of Adam I will draw them, with bonds of love. I will be to them like one lifting the yoke over their jaws, and I bent down to him so that he might eat.
first_reading.reason: Latin keeps the name: 'In funiculis Adam' (cords of Adam). 'Human cords' renders the Hebrew common noun, not the Vulgate's proper name (cf. 6:7 'sicut Adam' kept as Adam).

second_reading.note: 'In funiculis Adam' keeps the name Adam; 'human cords' translates the Hebrew common noun instead.

corrections.proposed_english: With the cords of Adam I will draw them, with bonds of love. I will be to them like one lifting the yoke over their jaws, and I bent down to him so that he might eat.

corrections.latin: Et dixit Ephraim : Verumtamen dives effectus sum ; inveni idolum mihi : omnes labores mei non invenient mihi iniquitatem quam peccavi.
corrections.english: Ephraim said, “Yet I have become rich; I have found an idol for myself. In all my labors they will find no iniquity in me in which I have sinned.”

first_reading.proposed: Ephraim said, “Yet I have become rich; I have found an idol for myself. All my labors will find for me no iniquity in which I have sinned.”
first_reading.reason: 'omnes labores mei non invenient mihi iniquitatem': 'labores' is the subject (my labours will not find me iniquity). 'In all my labors they will find… in me' follows the Hebrew/KJV construction.

second_reading.note: 'omnes labores mei' is the nominative subject of 'non invenient mihi'; 'In all my labors they will find' follows the Hebrew/KJV construction.

corrections.proposed_english: Ephraim said, “Yet I have become rich; I have found an idol for myself. All my labors will find for me no iniquity in which I have sinned.”

corrections.latin: Auditum facite in ædibus Azoti, et in ædibus terræ Ægypti, et dicite : Congregamini super montes Samariæ, et videte insanias multas in medio ejus, et calumniam patientes in penetralibus ejus.
corrections.english: Make it heard in the buildings of Ashdod and in the buildings of the land of Egypt, and say: ‘Gather on the mountains of Samaria and see the many outrages in her midst, and those suffering oppression in her inner chambers.’

first_reading.proposed: Make it heard in the buildings of Ashdod and in the buildings of the land of Egypt, and say: ‘Gather on the mountains of Samaria and see the many acts of madness in her midst, and those suffering oppression in her inner chambers.’
first_reading.reason: 'insanias multas' means many madnesses/follies; 'outrages' is not a sense of 'insania'.

second_reading.note: 'insanias multas' is 'many madnesses/follies'; 'outrages' loses the sense of 'insania'.

corrections.proposed_english: Make it heard in the buildings of Ashdod and in the buildings of the land of Egypt, and say: ‘Gather on the mountains of Samaria and see the many acts of madness in her midst, and those suffering oppression in her inner chambers.’

corrections.latin: [Venite ad Bethel, et impie agite ; ad Galgalam, et multiplicate prævaricationem : et afferte mane victimas vestras, tribus diebus decimas vestras.
corrections.english: “Come to Bethel and act wickedly; to Gilgal and multiply transgression. Bring your victims in the morning and your tithes every three days.

first_reading.proposed: “Come to Bethel and act wickedly; to Gilgal and multiply transgression. Bring your victims in the morning and your tithes in three days.
first_reading.reason: 'tribus diebus decimas vestras' is 'your tithes in three days'; 'every three days' is a reading of the Hebrew, not of the Latin ablative.

second_reading.note: Ablative 'tribus diebus' is 'in three days'; distributive 'every three days' would be 'tertio quoque die' and reads the Hebrew.

corrections.proposed_english: “Come to Bethel and act wickedly; to Gilgal and multiply transgression. Bring your victims in the morning and your tithes in three days.

corrections.latin: Quia cognovi multa scelera vestra, et fortia peccata vestra : hostes justi, accipientes munus, et pauperes deprimentes in porta.
corrections.english: For I know your many crimes and your mighty sins: enemies of the righteous, accepting bribes and thrusting aside the poor at the gate.

first_reading.proposed: For I know your many crimes and your mighty sins: enemies of the righteous, accepting bribes and oppressing the poor at the gate.
first_reading.reason: 'pauperes deprimentes in porta' is pressing down/oppressing the poor; 'thrusting aside' renders the Hebrew verb, not 'deprimentes'.

second_reading.note: 'deprimentes' is pressing down, oppressing; 'thrusting aside' renders the Hebrew verb.

corrections.proposed_english: For I know your many crimes and your mighty sins: enemies of the righteous, accepting bribes and oppressing the poor at the gate.

corrections.latin: Hæc ostendit mihi Dominus Deus : et ecce fictor locustæ in principio germinantium serotini imbris, et ecce serotinus post tonsionem regis.
corrections.english: The Lord God showed me this: see, One forming locusts at the beginning of the growth after the late rain; and see, the late growth was after the king's mowing.

first_reading.proposed: The Lord God showed me this: see, One forming locusts at the beginning of the growth after the late rain; and see, the late rain was after the king's mowing.
first_reading.reason: 'et ecce serotinus post tonsionem regis': 'serotinus' (masc.) is the late rain (imber) just named; 'late growth' follows the Hebrew.

second_reading.note: Masculine 'serotinus' picks up 'serotini imbris', the late rain; 'late growth' follows the Hebrew.

corrections.proposed_english: The Lord God showed me this: see, One forming locusts at the beginning of the growth after the late rain; and see, the late rain was after the king's mowing.

corrections.latin: Qui ædificat in cælo ascensionem suam, et fasciculum suum super terram fundavit ; qui vocat aquas maris, et effundit eas super faciem terræ : Dominus nomen ejus.
corrections.english: He builds His ascent in heaven and has founded His vault upon the earth; He calls the waters of the sea and pours them over the earth's surface—the Lord is His name.

first_reading.proposed: He builds His ascent in heaven and has founded His bundle upon the earth; He calls the waters of the sea and pours them over the earth's surface—the Lord is His name.
first_reading.reason: 'fasciculum suum' means His bundle; 'vault' is the modern rendering of the Hebrew word, not a sense of 'fasciculus'.

second_reading.note: 'fasciculum suum' is 'His bundle'; 'vault' is not a sense of 'fasciculus' and follows the Hebrew.

corrections.proposed_english: He builds His ascent in heaven and has founded His bundle upon the earth; He calls the waters of the sea and pours them over the earth's surface—the Lord is His name.

corrections.latin: Væ mihi, quia factus sum sicut qui colligit in autumno racemos vindemiæ ! non est botrus ad comedendum, præcoquas ficus desideravit anima mea.
corrections.english: Woe to me, for I have become like one gathering clusters after the autumn vintage! There is no bunch to eat; my soul has longed for early figs.

first_reading.proposed: Woe to me, for I have become like one gathering in autumn the clusters of the vintage! There is no bunch to eat; my soul has longed for early figs.
first_reading.reason: 'qui colligit in autumno racemos vindemiæ' is one who gathers in autumn the clusters of the vintage; 'after the autumn vintage' adds 'after' and reattaches 'autumno' to the vintage.

second_reading.note: 'in autumno' modifies 'colligit' and 'racemos vindemiæ' is its object; 'after' has no Latin behind it.

corrections.proposed_english: Woe to me, for I have become like one gathering in autumn the clusters of the vintage! There is no bunch to eat; my soul has longed for early figs.

corrections.latin: Et tu ergo inebriaberis, et eris despecta : et tu quæres auxilium ab inimico.
corrections.english: You too, then, will become drunk and be despised; you too will seek help against the enemy.

first_reading.proposed: You too, then, will become drunk and be despised; you too will seek help from the enemy.
first_reading.reason: 'quæres auxilium ab inimico' is 'you will seek help from the enemy'; 'against the enemy' gives the Hebrew sense (refuge from), not the Latin 'ab inimico'.

second_reading.note: 'quæres auxilium ab inimico' is help from the enemy; 'against the enemy' reverses the relation, following the Hebrew sense.

corrections.proposed_english: You too, then, will become drunk and be despised; you too will seek help from the enemy.

corrections.latin: Mundi sunt oculi tui, ne videas malum, et respicere ad iniquitatem non poteris. Quare respicis super iniqua agentes, et taces devorante impio justiorem se ?
corrections.english: Your eyes are pure, so that You do not look upon evil, and You cannot look approvingly on iniquity. Why do You look upon those who act wickedly and remain silent while the wicked devours one more just than himself?

first_reading.proposed: Your eyes are pure, so that You do not look upon evil, and You cannot look on iniquity. Why do You look upon those who act wickedly and remain silent while the wicked devours one more just than himself?
first_reading.reason: 'respicere ad iniquitatem non poteris' is simply 'You cannot look upon iniquity'; 'approvingly' is added with nothing in the Latin behind it.

second_reading.note: 'respicere ad iniquitatem non poteris' has no adverb; 'approvingly' is added.

corrections.proposed_english: Your eyes are pure, so that You do not look upon evil, and You cannot look on iniquity. Why do You look upon those who act wickedly and remain silent while the wicked devours one more just than himself?

corrections.latin: Quia tu spoliasti gentes multas, spoliabunt te omnes qui reliqui fuerint de populis, propter sanguinem hominis, et iniquitatem terræ, civitatis, et omnium habitantium in ea.
corrections.english: Because you have plundered many nations, all the peoples who remain will plunder you, because of human bloodshed and the violence done to the land, the city, and all who dwell in it.

first_reading.proposed: Because you have plundered many nations, all the peoples who remain will plunder you, because of human bloodshed and the iniquity done to the land, the city, and all who dwell in it.
first_reading.reason: 'iniquitatem terræ' is iniquity/wrong; 'violence' is the Hebrew word, not a sense of 'iniquitas'.

second_reading.note: 'iniquitatem terræ' is iniquity/wrong; 'violence' is the Hebrew word, outside the range of 'iniquitas'.

corrections.proposed_english: Because you have plundered many nations, all the peoples who remain will plunder you, because of human bloodshed and the iniquity done to the land, the city, and all who dwell in it.

corrections.latin: Quia replebitur terra, ut cognoscant gloriam Domini, quasi aquæ operientes mare.
corrections.english: For the earth will be filled with knowledge of the Lord's glory, like waters covering the sea.

first_reading.proposed: For the earth will be filled, so that they may know the Lord's glory, like waters covering the sea.
first_reading.reason: Latin has a purpose clause, 'replebitur terra, ut cognoscant gloriam Domini' (that they may know); 'filled with knowledge of the Lord's glory' is the Hebrew/KJV construction.

second_reading.note: 'replebitur terra, ut cognoscant gloriam Domini' is a purpose clause; 'filled with knowledge of' follows the Hebrew/KJV.

corrections.proposed_english: For the earth will be filled, so that they may know the Lord's glory, like waters covering the sea.

corrections.latin: Quia iniquitas Libani operiet te, et vastitas animalium deterrebit eos de sanguinibus hominum, et iniquitate terræ, et civitatis, et omnium habitantium in ea.
corrections.english: For the violence done to Lebanon will cover you, and the devastation of animals will terrify them, because of human bloodshed and the violence done to the land, the city, and all who dwell in it.

first_reading.proposed: For the iniquity done to Lebanon will cover you, and the devastation of animals will terrify them, because of human bloodshed and the iniquity done to the land, the city, and all who dwell in it.
first_reading.reason: 'iniquitas Libani' and 'iniquitate terræ' are iniquity/wrong; 'violence' (twice) is the Hebrew word, not a sense of 'iniquitas'.

second_reading.note: 'iniquitas Libani' and 'iniquitate terræ' are iniquity/wrong; 'violence' twice follows the Hebrew.

corrections.proposed_english: For the iniquity done to Lebanon will cover you, and the devastation of animals will terrify them, because of human bloodshed and the iniquity done to the land, the city, and all who dwell in it.

corrections.latin: Et erit fortitudo eorum in direptionem, et domus eorum in desertum : et ædificabunt domos, et non habitabunt ; et plantabunt vineas, et non bibent vinum earum.
corrections.english: Their wealth will become plunder and their houses a wasteland. They will build houses but not inhabit them; they will plant vineyards but not drink their wine.

first_reading.proposed: Their strength will become plunder and their houses a wasteland. They will build houses but not inhabit them; they will plant vineyards but not drink their wine.
first_reading.reason: 'fortitudo eorum' is their strength; 'wealth' renders the Hebrew word, not 'fortitudo'.

second_reading.note: 'fortitudo eorum' is their strength; 'wealth' renders the Hebrew word, not 'fortitudo'.

corrections.proposed_english: Their strength will become plunder and their houses a wasteland. They will build houses but not inhabit them; they will plant vineyards but not drink their wine.

corrections.latin: Prophetæ ejus vesani, viri infideles ; sacerdotes ejus polluerunt sanctum, injuste egerunt contra legem.
corrections.english: Her prophets are reckless, faithless men. Her priests have defiled the holy place and acted unjustly against the law.

first_reading.proposed: Her prophets are mad, faithless men. Her priests have defiled the holy place and acted unjustly against the law.
first_reading.reason: 'vesani' means mad, senseless; 'reckless' is the usual rendering of the Hebrew word, not of 'vesani'.

second_reading.note: 'vesani' is mad, out of their senses; 'reckless' is weaker and matches the usual rendering of the Hebrew.

corrections.proposed_english: Her prophets are mad, faithless men. Her priests have defiled the holy place and acted unjustly against the law.

corrections.latin: Propterea hæc dicit Dominus : Revertar ad Jerusalem in misericordiis, et domus mea ædificabitur in ea, ait Dominus exercituum, et perpendiculum extendetur super Jerusalem.]
corrections.english: Therefore thus says the Lord: I will return to Jerusalem with mercies, and My house will be built in her, says the Lord of hosts, and the measuring line will be stretched over Jerusalem.

first_reading.proposed: Therefore thus says the Lord: I will return to Jerusalem with mercies, and My house will be built in her, says the Lord of hosts, and the plumb line will be stretched over Jerusalem.
first_reading.reason: "perpendiculum" is a plumb line (builder's line), not a measuring line; "measuring line" reflects the Hebrew, not this Latin word.

second_reading.note: 'perpendiculum' is a plumb line; the measuring line is 'funiculus mensorum' at 2:1.

corrections.proposed_english: Therefore thus says the Lord: I will return to Jerusalem with mercies, and My house will be built in her, says the Lord of hosts, and the plumb line will be stretched over Jerusalem.

corrections.latin: Et ego ero ei, ait Dominus, murus ignis in circuitu, et in gloria ero in medio ejus.
corrections.english: And I, says the Lord, will be a wall of fire all around her, and I will be glory in her midst.”

first_reading.proposed: And I, says the Lord, will be a wall of fire all around her, and I will be in glory in her midst.”
first_reading.reason: "in gloria ero in medio ejus" = I will be in glory in her midst; "I will be glory" drops "in" and follows the Hebrew.

second_reading.note: 'in gloria ero in medio ejus' is 'I will be in glory'; the current English drops 'in'.

corrections.proposed_english: And I, says the Lord, will be a wall of fire all around her, and I will be in glory in her midst.”

corrections.latin: Et dixit ad me : Quid tu vides ? Et dixi : Vidi, et ecce candelabrum aureum totum, et lampas ejus super caput ipsius, et septem lucernæ ejus super illud, et septem infusoria lucernis quæ erant super caput ejus.
corrections.english: He said to me, “What do you see?” I said, “I saw—and look, a lampstand all of gold, with its reservoir on top of it, its seven lamps upon it, and seven channels for the lamps on its top.

first_reading.proposed: He said to me, “What do you see?” I said, “I saw—and look, a lampstand all of gold, with its lamp on top of it, its seven lamps upon it, and seven channels for the lamps on its top.
first_reading.reason: "lampas ejus" means its lamp (torch), not a reservoir; "reservoir" reflects the Hebrew bowl, not the Latin word.

second_reading.note: 'lampas ejus super caput ipsius' is its lamp; 'reservoir' is the Hebrew bowl, not 'lampas'.

corrections.proposed_english: He said to me, “What do you see?” I said, “I saw—and look, a lampstand all of gold, with its lamp on top of it, its seven lamps upon it, and seven channels for the lamps on its top.

corrections.latin: Et duæ olivæ super illud : una a dextris lampadis, et una a sinistris ejus.
corrections.english: And there are two olive trees beside it, one to the right of the reservoir and one to its left.”

first_reading.proposed: And there are two olive trees over it, one to the right of the lamp and one to its left.”
first_reading.reason: "super illud" = over/above it, not beside it; "a dextris lampadis" = to the right of the lamp, not of a reservoir. English follows the Hebrew.

second_reading.note: 'super illud' is over it and 'a dextris lampadis' is right of the lamp; 'beside' and 'reservoir' follow the Hebrew.

corrections.proposed_english: And there are two olive trees over it, one to the right of the lamp and one to its left.”

corrections.latin: Et ecce talentum plumbi portabatur, et ecce mulier una sedens in medio amphoræ.
corrections.english: And look, a talent of lead was being lifted up, and there was a woman sitting inside the amphora.

first_reading.proposed: And look, a talent of lead was being carried, and there was a woman sitting inside the amphora.
first_reading.reason: "portabatur" = was being carried; "lifted up" follows the Hebrew, not this Latin verb.

second_reading.note: 'portabatur' is 'was being carried'; 'lifted up' renders the Hebrew verb.

corrections.proposed_english: And look, a talent of lead was being carried, and there was a woman sitting inside the amphora.

corrections.latin: et loqueris ad eum, dicens : Hæc ait Dominus exercituum, dicens : Ecce vir, Oriens nomen ejus, et subter eum orietur, et ædificabit templum Domino.
corrections.english: Speak to him, saying: Thus says the Lord of hosts: Look, a man whose name is the Rising One! He will rise from his own place, and he will build a temple for the Lord.

first_reading.proposed: Speak to him, saying: Thus says the Lord of hosts: Look, a man whose name is the Rising One! Under him there will be a rising, and he will build a temple for the Lord.
first_reading.reason: "subter eum orietur" = under him he (it) shall spring up; "from his own place" is the usual interpretation of the Hebrew, not a rendering of "subter eum".

second_reading.note: 'subter eum orietur' is 'under him he will rise'; 'from his own place' follows the Hebrew, but the proposal's impersonal noun loses the personal verb.

corrections.proposed_english: Speak to him, saying: Thus says the Lord of hosts: Look, a man whose name is the Rising One! Under him he will rise, and he will build a temple for the Lord.

corrections.latin: Et miserunt ad domum Dei Sarasar et Rogommelech, et viri qui erant cum eo, ad deprecandam faciem Domini :
corrections.english: They sent Sharezer and Regem-melech, and the men who were with him, to the house of God to entreat the Lord's favor,

first_reading.proposed: Sharezer and Regem-melech, and the men who were with him, sent to the house of God to entreat the Lord's favor,
first_reading.reason: "viri qui erant cum eo" is nominative: Sarasar, Rogommelech and the men are the senders ("miserunt ad domum Dei"), not persons sent by an unnamed "they".

second_reading.note: 'viri qui erant cum eo' is nominative, so Sarasar, Rogommelech and the men are subjects of 'miserunt', not the ones sent.

corrections.proposed_english: Sharezer and Regem-melech, and the men who were with him, sent to the house of God to entreat the Lord's favor,

corrections.latin: Et noluerunt attendere, et averterunt scapulam recedentem, et aures suas aggravaverunt ne audirent.
corrections.english: But they refused to pay attention; they turned a stubborn shoulder and made their ears heavy so that they would not hear.

first_reading.proposed: But they refused to pay attention; they turned away a withdrawing shoulder and made their ears heavy so that they would not hear.
first_reading.reason: "scapulam recedentem" = a shoulder drawing back/departing; "stubborn" renders the Hebrew adjective, not "recedentem".

second_reading.note: 'averterunt scapulam recedentem' is a shoulder drawing away; 'stubborn' renders the Hebrew adjective.

corrections.proposed_english: But they refused to pay attention; they turned away a withdrawing shoulder and made their ears heavy so that they would not hear.

corrections.latin: Quoniam extendi mihi Judam quasi arcum : implevi Ephraim : et suscitabo filios tuos, Sion, super filios tuos, Græcia : et ponam te quasi gladium fortium.
corrections.english: For I have bent Judah for Myself as a bow and fitted Ephraim into it. I will rouse your sons, Zion, against your sons, Greece, and make you like a warrior's sword.

first_reading.proposed: For I have bent Judah for Myself as a bow; I have filled Ephraim. I will rouse your sons, Zion, against your sons, Greece, and make you like a warrior's sword.
first_reading.reason: "implevi Ephraim" = I have filled Ephraim; "fitted Ephraim into it" makes Ephraim the arrow set in the bow, an interpretation of the Hebrew not stated by the Latin.

second_reading.note: 'implevi Ephraim' is 'I have filled Ephraim'; 'fitted … into it' adds the arrow image from the Hebrew.

corrections.proposed_english: For I have bent Judah for Myself as a bow; I have filled Ephraim. I will rouse your sons, Zion, against your sons, Greece, and make you like a warrior's sword.

corrections.latin: Ulula, abies, quia cecidit cedrus, quoniam magnifici vastati sunt : ululate, quercus Basan, quoniam succisus est saltus munitus.
corrections.english: Wail, cypress, for the cedar has fallen, because the magnificent trees have been laid waste. Wail, oaks of Bashan, for the fortified forest has been cut down.

first_reading.proposed: Wail, fir tree, for the cedar has fallen, because the magnificent trees have been laid waste. Wail, oaks of Bashan, for the fortified forest has been cut down.
first_reading.reason: "abies" is the fir tree, not the cypress; "cypress" reflects modern renderings of the Hebrew.

second_reading.note: 'abies' is the fir; cypress would be 'cupressus'.

corrections.proposed_english: Wail, fir tree, for the cedar has fallen, because the magnificent trees have been laid waste. Wail, oaks of Bashan, for the fortified forest has been cut down.

corrections.latin: Ecce ego ponam Jerusalem superliminare crapulæ omnibus populis in circuitu : sed et Juda erit in obsidione contra Jerusalem.
corrections.english: Look, I will make Jerusalem a threshold of drunkenness to all the surrounding peoples. Judah too will be involved in the siege against Jerusalem.

first_reading.proposed: Look, I will make Jerusalem a lintel of drunkenness to all the surrounding peoples. Judah too will be involved in the siege against Jerusalem.
first_reading.reason: "superliminare" is the lintel (the beam above the door), not the threshold (limen).

second_reading.note: 'superliminare' is the lintel above the door; threshold is 'limen'.

corrections.proposed_english: Look, I will make Jerusalem a lintel of drunkenness to all the surrounding peoples. Judah too will be involved in the siege against Jerusalem.

corrections.latin: Et revertetur omnis terra usque ad desertum, de colle Remmon ad austrum Jerusalem : et exaltabitur, et habitabit in loco suo, a porta Benjamin usque ad locum portæ prioris, et usque ad portam angulorum, et a turre Hananeel usque ad torcularia regis.
corrections.english: All the land will become like the desert, from the hill of Rimmon south of Jerusalem. Jerusalem will be raised up and remain in her place, from the Benjamin Gate to the site of the former gate, as far as the Corner Gate, and from the Tower of Hananel to the king's winepresses.

first_reading.proposed: All the land will return as far as the desert, from the hill of Rimmon south of Jerusalem. Jerusalem will be raised up and remain in her place, from the Benjamin Gate to the site of the former gate, as far as the Corner Gate, and from the Tower of Hananel to the king's winepresses.
first_reading.reason: "revertetur omnis terra usque ad desertum" = all the land shall return as far as the desert; "will become like the desert" follows the Hebrew (turned into a plain), not the Latin.

second_reading.note: 'revertetur omnis terra usque ad desertum' is 'will return as far as the desert'; 'become like the desert' follows the Hebrew.

corrections.proposed_english: All the land will return as far as the desert, from the hill of Rimmon south of Jerusalem. Jerusalem will be raised up and remain in her place, from the Benjamin Gate to the site of the former gate, as far as the Corner Gate, and from the Tower of Hananel to the king's winepresses.

corrections.latin: Et sic erit ruina equi, et muli, et cameli, et asini, et omnium jumentorum quæ fuerint in castris illis, sicut ruina hæc.
corrections.english: A plague like this will fall upon the horse, mule, camel, donkey, and all the beasts in those camps.

first_reading.proposed: A ruin like this will fall upon the horse, mule, camel, donkey, and all the beasts in those camps.
first_reading.reason: "ruina ... sicut ruina hæc" = ruin, downfall, destruction; "plague" renders the Hebrew word (Latin "plaga" stands only in v. 12).

second_reading.note: 'ruina … sicut ruina hæc' is ruin/destruction; 'plague' would be 'plaga' (v. 12) and follows the Hebrew.

corrections.proposed_english: A ruin like this will fall upon the horse, mule, camel, donkey, and all the beasts in those camps.

corrections.latin: Quod etsi familia Ægypti non ascenderit et non venerit, nec super eos erit : sed erit ruina, qua percutiet Dominus omnes gentes quæ non ascenderint ad celebrandam festivitatem tabernaculorum.
corrections.english: If the family of Egypt does not go up and does not come, there will be none upon them either; instead there will be the plague with which the Lord strikes all the nations that do not go up to celebrate the Festival of Tabernacles.

first_reading.proposed: If the family of Egypt does not go up and does not come, there will be none upon them either; instead there will be the ruin with which the Lord strikes all the nations that do not go up to celebrate the Festival of Tabernacles.
first_reading.reason: "erit ruina, qua percutiet Dominus" = there will be the ruin/destruction with which the Lord strikes; "plague" renders the Hebrew, not "ruina".

second_reading.note: 'erit ruina, qua percutiet Dominus' is ruin/destruction; 'plague' follows the Hebrew, not 'ruina'.

corrections.proposed_english: If the family of Egypt does not go up and does not come, there will be none upon them either; instead there will be the ruin with which the Lord strikes all the nations that do not go up to celebrate the Festival of Tabernacles.

corrections.latin: Hoc erit peccatum Ægypti, et hoc peccatum omnium gentium quæ non ascenderint ad celebrandam festivitatem tabernaculorum.
corrections.english: This will be Egypt's punishment for sin and the punishment for sin of all the nations that do not go up to celebrate the Festival of Tabernacles.

first_reading.proposed: This will be Egypt's sin and the sin of all the nations that do not go up to celebrate the Festival of Tabernacles.
first_reading.reason: "Hoc erit peccatum Ægypti, et hoc peccatum omnium gentium" says sin; "punishment for sin" (twice) adds an interpretation the Latin word does not carry.

second_reading.note: 'Hoc erit peccatum Ægypti, et hoc peccatum omnium gentium' says sin; 'punishment for' is added twice.

corrections.proposed_english: This will be Egypt's sin and the sin of all the nations that do not go up to celebrate the Festival of Tabernacles.

corrections.latin: Disperdet Dominus virum qui fecerit hoc, magistrum et discipulum, de tabernaculis Jacob, et offerentem munus Domino exercituum.
corrections.english: May the Lord destroy from the tents of Jacob the man who does this, teacher and disciple, and the one who presents an offering to the Lord of hosts.

first_reading.proposed: The Lord will destroy from the tents of Jacob the man who does this, teacher and disciple, and the one who presents an offering to the Lord of hosts.
first_reading.reason: "Disperdet Dominus" is future indicative, a statement that the Lord will destroy; "May the Lord destroy" turns it into a wish (that would be "disperdat").

second_reading.note: 'Disperdet' is future indicative, 'will destroy'; a wish would be 'disperdat'.

corrections.proposed_english: The Lord will destroy from the tents of Jacob the man who does this, teacher and disciple, and the one who presents an offering to the Lord of hosts.

corrections.latin: Ecce ego mitto angelum meum, et præparabit viam ante faciem meam : et statim veniet ad templum suum Dominator quem vos quæritis, et angelus testamenti quem vos vultis. Ecce venit, dicit Dominus exercituum.
corrections.english: Look, I am sending My messenger, and he will prepare the way before Me. Suddenly the Ruler whom you seek will come to His temple, and the messenger of the covenant whom you desire. Look, he is coming, says the Lord of hosts.

first_reading.proposed: Look, I am sending My messenger, and he will prepare the way before Me. Immediately the Ruler whom you seek will come to His temple, and the messenger of the covenant whom you desire. Look, he is coming, says the Lord of hosts.
first_reading.reason: "statim veniet" = will come at once, immediately; "Suddenly" renders the Hebrew adverb, not "statim".

second_reading.note: 'statim veniet' is at once, immediately; 'suddenly' would be 'subito' and follows the Hebrew.

corrections.proposed_english: Look, I am sending My messenger, and he will prepare the way before Me. Immediately the Ruler whom you seek will come to His temple, and the messenger of the covenant whom you desire. Look, he is coming, says the Lord of hosts.

corrections.latin: Et siquidem fuerit domus illa digna, veniet pax vestra super eam: si autem non fuerit digna, pax vestra revertetur ad vos.
corrections.english: And if that house be worthy, your peace shall come upon it; but if it do not be worthy, your peace shall return to you.

first_reading.proposed: And if that house be worthy, your peace shall come upon it; but if it be not worthy, your peace shall return to you.
first_reading.reason: "if it do not be worthy" is ungrammatical English for "si autem non fuerit digna" (if it be not worthy); a slip of the modernisation.

second_reading.note: 'si autem non fuerit digna' is 'if it be not worthy'; 'if it do not be' is broken English.

corrections.proposed_english: And if that house be worthy, your peace shall come upon it; but if it be not worthy, your peace shall return to you.

corrections.latin: Et stupebant omnes turbæ, et dicebant: Numquid hic est filius David?
corrections.english: And all the multitudes were amazed, and said: Is not this the son of David?

first_reading.proposed: And all the multitudes were amazed, and said: Is this the son of David?
first_reading.reason: "Numquid hic est filius David?" asks doubtfully (Can this be...?), expecting no; "Is not this" renders "nonne" and reverses the expected answer.

second_reading.note: 'Numquid hic est' asks doubtfully, expecting no; 'Is not this' renders 'nonne' and reverses the expectation.

corrections.proposed_english: And all the multitudes were amazed, and said: Is this the son of David?

corrections.latin: Et ait illis: Inimicus homo hoc fecit. Servi autem dixerunt ei: Vis, imus, et colligimus ea?
corrections.english: And he said to them: An enemy has done this. And the servants said to him: Will you that we go and gather it up?

first_reading.proposed: And he said to them: An enemy has done this. And the servants said to him: Will you that we go and gather them up?
first_reading.reason: "colligimus ea" (plural, the zizania); after the change of "cockle" to "weeds" (v. 27) the singular "it" no longer agrees.

second_reading.note: 'colligimus ea' is neuter plural for 'zizania', now 'weeds'; singular 'it' no longer agrees.

corrections.proposed_english: And he said to them: An enemy has done this. And the servants said to him: Will you that we go and gather them up?

corrections.latin: Et ait: Non: ne forte colligentes zizania, eradicetis simul cum eis et triticum.
corrections.english: And he said: No, lest gathering up the weeds, you root up the wheat also together with it.

first_reading.proposed: And he said: No, lest gathering up the weeds, you root up the wheat also together with them.
first_reading.reason: "simul cum eis" = together with them; "it" is left over from the Douay singular "cockle" and does not agree with "weeds".

second_reading.note: 'simul cum eis' is plural, 'together with them'; 'it' does not agree with 'the weeds'.

corrections.proposed_english: And he said: No, lest gathering up the weeds, you root up the wheat also together with them.

corrections.latin: Sinite utraque crescere usque ad messem, et in tempore messis dicam messoribus: Colligite primum zizania, et alligate ea in fasciculos ad comburendum: triticum autem congregate in horreum meum.
corrections.english: Suffer both to grow until the harvest, and in the time of the harvest I will say to the reapers: Gather up first the weeds, and bind it into bundles to burn, but the wheat gather you into my barn.

first_reading.proposed: Suffer both to grow until the harvest, and in the time of the harvest I will say to the reapers: Gather up first the weeds, and bind them into bundles to burn, but the wheat gather you into my barn.
first_reading.reason: "alligate ea" = bind them; "bind it" does not agree with "the weeds" (leftover of the Douay singular "cockle").

second_reading.note: 'alligate ea' is 'bind them'; 'bind it' disagrees with 'the weeds'.

corrections.proposed_english: Suffer both to grow until the harvest, and in the time of the harvest I will say to the reapers: Gather up first the weeds, and bind them into bundles to burn, but the wheat gather you into my barn.

corrections.latin: Sicut ergo colliguntur zizania, et igni comburuntur: sic erit in consummatione sæculi.
corrections.english: Even as weeds therefore is gathered up, and burnt with fire: so shall it be at the end of the world.

first_reading.proposed: Even as weeds therefore are gathered up, and burnt with fire: so shall it be at the end of the world.
first_reading.reason: "colliguntur zizania" is plural; "weeds ... is gathered up" is a broken agreement left by replacing the Douay singular "cockle".

second_reading.note: 'colliguntur zizania' is plural; 'weeds … is gathered up' is broken agreement.

corrections.proposed_english: Even as weeds therefore are gathered up, and burnt with fire: so shall it be at the end of the world.

corrections.latin: Accessit autem et qui duo talenta acceperat, et ait: Domine, duo talenta tradidisti mihi, ecce alia duo lucratus sum.
corrections.english: And he also that had received the two talents came and said: Lord, you deliveredst two talents to me. Behold I have gained other two.

first_reading.proposed: And he also that had received the two talents came and said: Lord, you delivered two talents to me. Behold I have gained other two.
first_reading.reason: "you deliveredst" keeps the archaic second-person singular ending after modernised "you" (Latin "tradidisti"); ungrammatical leftover from "thou deliveredst".

second_reading.note: 'tradidisti' is 'you delivered'; 'you deliveredst' is an ungrammatical leftover of 'thou deliveredst'.

corrections.proposed_english: And he also that had received the two talents came and said: Lord, you delivered two talents to me. Behold I have gained other two.

corrections.latin: dicens: Peccavi, tradens sanguinem justum. At illi dixerunt: Quid ad nos? tu videris.
corrections.english: Saying: I have sinned in betraying innocent blood. But they said: What is that to us? Look you to it.

first_reading.proposed: Saying: I have sinned in betraying just blood. But they said: What is that to us? Look you to it.
first_reading.reason: "innocent blood" is Challoner's wording after the Greek/KJV; the Latin has "sanguinem justum", just blood (cf. "sanguis justus" 23:35, "justi hujus" 27:24, both rendered "just").

second_reading.note: 'sanguinem justum' is just blood; 'innocent' follows the Greek, and the Latin uses 'innocens' separately at 27:24.

corrections.proposed_english: Saying: I have sinned in betraying just blood. But they said: What is that to us? Look you to it.

corrections.latin: confidit in Deo: liberet nunc, si vult eum: dixit enim: Quia Filius Dei sum.
corrections.english: He trusted in God: let him now deliver him if he will have him. For he said: I am the Son of God.

first_reading.proposed: He trusts in God: let him now deliver him if he will have him. For he said: I am the Son of God.
first_reading.reason: "confidit" is present tense (the perfect of confido is "confisus est"): he trusts in God, not "trusted".

second_reading.note: 'confidit' is present tense of the semi-deponent (perfect 'confisus est'): 'He trusts', not 'trusted'.

corrections.proposed_english: He trusts in God: let him now deliver him if he will have him. For he said: I am the Son of God.

corrections.latin: Quæ cum abiissent, ecce quidam de custodibus venerunt in civitatem, et nuntiaverunt principibus sacerdotum omnia quæ facta fuerant.
corrections.english: While they were going, behold, some of the guards came into the city and reported to the chief priests everything that had happened.

first_reading.proposed: When they had gone, behold, some of the guards came into the city and reported to the chief priests everything that had happened.
first_reading.reason: "Quæ cum abiissent" is pluperfect: when they (the women) had departed. "While they were going" follows the Greek present participle, not the Latin.

second_reading.note: 'Quæ cum abiissent' is pluperfect, 'when they had gone'; 'while they were going' follows the Greek participle.

corrections.proposed_english: When they had gone, behold, some of the guards came into the city and reported to the chief priests everything that had happened.

corrections.latin: Et venerunt trans fretum maris in regionem Gerasenorum.
corrections.english: And they came over the narrow of the sea, into the country of the Gerasens.

first_reading.proposed: And they came over the strait of the sea, into the country of the Gerasens.
first_reading.reason: "the narrow of the sea" is broken English: Douay "strait" (noun, for "fretum") has been wrongly modernised to the adjective "narrow".

second_reading.note: 'trans fretum maris' is 'over the strait of the sea'; 'the narrow of the sea' is broken English.

corrections.proposed_english: And they came over the strait of the sea, into the country of the Gerasens.

corrections.latin: Et cum transcendisset Jesus in navi rursum trans fretum, convenit turba multa ad eum, et erat circa mare.
corrections.english: And when Jesus had passed again in the boat over the narrow, a great multitude assembled together to him, and he was near to the sea.

first_reading.proposed: And when Jesus had passed again in the boat over the strait, a great multitude assembled together to him, and he was near to the sea.
first_reading.reason: "over the narrow" is broken English: "trans fretum" is "over the strait"; the noun "strait" was wrongly replaced by the adjective "narrow".

second_reading.note: 'trans fretum' is 'over the strait'; 'over the narrow' is broken English.

corrections.proposed_english: And when Jesus had passed again in the boat over the strait, a great multitude assembled together to him, and he was near to the sea.

corrections.latin: Et intuens illos Jesus, ait: Apud homines impossibile est, sed non apud Deum: omnia enim possibilia sunt apud Deum.
corrections.english: And Jesus looking on them, says with men it is impossible; but not with God. For all things are possible with God.

first_reading.proposed: And Jesus looking on them, says: With men it is impossible; but not with God. For all things are possible with God.
first_reading.reason: Colon and capital lost after "says" ("ait: Apud homines impossibile est"), so the text reads as "says with men"; the speech is not marked off.

second_reading.note: 'ait: Apud homines impossibile est' opens direct speech; without colon and capital the English runs 'says with men'.

corrections.proposed_english: And Jesus looking on them, says: With men it is impossible; but not with God. For all things are possible with God.

corrections.latin: Et respondens angelus dixit ei: Ego sum Gabriel, qui asto ante Deum: et missus sum loqui ad te, et hæc tibi evangelizare.
corrections.english: And the angel answered him: I am Gabriel, who stand before God and am sent to speak to you and to bring you these good news.

first_reading.proposed: And the angel answered him: I am Gabriel, who stand before God and am sent to speak to you and to bring you this good news.
first_reading.reason: Grammatical slip from modernising: 'these good news' (for 'hæc tibi evangelizare'); 'news' is singular in modern English, so 'this good news'.

second_reading.note: 'hæc tibi evangelizare': 'news' is singular in English, so 'these good news' is ungrammatical.

corrections.proposed_english: And the angel answered him: I am Gabriel, who stand before God and am sent to speak to you and to bring you this good news.

corrections.latin: et ut darent hostiam secundum quod dictum est in lege Domini, par turturum, aut duos pullos columbarum.
corrections.english: And to offer a sacrifice, just as it is written in the law of the Lord, a pair of turtledoves or two young pigeons:

first_reading.proposed: And to offer a sacrifice, just as it is said in the law of the Lord, a pair of turtledoves or two young pigeons:
first_reading.reason: 'secundum quod dictum est' means 'as it is said', not 'written' (contrast 'scriptum est' in v. 23).

second_reading.note: 'dictum est' is 'it is said'; 'written' is 'scriptum est', which the Latin uses in v. 23.

corrections.proposed_english: And to offer a sacrifice, just as it is said in the law of the Lord, a pair of turtledoves or two young pigeons:

corrections.latin: Perambulabat autem magis sermo de illo: et conveniebant turbæ multæ ut audirent, et curarentur ab infirmitatibus suis.
corrections.english: But the fame of him went abroad the more: and great multitudes came together to hear and to be healed by him of their infirmities.

first_reading.proposed: But the fame of him went abroad the more: and great multitudes came together to hear and to be healed of their infirmities.
first_reading.reason: 'by him' has no Latin behind it: 'ut audirent, et curarentur ab infirmitatibus suis' has no 'ab eo'; the Douay wording reflects the Greek received text.

second_reading.note: 'curarentur ab infirmitatibus suis' has no 'ab eo'; 'by him' is added from the Greek received text.

corrections.proposed_english: But the fame of him went abroad the more: and great multitudes came together to hear and to be healed of their infirmities.

corrections.latin: Factum est autem in una dierum: et ipse ascendit in naviculam, et discipuli ejus, et ait ad illos: Transfretemus trans stagnum. Et ascenderunt.
corrections.english: And it happened on a certain day that he went into a little boat with his disciples. And he said to them: Let us go over to the other side of the lake. And they launched forth.

first_reading.proposed: And it happened on a certain day that he went into a little boat with his disciples. And he said to them: Let us go over to the other side of the lake. And they went aboard.
first_reading.reason: 'Et ascenderunt' means 'they went up/embarked' (same verb as 'ascendit in naviculam'); 'launched forth' renders the Greek verb, not the Latin.

second_reading.note: 'Et ascenderunt' repeats the verb of 'ascendit in naviculam' (went up, embarked); 'launched forth' renders the Greek verb, not 'ascenderunt'.

corrections.proposed_english: And it happened on a certain day that he went into a little boat with his disciples. And he said to them: Let us go over to the other side of the lake. And they went aboard.

corrections.latin: Et conversus increpavit illos, dicens: Nescitis cujus spiritus estis.
corrections.english: And turning, he rebuked them, saying: you do not know of what spirit you are.

first_reading.proposed: And turning, he rebuked them, saying: You do not know of what spirit you are.
first_reading.reason: Lower-case 'you' begins the quoted speech ('Nescitis cujus spiritus estis'); elsewhere speech after a colon is capitalised.

second_reading.note: Direct speech 'Nescitis cujus spiritus estis' begins a new sentence after 'dicens:'; lower-case 'you' is a slip.

corrections.proposed_english: And turning, he rebuked them, saying: You do not know of what spirit you are.

corrections.latin: Vide ergo ne lumen quod in te est, tenebræ sint.
corrections.english: Take care therefore that the light which is in you do not be darkness.

first_reading.proposed: Take care therefore that the light which is in you be not darkness.
first_reading.reason: Ungrammatical 'do not be darkness' for 'ne ... tenebræ sint'; the subjunctive needs 'be not darkness'.

second_reading.note: 'ne ... tenebræ sint' is 'be not darkness'; 'do not be darkness' is broken English.

corrections.proposed_english: Take care therefore that the light which is in you be not darkness.

corrections.latin: Si ergo neque quod minimum est potestis, quid de ceteris solliciti estis?
corrections.english: If then you do not be able to do so much as the least thing, why are you anxious for the rest?

first_reading.proposed: If then you are not able to do so much as the least thing, why are you anxious for the rest?
first_reading.reason: Ungrammatical 'you do not be able' for 'neque ... potestis' ('you are not able'); a slip from modernising 'ye be not able'.

second_reading.note: 'neque ... potestis' is 'you are not able'; 'you do not be able' is ungrammatical.

corrections.proposed_english: If then you are not able to do so much as the least thing, why are you anxious for the rest?

corrections.latin: Sicut illi decem et octo, supra quos cecidit turris in Siloë, et occidit eos: putatis quia et ipsi debitores fuerint præter omnes homines habitantes in Jerusalem?
corrections.english: Or those eighteen upon whom the tower fell in Siloam and slew them: think you that they also were debtors above all the men that dwelt in Jerusalem?

first_reading.proposed: Like those eighteen upon whom the tower fell in Siloam and slew them: think you that they also were debtors above all the men that dwelt in Jerusalem?
first_reading.reason: 'Sicut illi decem et octo' is 'Like/as those eighteen'; the opening 'Or' follows the Greek conjunction, not the Latin 'Sicut'.

second_reading.note: 'Sicut illi decem et octo' is 'Like those eighteen'; 'Or' renders the Greek conjunction, not 'Sicut'.

corrections.proposed_english: Like those eighteen upon whom the tower fell in Siloam and slew them: think you that they also were debtors above all the men that dwelt in Jerusalem?

corrections.latin: Erat autem docens in synagoga eorum sabbatis.
corrections.english: And he was teaching in their synagogue on their sabbath.

first_reading.proposed: And he was teaching in their synagogue on the sabbath.
