first_reading.reason: 'sabbatis' has no possessive; 'eorum' belongs only to 'synagoga', so 'on their sabbath' adds a word the Latin lacks.

second_reading.note: 'in synagoga eorum sabbatis' has one 'eorum', with 'synagoga'; 'their sabbath' repeats a possessive the Latin lacks.

corrections.proposed_english: And he was teaching in their synagogue on the sabbath.

corrections.latin: Et laudavit dominus villicum iniquitatis, quia prudenter fecisset: quia filii hujus sæculi prudentiores filiis lucis in generatione sua sunt.
corrections.english: The master praised the unjust steward because he had acted prudently. For the children of this age are more prudent toward their own generation than the children of light.

first_reading.proposed: The master praised the unjust steward because he had acted prudently. For the children of this age are more prudent in their generation than the children of light.
first_reading.reason: 'in generatione sua' (ablative) is 'in their generation'; 'toward their own generation' renders the Greek preposition, not the Latin.

second_reading.note: 'in generatione sua' (in with ablative) is 'in their generation'; 'toward' follows the Greek preposition.

corrections.proposed_english: The master praised the unjust steward because he had acted prudently. For the children of this age are more prudent in their generation than the children of light.

corrections.latin: Et ait illis: Vos estis qui justificatis vos coram hominibus: Deus autem novit corda vestra: quia quod hominibus altum est, abominatio est ante Deum.
corrections.english: And he said to them: you are they who justify yourselves before men, but God knows your hearts. For that which is high to men is an abomination before God.

first_reading.proposed: And he said to them: You are they who justify yourselves before men, but God knows your hearts. For that which is high to men is an abomination before God.
first_reading.reason: Lower-case 'you' begins the quoted speech ('Vos estis qui justificatis vos'); elsewhere speech after a colon is capitalised.

second_reading.note: Direct speech 'Vos estis qui justificatis vos' begins after 'ait illis:'; lower-case 'you' is a slip.

corrections.proposed_english: And he said to them: You are they who justify yourselves before men, but God knows your hearts. For that which is high to men is an abomination before God.

corrections.latin: At illi cogitabant intra se, dicentes: Quia si dixerimus: De cælo, dicet: Quare ergo non credidistis illi?
corrections.english: But they thought within themselves, saying: If we shall say, From heaven: he will say: Why then did you not believe in him?

first_reading.proposed: But they thought within themselves, saying: If we shall say, From heaven: he will say: Why then did you not believe him?
first_reading.reason: 'credidistis illi' (dative) is 'believed him', i.e. gave credence to John; 'believe in him' adds a sense the Latin lacks.

second_reading.note: 'credidistis illi' with the dative is 'believed him' (gave him credence), not 'believed in him'.

corrections.proposed_english: But they thought within themselves, saying: If we shall say, From heaven: he will say: Why then did you not believe him?

corrections.latin: Ait: Ego vox clamantis in deserto: Dirigite viam Domini, sicut dixit Isaias propheta.
corrections.english: He said: I am a voice crying in the wilderness, Make straight the way of the Lord, as Isaiah the prophet said.

first_reading.proposed: He said: I am the voice of one crying in the wilderness, Make straight the way of the Lord, as Isaiah the prophet said.
first_reading.reason: 'vox clamantis' is 'the voice of one crying' (genitive participle); 'a voice crying' drops the person who cries and makes the voice itself the crier.

second_reading.note: 'vox clamantis' has the genitive participle: 'the voice of one crying'; 'a voice crying' makes the voice the crier.

corrections.proposed_english: He said: I am the voice of one crying in the wilderness, Make straight the way of the Lord, as Isaiah the prophet said.

corrections.latin: Venite, et videte hominem qui dixit mihi omnia quæcumque feci: numquid ipse est Christus?
corrections.english: Come, and see a man who has told me all things whatever I have done. Is not he the Christ?

first_reading.proposed: Come, and see a man who has told me all things whatever I have done. Is he perhaps the Christ?
first_reading.reason: 'numquid ipse est Christus?' is a tentative question ('can this be the Christ?'); 'Is not he the Christ?' turns it into a question expecting yes, as if the Latin were 'nonne'.

second_reading.note: 'numquid ipse est Christus?' is a tentative question; 'Is not he' would need 'nonne' and expects yes.

corrections.proposed_english: Come, and see a man who has told me all things whatever I have done. Is he perhaps the Christ?

corrections.latin: Et exinde quærebat Pilatus dimittere eum. Judæi autem clamabant dicentes: Si hunc dimittis, non es amicus Cæsaris. Omnis enim qui se regem facit, contradicit Cæsari.
corrections.english: And from now on Pilate sought to release him. But the Jews cried out, saying: If you release this man, you are not Caesar’s friend. For whoever makes himself a king speaks against Caesar.

first_reading.proposed: And from then on Pilate sought to release him. But the Jews cried out, saying: If you release this man, you are not Caesar’s friend. For whoever makes himself a king speaks against Caesar.
first_reading.reason: "exinde quærebat" = from then on he sought (narrative past); "from now on" misplaces the time reference.

second_reading.note: 'exinde quærebat' is narrative past, 'from then on he sought'; 'from now on' misplaces the time.

corrections.proposed_english: And from then on Pilate sought to release him. But the Jews cried out, saying: If you release this man, you are not Caesar’s friend. For whoever makes himself a king speaks against Caesar.

corrections.latin: Postea sciens Jesus quia omnia consummata sunt, ut consummaretur Scriptura, dixit: Sitio.
corrections.english: Afterwards, Jesus knowing that all things were now accomplished, that the scripture might be fulfilled, said: I thirst.

first_reading.proposed: Afterwards, Jesus knowing that all things were accomplished, that the scripture might be fulfilled, said: I thirst.
first_reading.reason: "quia omnia consummata sunt" has no "jam"; the English adds "now" (as in the Greek).

second_reading.note: The card reads 'quia omnia consummata sunt' with no 'jam'; 'now' is an added word matching the Greek.

corrections.proposed_english: Afterwards, Jesus knowing that all things were accomplished, that the scripture might be fulfilled, said: I thirst.

corrections.latin: Tunc ergo introivit et ille discipulus qui venerat primus ad monumentum: et vidit, et credidit:
corrections.english: Then the other disciple, who had come first to the tomb, also entered; and he saw and believed.

first_reading.proposed: Then that disciple, who had come first to the tomb, also entered; and he saw and believed.
first_reading.reason: "et ille discipulus" = that disciple also; "the other disciple" follows the Greek wording, not this Latin.

second_reading.note: 'et ille discipulus qui venerat primus' is 'that disciple also'; 'the other' follows the Greek, not 'ille'.

corrections.proposed_english: Then that disciple, who had come first to the tomb, also entered; and he saw and believed.

corrections.latin: Dixit autem eis: Non est vestrum nosse tempora vel momenta quæ Pater posuit in sua potestate:
corrections.english: He said to them, “It is not for you to know the times or seasons that the Father has set by his own authority.

first_reading.proposed: He said to them, “It is not for you to know the times or moments that the Father has set by his own authority.
first_reading.reason: "tempora vel momenta" = times or moments; "seasons" is the Greek/KJV wording, not the Latin "momenta".

second_reading.note: 'tempora vel momenta': 'momenta' is 'moments', not 'seasons', which is the Greek/KJV wording.

corrections.proposed_english: He said to them, “It is not for you to know the times or moments that the Father has set by his own authority.

corrections.latin: Et cum introissent in cœnaculum, ascenderunt ubi manebant Petrus, et Joannes, Jacobus, et Andreas, Philippus, et Thomas, Bartholomæus, et Matthæus, Jacobus Alphæi, et Simon Zelotes, et Judas Jacobi.
corrections.english: And when they had come in, they went up into an upper room, where abode Peter and John, James and Andrew, Philip and Thomas, Bartholomew and Matthew, James of Alphaeus and Simon Zelotes and Jude the brother of James.

first_reading.proposed: And when they had come into the upper room, they went up where abode Peter and John, James and Andrew, Philip and Thomas, Bartholomew and Matthew, James of Alphaeus and Simon Zelotes and Jude of James.
first_reading.reason: "cum introissent in cœnaculum, ascenderunt ubi manebant": the upper room goes with "entered", not "went up" (Greek order). "Judas Jacobi" = Jude of James; "the brother" is added.

second_reading.note: 'cum introissent in cœnaculum, ascenderunt ubi manebant' ties the upper room to entering; 'Judas Jacobi' is a bare genitive like 'Jacobus Alphæi'.

corrections.proposed_english: And when they had come into the upper room, they went up where abode Peter and John, James and Andrew, Philip and Thomas, Bartholomew and Matthew, James of Alphaeus and Simon Zelotes and Jude of James.

corrections.latin: Et hic quidem possedit agrum de mercede iniquitatis, et suspensus crepuit medius: et diffusa sunt omnia viscera ejus.
corrections.english: And he indeed has possessed a field of the reward of iniquity, and being hung, burst asunder in the midst: and all his heart gushed out.

first_reading.proposed: And he indeed has possessed a field of the reward of iniquity, and being hung, burst asunder in the midst: and all his bowels gushed out.
first_reading.reason: "diffusa sunt omnia viscera ejus": viscera = bowels, entrails; "heart" is a mistranslation.

second_reading.note: 'diffusa sunt omnia viscera ejus': 'viscera' is bowels or entrails, not 'heart'.

corrections.proposed_english: And he indeed has possessed a field of the reward of iniquity, and being hung, burst asunder in the midst: and all his bowels gushed out.

corrections.latin: hunc, definito consilio et præscientia Dei traditum, per manus iniquorum affligentes interemistis:
corrections.english: This same being delivered up, by the determinate counsel and foreknowledge of God, you by the hands of wicked men have crucified and slain.

first_reading.proposed: This same being delivered up, by the determinate counsel and foreknowledge of God, you by the hands of wicked men have afflicted and slain.
first_reading.reason: Latin has "affligentes interemistis" (afflicting, you slew); "crucified" renders the other reading "affigentes" / the Greek.

second_reading.note: The card reads 'affligentes interemistis' (afflicting, you slew); 'crucified' renders the other reading 'affigentes' and the Greek.

corrections.proposed_english: This same being delivered up, by the determinate counsel and foreknowledge of God, you by the hands of wicked men have afflicted and slain.

corrections.latin: David enim dicit in eum: Providebam Dominum in conspectu meo semper: quoniam a dextris est mihi, ne commovear:
corrections.english: For David says concerning him: I foresaw the Lord before my face: because he is at my right hand, that I may not be moved.

first_reading.proposed: For David says concerning him: I foresaw the Lord before my face always: because he is at my right hand, that I may not be moved.
first_reading.reason: "in conspectu meo semper": "semper" (always) is not rendered.

second_reading.note: 'in conspectu meo semper': 'semper' (always) is left untranslated.

corrections.proposed_english: For David says concerning him: I foresaw the Lord before my face always: because he is at my right hand, that I may not be moved.

corrections.latin: Et in fide nominis ejus, hunc quem vos vidistis et nostis, confirmavit nomen ejus: et fides, quæ per eum est, dedit integram sanitatem istam in conspectu omnium vestrum.
corrections.english: And in the faith of his name, this man, whom you have seen and known, has his name strengthened. And the faith which is by him has given this perfect soundness in the sight of you all.

first_reading.proposed: And in the faith of his name, his name has strengthened this man, whom you have seen and known. And the faith which is by him has given this perfect soundness in the sight of you all.
first_reading.reason: "hunc ... confirmavit nomen ejus" = his name has strengthened this man; "this man ... has his name strengthened" reads as if the man's name were strengthened.

second_reading.note: 'hunc ... confirmavit nomen ejus': 'nomen' is subject, 'hunc' object; the current English makes the man's name the thing strengthened.

corrections.proposed_english: And in the faith of his name, his name has strengthened this man, whom you have seen and known. And the faith which is by him has given this perfect soundness in the sight of you all.

corrections.latin: et Annas princeps sacerdotum, et Caiphas, et Joannes, et Alexander, et quotquot erant de genere sacerdotali.
corrections.english: And Annas the high priest and Caiaphas and John and Alexander: and as many as were of the kindred of the high priest.

first_reading.proposed: And Annas the high priest and Caiaphas and John and Alexander: and as many as were of the priestly kindred.
first_reading.reason: "de genere sacerdotali" = of the priestly kindred; "of the high priest" follows the Greek, not this Latin.

second_reading.note: 'de genere sacerdotali' is 'of the priestly kindred'; 'of the high priest' follows the Greek adjective.

corrections.proposed_english: And Annas the high priest and Caiaphas and John and Alexander: and as many as were of the priestly kindred.

corrections.latin: At illi comminantes dimiserunt eos, non invenientes quomodo punirent eos propter populum: quia omnes clarificabant id quod factum fuerat in eo quod acciderat.
corrections.english: But they, threatening, sent them away, not finding how they might punish them, because of the people: for all men glorified what had been done, in that which had happen.

first_reading.proposed: But they, threatening, sent them away, not finding how they might punish them, because of the people: for all men glorified what had been done, in that which had happened.
first_reading.reason: "had happen" is a grammatical slip for "had happened" ("quod acciderat").

second_reading.note: 'quod acciderat' is 'had happened'; 'had happen' is a grammatical slip.

corrections.proposed_english: But they, threatening, sent them away, not finding how they might punish them, because of the people: for all men glorified what had been done, in that which had happened.

corrections.latin: Confestim cecidit ante pedes ejus, et expiravit. Intrantes autem juvenes invenerunt illam mortuam: et extulerunt, et sepelierunt ad virum suum.
corrections.english: Immediately, she fell down before his feet and breathed his last. And the young men coming in found her dead: and carried her out and buried her by her husband.

first_reading.proposed: Immediately, she fell down before his feet and breathed her last. And the young men coming in found her dead: and carried her out and buried her by her husband.
first_reading.reason: "cecidit ... et expiravit": the subject is Saphira; "breathed his last" is a slip for "her last".

second_reading.note: 'cecidit ... et expiravit' has the woman as subject ('invenerunt illam mortuam'); 'his last' is a slip for 'her last'.

corrections.proposed_english: Immediately, she fell down before his feet and breathed her last. And the young men coming in found her dead: and carried her out and buried her by her husband.

corrections.latin: Et nunc itaque dico vobis, discedite ab hominibus istis, et sinite illos: quoniam si est ex hominibus consilium hoc aut opus, dissolvetur:
corrections.english: And now, therefore, I say to you: Refrain from these men and let them alone. For if this council or this work be of men, it will come to nought:

first_reading.proposed: And now, therefore, I say to you: Refrain from these men and let them alone. For if this counsel or this work be of men, it will come to nought:
first_reading.reason: "consilium hoc aut opus" = this counsel (plan) or work; "council" (an assembly) is the wrong word/spelling in modern English.

second_reading.note: 'consilium hoc aut opus' is a plan, 'counsel'; 'council' is an assembly (Latin 'concilium').

corrections.proposed_english: And now, therefore, I say to you: Refrain from these men and let them alone. For if this counsel or this work be of men, it will come to nought:

corrections.latin: Locus autem Scripturæ quem legebat, erat hic: Tamquam ovis ad occisionem ductus est: et sicut agnus coram tondente se, sine voce, sic non aperuit os suum.
corrections.english: And the place of the scripture which he was reading was this: He was led as a sheep to the slaughter: and like a lamb without voice before his shearer, so opens he not his mouth.

first_reading.proposed: And the place of the scripture which he was reading was this: He was led as a sheep to the slaughter: and like a lamb without voice before his shearer, so opened he not his mouth.
first_reading.reason: "non aperuit os suum" is perfect (did not open); the present "opens" follows the Greek, not the Latin.

second_reading.note: 'non aperuit os suum' is perfect, matching 'ductus est'; the present 'opens' follows the Greek.

corrections.proposed_english: And the place of the scripture which he was reading was this: He was led as a sheep to the slaughter: and like a lamb without voice before his shearer, so opened he not his mouth.

corrections.latin: Et Dominus ad eum: Surge, et vade in vicum qui vocatur Rectus: et quære in domo Judæ Saulum nomine Tarsensem: ecce enim orat.
corrections.english: And the Lord said to him: Arise and go into the street that is called Narrow and seek in the house of Judas, one named Saul of Tarsus. For behold he prays.

first_reading.proposed: And the Lord said to him: Arise and go into the street that is called Straight and seek in the house of Judas, one named Saul of Tarsus. For behold he prays.
first_reading.reason: "vicum qui vocatur Rectus" = the street called Straight; "Narrow" is a wrong name (misreading of Douay "Strait").

second_reading.note: 'vicum qui vocatur Rectus' is the street called Straight; 'Narrow' misreads Douay 'Strait' and gives a wrong name.

corrections.proposed_english: And the Lord said to him: Arise and go into the street that is called Straight and seek in the house of Judas, one named Saul of Tarsus. For behold he prays.

corrections.latin: Ait autem Petrus: Absit Domine, quia numquam manducavi omne commune et immundum.
corrections.english: But Peter said: Far be it from me. For I never did eat anything that is common and unclean.

first_reading.proposed: But Peter said: Far be it from me, Lord. For I never did eat anything that is common and unclean.
first_reading.reason: "Absit Domine": the vocative "Domine" (Lord) is not rendered.

second_reading.note: 'Absit Domine': the vocative 'Domine' is left untranslated.

corrections.proposed_english: But Peter said: Far be it from me, Lord. For I never did eat anything that is common and unclean.

corrections.latin: Qui dixerunt: Cornelius centurio, vir justus et timens Deum, et testimonium habens ab universa gente Judæorum, responsum accepit ab angelo sancto accersire te in domum suam, et audire verba abs te.
corrections.english: Who said: Cornelius, a centurion, a just man and one that fears God, and having good testimony from all the nation of the Jews, received an answer of an holy angel, to send for you into his house And to hear words of you.

first_reading.proposed: Who said: Cornelius, a centurion, a just man and one that fears God, and having good testimony from all the nation of the Jews, received an answer of an holy angel, to send for you into his house and to hear words of you.
first_reading.reason: Stray capital mid-sentence: "into his house And to hear" should read "and to hear".

second_reading.note: 'in domum suam, et audire verba abs te' is one continuous clause; capital 'And' mid-sentence is a slip.

corrections.proposed_english: Who said: Cornelius, a centurion, a just man and one that fears God, and having good testimony from all the nation of the Jews, received an answer of an holy angel, to send for you into his house and to hear words of you.

corrections.latin: Et erat manus Domini cum eis: multusque numerus credentium conversus est ad Dominum.
corrections.english: And the hand of he Lord was with them: and a great number believing, were converted to the Lord.

first_reading.proposed: And the hand of the Lord was with them: and a great number believing, were converted to the Lord.
first_reading.reason: Misspelling: "the hand of he Lord" should read "the hand of the Lord" ("manus Domini").

second_reading.note: 'manus Domini' is 'the hand of the Lord'; 'he Lord' is a misspelling.

corrections.proposed_english: And the hand of the Lord was with them: and a great number believing, were converted to the Lord.

corrections.latin: Occidit autem Jacobum fratrem Joannis gladio.
corrections.english: And he killed James, the brother of John, With the sword.

first_reading.proposed: And he killed James, the brother of John, with the sword.
first_reading.reason: Stray capital mid-sentence: "With the sword" should read "with the sword".

second_reading.note: 'fratrem Joannis gladio' continues the sentence; capital 'With' is a slip.

corrections.proposed_english: And he killed James, the brother of John, with the sword.

corrections.latin: Ministrantibus autem illis Domino, et jejunantibus, dixit illis Spiritus Sanctus: Segregate mihi Saulum et Barnabam in opus ad quod assumpsi eos.
corrections.english: And as they were ministering to the Lord and fasting, the Holy Spirit said to them: Separate me Saul and Barnabas, for the work to what I have taken them.

first_reading.proposed: And as they were ministering to the Lord and fasting, the Holy Spirit said to them: Separate me Saul and Barnabas, for the work to which I have taken them.
first_reading.reason: "in opus ad quod assumpsi eos" = the work to which I have taken them; "to what" is a grammatical slip for the relative.

second_reading.note: 'in opus ad quod assumpsi eos' needs the relative 'to which'; 'to what' is ungrammatical.

corrections.proposed_english: And as they were ministering to the Lord and fasting, the Holy Spirit said to them: Separate me Saul and Barnabas, for the work to which I have taken them.

corrections.latin: Audientes autem gentes, gavisæ sunt, et glorificabant verbum Domini: et crediderunt quotquot erant præordinati ad vitam æternam.
corrections.english: And the Gentiles hearing it were glad and glorified the word of the Lord: and as many as were ordained to life everlasting believed.

first_reading.proposed: And the Gentiles hearing it were glad and glorified the word of the Lord: and as many as were preordained to life everlasting believed.
first_reading.reason: "præordinati" = preordained; plain "ordained" follows the Greek/KJV wording and drops the Latin "præ-".

second_reading.note: 'præordinati' carries the distinctive Vulgate prefix 'præ-': 'preordained'; plain 'ordained' drops it.

corrections.proposed_english: And the Gentiles hearing it were glad and glorified the word of the Lord: and as many as were preordained to life everlasting believed.

corrections.latin: Et quidem non sine testimonio semetipsum reliquit benefaciens de cælo, dans pluvias et tempora fructifera, implens cibo et lætitia corda nostra.
corrections.english: Nevertheless he left not himself without testimony, doing good from heaven, giving rains and fruitful Seasons, filling our hearts with food and gladness.

first_reading.proposed: Nevertheless he left not himself without testimony, doing good from heaven, giving rains and fruitful seasons, filling our hearts with food and gladness.
first_reading.reason: Stray capital mid-sentence: "fruitful Seasons" should read "fruitful seasons".

second_reading.note: 'tempora fructifera' is an ordinary noun phrase; capital 'Seasons' is a slip.

corrections.proposed_english: Nevertheless he left not himself without testimony, doing good from heaven, giving rains and fruitful seasons, filling our hearts with food and gladness.

corrections.latin: Transeuntes autem Phrygiam et Galatiæ regionem, vetati sunt a Spiritu Sancto loqui verbum Dei in Asia.
corrections.english: And when they had passed through Phrygia and the country of Galatia, they were forbidden by the Holy Spirit to preach the word in Asia.

first_reading.proposed: And when they had passed through Phrygia and the country of Galatia, they were forbidden by the Holy Spirit to preach the word of God in Asia.
first_reading.reason: "loqui verbum Dei in Asia": "Dei" (of God) is not rendered; "the word" alone follows the Greek.

second_reading.note: 'loqui verbum Dei in Asia': 'Dei' is left untranslated.

corrections.proposed_english: And when they had passed through Phrygia and the country of Galatia, they were forbidden by the Holy Spirit to preach the word of God in Asia.

corrections.latin: quærere Deum si forte attrectent eum, aut inveniant, quamvis non longe sit ab unoquoque nostrum.
corrections.english: That they should seek God, if perhaps they may feel after him or find him, although he do not be far from each of us.

first_reading.proposed: That they should seek God, if perhaps they may feel after him or find him, although he be not far from each of us.
first_reading.reason: "quamvis non longe sit" = although he be not far; "he do not be far" is a grammatical slip.

second_reading.note: 'quamvis non longe sit' is 'although he be not far'; 'he do not be far' is ungrammatical.

corrections.proposed_english: That they should seek God, if perhaps they may feel after him or find him, although he be not far from each of us.

corrections.latin: Genus ergo cum simus Dei, non debemus æstimare auro, aut argento, aut lapidi, sculpturæ artis, et cogitationis hominis, divinum esse simile.
corrections.english: Being therefore the offspring of God, we must not suppose the divinity to be like to gold or silver or stone, the graving of are and device of man.

first_reading.proposed: Being therefore the offspring of God, we must not suppose the divinity to be like to gold or silver or stone, the graving of art and device of man.
first_reading.reason: Misspelling: "the graving of are" should read "of art" ("sculpturæ artis").

second_reading.note: 'sculpturæ artis' is 'the graving of art'; 'of are' is a misspelling.

corrections.proposed_english: Being therefore the offspring of God, we must not suppose the divinity to be like to gold or silver or stone, the graving of art and device of man.

corrections.latin: Contradicentibus autem eis, et blasphemantibus, excutiens vestimenta sua, dixit ad eos: Sanguis vester super caput vestrum: mundus ego: ex hoc ad gentes vadam.
corrections.english: But they opposition and blaspheming, he shook his garments and said to them: Your blood be upon your own heads: I am clean. From now on I will go to the Gentiles.

first_reading.proposed: But they opposing and blaspheming, he shook his garments and said to them: Your blood be upon your own heads: I am clean. From now on I will go to the Gentiles.
first_reading.reason: "Contradicentibus autem eis" = as they opposed; "But they opposition and blaspheming" is a broken phrase (noun for participle).

second_reading.note: 'Contradicentibus autem eis, et blasphemantibus' needs a participle, 'opposing'; 'they opposition' is broken English.

corrections.proposed_english: But they opposing and blaspheming, he shook his garments and said to them: Your blood be upon your own heads: I am clean. From now on I will go to the Gentiles.

corrections.latin: Et descendens Cæsaream, ascendit, et salutavit ecclesiam, et descendit Antiochiam.
corrections.english: And going down to Cæsarea, he went up to Jerusalem and greeted the church: and so came down to Antioch.

first_reading.proposed: And going down to Cæsarea, he went up and greeted the church: and so came down to Antioch.
first_reading.reason: "ascendit, et salutavit ecclesiam": the Latin names no destination; "to Jerusalem" is an interpretive addition.

second_reading.note: 'ascendit, et salutavit ecclesiam' names no destination; 'to Jerusalem' is an interpretive addition.

corrections.proposed_english: And going down to Cæsarea, he went up and greeted the church: and so came down to Antioch.

corrections.latin: Erant autem quidam Judæi, Scevæ principis sacerdotum septem filii, qui hoc faciebant.
corrections.english: And there were certain men, seven sons of Sceva, a Jew, a chief priest, that did this.

first_reading.proposed: And there were certain Jews, seven sons of Sceva, a chief priest, that did this.
first_reading.reason: "quidam Judæi, Scevæ principis sacerdotum septem filii": Judæi is nominative plural (certain Jews, the sons); "Sceva, a Jew" follows the Greek genitive.

second_reading.note: 'quidam Judæi, Scevæ principis sacerdotum septem filii': 'Judæi' is nominative plural with 'quidam', not a genitive describing Sceva.

corrections.proposed_english: And there were certain Jews, seven sons of Sceva, a chief priest, that did this.

corrections.latin: Hoc autem notum factum est omnibus Judæis, atque gentilibus qui habitabant Ephesi: et cecidit timor super omnes illos, et magnificabatur nomen Domini Jesu.
corrections.english: And this became known to all the Jews and the Gentiles that dwelt a Ephesus. And fear fell on them all: and the name of the Lord Jesus was magnified.

first_reading.proposed: And this became known to all the Jews and the Gentiles that dwelt at Ephesus. And fear fell on them all: and the name of the Lord Jesus was magnified.
first_reading.reason: Misspelling: "dwelt a Ephesus" should read "dwelt at Ephesus" ("habitabant Ephesi").

second_reading.note: 'qui habitabant Ephesi' is 'that dwelt at Ephesus'; 'a Ephesus' is a misspelling.

corrections.proposed_english: And this became known to all the Jews and the Gentiles that dwelt at Ephesus. And fear fell on them all: and the name of the Lord Jesus was magnified.

corrections.latin: Non enim subterfugi, quominus annuntiarem omne consilium Dei vobis.
corrections.english: For I have not spared to declare to you all, the counsel of God.

first_reading.proposed: For I have not spared to declare to you all the counsel of God.
first_reading.reason: "omne consilium Dei vobis": omne modifies consilium (the whole counsel of God); the comma in "to you all, the counsel" attaches "all" to "you".

second_reading.note: 'omne consilium Dei vobis': 'omne' modifies 'consilium'; the comma after 'you all' attaches it to 'vobis'.

corrections.proposed_english: For I have not spared to declare to you all the counsel of God.

corrections.latin: De his autem qui crediderunt ex gentibus, nos scripsimus judicantes ut abstineant se ab idolis immolato, et sanguine, et suffocato, et fornicatione.
corrections.english: But, as touching the Gentiles that believe, we have written, decreeing that they should only refrain themselves from that which has been offered to idols and from blood and from things strangled and from sexual immorality.

first_reading.proposed: But, as touching the Gentiles that believe, we have written, decreeing that they should refrain themselves from that which has been offered to idols and from blood and from things strangled and from sexual immorality.
first_reading.reason: "only" is added; the Latin has simply "ut abstineant se ab idolis immolato" (that they abstain), with no "tantum" or "solum".

second_reading.note: 'judicantes ut abstineant se' has no 'tantum' or 'solum'; 'only' is added.

corrections.proposed_english: But, as touching the Gentiles that believe, we have written, decreeing that they should refrain themselves from that which has been offered to idols and from blood and from things strangled and from sexual immorality.

corrections.latin: Viderant enim Trophimum Ephesium in civitate cum ipso, quem æstimaverunt quoniam in templum introduxisset Paulus.
corrections.english: (For they had seen Trophimus the Ephesian in the city with him. whom they supposed that Paul had brought into the temple.)

first_reading.proposed: (For they had seen Trophimus the Ephesian in the city with him, whom they supposed that Paul had brought into the temple.)
first_reading.reason: Stray full stop before lower-case "whom" breaks the sentence ("cum ipso, quem æstimaverunt"); should be a comma.

second_reading.note: 'cum ipso, quem æstimaverunt' is one sentence; the full stop before lower-case 'whom' breaks it.

corrections.proposed_english: (For they had seen Trophimus the Ephesian in the city with him, whom they supposed that Paul had brought into the temple.)

corrections.latin: Ille autem dixit: Judæis convenit rogare te ut crastina die producas Paulum in concilium, quasi aliquid certius inquisituri sint de illo:
corrections.english: And he said: The Jews have agreed to desire you that you would bring forth Paul to-next day into the council, as if they meant to inquire some thing more certain touching him.

first_reading.proposed: And he said: The Jews have agreed to desire you that you would bring forth Paul tomorrow into the council, as if they meant to inquire some thing more certain touching him.
first_reading.reason: "to-next day" is a garbled modernisation of "to-morrow" for "crastina die" (tomorrow).

second_reading.note: 'crastina die' is 'tomorrow'; 'to-next day' is a garbled form.

corrections.proposed_english: And he said: The Jews have agreed to desire you that you would bring forth Paul tomorrow into the council, as if they meant to inquire some thing more certain touching him.

corrections.latin: simul et sperans quod pecunia ei daretur a Paulo, propter quod et frequenter accersens eum, loquebatur cum eo.
corrections.english: Hoping also also that money should be given him by Paul: for which cause also oftentimes sending for him, he spoke with him.

first_reading.proposed: Hoping also that money should be given him by Paul: for which cause also oftentimes sending for him, he spoke with him.
first_reading.reason: Doubled word "also also" for "simul et sperans".

second_reading.note: 'simul et sperans': the doubled 'also' replaced Douay 'withal' for 'simul'; keep 'et' as 'also' and render 'simul'.

corrections.proposed_english: Hoping also at the same time that money should be given him by Paul: for which cause also oftentimes sending for him, he spoke with him.

corrections.latin: Qui cum perductus esset, circumsteterunt eum, qui ab Jerosolyma descenderant Judæi, multas et graves causas objicientes, quas non poterant probare:
corrections.english: Who being brought, the Jews stood about him, who had come down from Jerusalem, objecting many and grievious causes, which they could not prove:

first_reading.proposed: Who being brought, the Jews stood about him, who had come down from Jerusalem, objecting many and grievous causes, which they could not prove:
first_reading.reason: Misspelling "grievious" for "grievous" ("graves causas").

second_reading.note: 'multas et graves causas': 'grievious' is a misspelling of 'grievous'.

corrections.proposed_english: Who being brought, the Jews stood about him, who had come down from Jerusalem, objecting many and grievous causes, which they could not prove:

corrections.latin: De quo, cum stetissent accusatores, nullam causam deferebant, de quibus ego suspicabar malum.
corrections.english: Against whom, when the accusers stood up, they brought no accusation of this which I thought ill of:

first_reading.proposed: Against whom, when the accusers stood up, they brought no accusation of things which I thought ill of:
first_reading.reason: "de quibus ego suspicabar malum" is plural (of the things of which I suspected evil); "of this which" is singular and leaves the sentence awkward.

second_reading.note: 'de quibus ego suspicabar malum' is plural, 'of things'; 'of this which' is singular.

corrections.proposed_english: Against whom, when the accusers stood up, they brought no accusation of things which I thought ill of:

corrections.latin: Agrippa autem dixit ad Festum: Volebam et ipse hominem audire. Cras, inquit, audies eum.
corrections.english: And Agrippa said to Festus: I would also hear the man, myself. To-next day, said he, you shall hear him.

first_reading.proposed: And Agrippa said to Festus: I would also hear the man, myself. Tomorrow, said he, you shall hear him.
first_reading.reason: "To-next day" is a garbled modernisation of "To-morrow" for "Cras" (tomorrow).

second_reading.note: 'Cras' is 'Tomorrow'; 'To-next day' is a garbled form.

corrections.proposed_english: And Agrippa said to Festus: I would also hear the man, myself. Tomorrow, said he, you shall hear him.

corrections.latin: Et nunc, in spe quæ ad patres nostros repromissionis facta est a Deo, sto judicio subjectus:
corrections.english: And now for the hope of the promise that was made by God to the fathers, do I stand subject to judgment:

first_reading.proposed: And now for the hope of the promise that was made by God to our fathers, do I stand subject to judgment:
first_reading.reason: "ad patres nostros" is "to our fathers"; the English drops "nostros".

second_reading.note: 'ad patres nostros': 'nostros' (our) is left untranslated.

corrections.proposed_english: And now for the hope of the promise that was made by God to our fathers, do I stand subject to judgment:

corrections.latin: Quid incredibile judicatur apud vos, si Deus mortuos suscitat?
corrections.english: Why should it be thought a thing incredible that God should raise the dead?

first_reading.proposed: Why should it be thought a thing incredible among you that God should raise the dead?
first_reading.reason: "apud vos" (among you, in your judgment) is left untranslated.

second_reading.note: 'judicatur apud vos': 'apud vos' (among you) is left untranslated.

corrections.proposed_english: Why should it be thought a thing incredible among you that God should raise the dead?

corrections.latin: In quibus dum irem Damascum cum potestate et permissu principum sacerdotum,
corrections.english: Whereupon, when I was going to Damascus with authority and permission of the chief priest,

first_reading.proposed: Whereupon, when I was going to Damascus with authority and permission of the chief priests,
first_reading.reason: "principum sacerdotum" is genitive plural, the chief priests (as in 26:10); the English has the singular "chief priest".

second_reading.note: 'principum sacerdotum' is genitive plural, 'of the chief priests'; the English has the singular.

corrections.proposed_english: Whereupon, when I was going to Damascus with authority and permission of the chief priests,

corrections.latin: Secundum autem duritiam tuam, et impœnitens cor, thesaurizas tibi iram in die iræ, et revelationis justi judicii Dei,
corrections.english: But according to your hardness and impenitent heart, you store up up to yourself wrath, against the day of wrath and revelation of the just judgment of God:

first_reading.proposed: But according to your hardness and impenitent heart, you store up to yourself wrath, against the day of wrath and revelation of the just judgment of God:
first_reading.reason: Doubled word "up up" in the rendering of "thesaurizas tibi iram".

second_reading.note: 'thesaurizas tibi iram': 'up up' is a doubled word.

corrections.proposed_english: But according to your hardness and impenitent heart, you store up to yourself wrath, against the day of wrath and revelation of the just judgment of God:

corrections.latin: Si igitur præputium justitias legis custodiat, nonne præputium illius in circumcisionem reputabitur?
corrections.english: If then, the uncircumcised keep the justices of the law, shall not this uncircumcision be counted for circumcision?

first_reading.proposed: If then, the uncircumcised keep the justices of the law, shall not his uncircumcision be counted for circumcision?
first_reading.reason: "præputium illius" is "his uncircumcision" (genitive of ille); "this uncircumcision" loses the possessive.

second_reading.note: 'præputium illius' has the genitive of 'ille', 'his uncircumcision'; 'this' loses the possessive.

corrections.proposed_english: If then, the uncircumcised keep the justices of the law, shall not his uncircumcision be counted for circumcision?

corrections.latin: (sicut scriptum est: Quia patrem multarum gentium posui te) ante Deum, cui credidit, qui vivificat mortuos, et vocat ea quæ non sunt, tamquam ea quæ sunt:
corrections.english: (As it is written: I have made you a father of many nations), before God, whom he believed: who gives life the dead and calls those things that are not, as those that are.

first_reading.proposed: (As it is written: I have made you a father of many nations), before God, whom he believed: who gives life to the dead and calls those things that are not, as those that are.
first_reading.reason: Missing word: "who gives life the dead" for "qui vivificat mortuos" needs "to".

second_reading.note: 'qui vivificat mortuos': 'gives life the dead' is missing 'to'.

corrections.proposed_english: (As it is written: I have made you a father of many nations), before God, whom he believed: who gives life to the dead and calls those things that are not, as those that are.

corrections.latin: Liberati autem a peccato, servi facti estis justitiæ.
corrections.english: Being then freed from sin, we have been made servants of justice.

first_reading.proposed: Being then freed from sin, you have been made servants of justice.
first_reading.reason: "servi facti estis justitiæ" is second person plural (you have been made); the English has "we have been made", changing who is addressed.

second_reading.note: 'servi facti estis' is second person plural, 'you have been made'; 'we' changes who is addressed.

corrections.proposed_english: Being then freed from sin, you have been made servants of justice.

corrections.latin: Ipse enim Spiritus testimonium reddit spiritui nostro quod sumus filii Dei.
corrections.english: The Spirit himself bears witness with our spirit that we are children of God.

first_reading.proposed: The Spirit himself bears witness to our spirit that we are children of God.
first_reading.reason: "testimonium reddit spiritui nostro" is dative, gives testimony to our spirit; "with our spirit" follows the Greek compound verb, not the Latin.

second_reading.note: 'testimonium reddit spiritui nostro' has the dative, 'to our spirit'; 'with' follows the Greek compound verb.

corrections.proposed_english: The Spirit himself bears witness to our spirit that we are children of God.

corrections.latin: Sed quid dicit Scriptura? Prope est verbum in ore tuo, et in corde tuo: hoc est verbum fidei, quod prædicamus.
corrections.english: But what says the scripture? The word is near you; even in your mouth and in your heart. This is the word of faith, which we preach.

first_reading.proposed: But what says the scripture? The word is near; in your mouth and in your heart. This is the word of faith, which we preach.
first_reading.reason: "Prope est verbum in ore tuo, et in corde tuo" has no "te"; "near you; even" follows the Greek/Douay wording, adding a pronoun the Latin lacks.

second_reading.note: 'Prope est verbum in ore tuo' has no 'te' or 'even'; the proposal is right but its semicolon leaves a fragment, so use a comma.

corrections.proposed_english: But what says the scripture? The word is near, in your mouth and in your heart. This is the word of faith, which we preach.

corrections.latin: Nox præcessit, dies autem appropinquavit. Abjiciamus ergo opera tenebrarum, et induamur arma lucis.
corrections.english: The night is passed And the day is near. Let us, therefore cast off the works of darkness and put on the armour of light.

first_reading.proposed: The night is passed and the day is near. Let us, therefore cast off the works of darkness and put on the armour of light.
first_reading.reason: Stray capital mid-sentence: "is passed And the day" ("Nox præcessit, dies autem appropinquavit").

second_reading.note: 'Nox præcessit, dies autem appropinquavit' is one sentence; capital 'And' is a slip.

corrections.proposed_english: The night is passed and the day is near. Let us, therefore cast off the works of darkness and put on the armour of light.

corrections.latin: Deus autem pacis sit cum omnibus vobis. Amen.
corrections.english: Now the God of peace be with, you all. Amen.

first_reading.proposed: Now the God of peace be with you all. Amen.
first_reading.reason: Stray comma splitting "with, you all" ("sit cum omnibus vobis").

second_reading.note: 'sit cum omnibus vobis' is 'be with you all'; the comma after 'with' is stray.

corrections.proposed_english: Now the God of peace be with you all. Amen.

corrections.latin: Salutate eos qui sunt ex Aristoboli domo. Salutate Herodionem cognatum meum. Salutate eos qui sunt ex Narcisi domo, qui sunt in Domino.
corrections.english: Greet them that are of Aristobulus’ household. Greet Herodian, my kinsman. Greet them that are of Narcissus’ household, who are in the Lord.

first_reading.proposed: Greet them that are of Aristobulus’ household. Greet Herodion, my kinsman. Greet them that are of Narcissus’ household, who are in the Lord.
first_reading.reason: Name misspelt: "Herodionem" is the accusative of Herodion; "Herodian" is not the name (same person, wrong spelling).

second_reading.note: 'Herodionem' is the accusative of Herodion; 'Herodian' is an old misspelling, not a modern name form.

corrections.proposed_english: Greet them that are of Aristobulus’ household. Greet Herodion, my kinsman. Greet them that are of Narcissus’ household, who are in the Lord.

corrections.latin: Ad verecundiam vestram dico. Sic non est inter vos sapiens quisquam, qui possit judicare inter fratrem suum?
corrections.english: I speak to your shame. Is it so that there is not among you anyone wise man that is able to judge between his brothers?

first_reading.proposed: I speak to your shame. Is it so that there is not among you any one wise man that is able to judge between his brothers?
first_reading.reason: "anyone wise man" is ungrammatical; "sapiens quisquam" is "any one wise man".

second_reading.note: 'sapiens quisquam' is 'any one wise man'; 'anyone wise man' is ungrammatical.

corrections.proposed_english: I speak to your shame. Is it so that there is not among you any one wise man that is able to judge between his brothers?

corrections.latin: Nescitis quoniam corpora vestra membra sunt Christi? Tollens ergo membra Christi, faciam membra meretricis? Absit.
corrections.english: Do you not know that your bodies are the members of Christ? Shall I then take the members of Christ and make them the members of an prostitute? God forbid!

first_reading.proposed: Do you not know that your bodies are the members of Christ? Shall I then take the members of Christ and make them the members of a prostitute? God forbid!
first_reading.reason: Wrong article: "an prostitute" ("membra meretricis") should be "a prostitute".

second_reading.note: 'membra meretricis': 'an prostitute' has the wrong article.

corrections.proposed_english: Do you not know that your bodies are the members of Christ? Shall I then take the members of Christ and make them the members of a prostitute? God forbid!

corrections.latin: Volo enim omnes vos esse sicut meipsum: sed unusquisque proprium donum habet ex Deo: alius quidem sic, alius vero sic.
corrections.english: For I would that all men were even as myself. But everyone has his proper gift from God: one after this manner, and another after that.

first_reading.proposed: For I would that all of you were even as myself. But everyone has his proper gift from God: one after this manner, and another after that.
first_reading.reason: "Volo enim omnes vos esse" is "all of you"; "all men" follows the Greek reading (all men), not the Latin "vos".

second_reading.note: 'Volo enim omnes vos esse' is 'all of you'; 'all men' is the Greek reading, not the Latin 'vos'.

corrections.proposed_english: For I would that all of you were even as myself. But everyone has his proper gift from God: one after this manner, and another after that.

corrections.latin: Porro hoc ad utilitatem vestram dico: non ut laqueum vobis injiciam, sed ad id, quod honestum est, et quod facultatem præbeat sine impedimento Dominum obsecrandi.
corrections.english: And this I speak for your profit, not to cast a snare upon you, but for that which is decent and which may give you power to attend upon the Lord, without impediment.

first_reading.proposed: And this I speak for your profit, not to cast a snare upon you, but for that which is decent and which may give you power to entreat the Lord, without impediment.
first_reading.reason: "Dominum obsecrandi" means of beseeching, praying to the Lord; "attend upon the Lord" does not render "obsecrare".

second_reading.note: 'Dominum obsecrandi' is 'of beseeching the Lord'; 'attend upon' renders the Greek, not 'obsecrare'.

corrections.proposed_english: And this I speak for your profit, not to cast a snare upon you, but for that which is decent and which may give you power to entreat the Lord, without impediment.

corrections.latin: Et si aliis non sum Apostolus, sed tamen vobis sum: nam signaculum apostolatus mei vos estis in Domino.
corrections.english: And if to others I do not be an apostle, but yet to you I am. For you are the seal of my apostleship in the Lord.

first_reading.reason: "I do not be an apostle" is ungrammatical (garbled modernisation of "I be not") for "non sum Apostolus".

second_reading.note: "non sum Apostolus" = I am not an apostle; "I do not be" is broken English.

corrections.proposed_english: And if to others I am not an apostle, but yet to you I am. For you are the seal of my apostleship in the Lord.

corrections.latin: Numquid secundum hominem hæc dico? an et lex hæc non dicit?
corrections.english: Speak I these things according to man? Or does not the law also say; these things?

first_reading.proposed: Speak I these things according to man? Or does not the law also say these things?

second_reading.note: "lex hæc non dicit" is one clause; the semicolon after "say" wrongly splits verb from object.

corrections.proposed_english: Speak I these things according to man? Or does not the law also say these things?

corrections.latin: Sine offensione estote Judæis, et gentibus, et ecclesiæ Dei:

first_reading.reason: "Judæis" is plural, to the Jews, parallel with "gentibus"; the English has the singular "the Jew".

second_reading.note: "Judæis" is plural, parallel with "gentibus"; the singular "the Jew" does not match the Latin number.

corrections.proposed_english: Be without offence to the Jews, and to the Gentiles and to the church of God:

corrections.latin: Quotiescumque enim manducabitis panem hunc, et calicem bibetis, mortem Domini annuntiabitis donec veniat.

first_reading.proposed: For whenever you eat this bread and drink the cup, you will proclaim the Lord’s death until he comes.

second_reading.note: "annuntiabitis" is future; the present "you proclaim" follows the Greek, not this Latin.

corrections.proposed_english: For whenever you eat this bread and drink the cup, you will proclaim the Lord’s death until he comes.

corrections.latin: Videmus nunc per speculum in ænigmate: tunc autem facie ad faciem. Nunc cognosco ex parte: tunc autem cognoscam sicut et cognitus sum.
corrections.english: For now we see through a mirror, in a riddle, but then face to face. Now I know in part, but then I shall know just as I have been known.

first_reading.proposed: Now we see through a mirror, in a riddle, but then face to face. Now I know in part, but then I shall know just as I have been known.
first_reading.reason: 'For' is added from the Greek/KJV (gar); the Latin begins simply 'Videmus nunc' with no 'enim'.

second_reading.note: "Videmus nunc" has no "enim"; the opening "For" is added from the Greek.

corrections.proposed_english: Now we see through a mirror, in a riddle, but then face to face. Now I know in part, but then I shall know just as I have been known.

corrections.latin: Qui loquitur lingua, semetipsum ædificat: qui autem prophetat, ecclesiam Dei ædificat.
corrections.english: He that speaks in a tongue builds up himself: but he that prophesies, builds up the church.

first_reading.proposed: He that speaks in a tongue builds up himself: but he that prophesies, builds up the church of God.
first_reading.reason: 'ecclesiam Dei ædificat' = builds up the church of God; 'Dei' is left untranslated.

second_reading.note: "ecclesiam Dei ædificat": "Dei" is left untranslated in the current English.

corrections.proposed_english: He that speaks in a tongue builds up himself: but he that prophesies, builds up the church of God.

corrections.latin: Si autem Christus non resurrexit, inanis est ergo prædicatio nostra, inanis est et fides vestra:
corrections.english: And if Christ do not be risen again, then is our preaching vain: and your faith is also vain.

first_reading.proposed: And if Christ is not risen again, then is our preaching vain: and your faith is also vain.
first_reading.reason: 'do not be risen' is broken English (faulty modernisation of 'be not risen') for 'non resurrexit'.

second_reading.note: "non resurrexit"; "do not be risen" is broken English.

corrections.proposed_english: And if Christ is not risen again, then is our preaching vain: and your faith is also vain.

corrections.latin: Quod si Christus non resurrexit, vana est fides vestra: adhuc enim estis in peccatis vestris.
corrections.english: And if Christ do not be risen again, your faith is vain: for you are yet in your sins.

first_reading.proposed: And if Christ is not risen again, your faith is vain: for you are yet in your sins.
first_reading.reason: 'do not be risen' is broken English (faulty modernisation of 'be not risen') for 'non resurrexit'.

second_reading.note: "non resurrexit"; "do not be risen" is broken English.

corrections.proposed_english: And if Christ is not risen again, your faith is vain: for you are yet in your sins.

corrections.latin: Si secundum hominem ad bestias pugnavi Ephesi, quid mihi prodest, si mortui non resurgunt? Manducemus, et bibamus, cras enim moriemur.
corrections.english: If (according to man) I fought with beasts at Ephesus, what does it profit me, if the dead rise not again? Let us eat and drink, for to next day we shall die.

first_reading.proposed: If (according to man) I fought with beasts at Ephesus, what does it profit me, if the dead rise not again? Let us eat and drink, for tomorrow we shall die.
first_reading.reason: 'for to next day we shall die' is a broken modernisation of 'to morrow'; 'cras enim moriemur' = for tomorrow we shall die.

second_reading.note: "cras enim moriemur" = for tomorrow we shall die; "to next day" is not English.

corrections.proposed_english: If (according to man) I fought with beasts at Ephesus, what does it profit me, if the dead rise not again? Let us eat and drink, for tomorrow we shall die.

corrections.latin: Per unam sabbati unusquisque vestrum apud se seponat, recondens quod ei bene placuerit: ut non, cum venero, tunc collectæ fiant.
corrections.english: On the first day of the week, let each of you put apart with himself, laying up what it shall well please him: that when I come, the collections do not be then to be made.

first_reading.proposed: On the first day of the week, let each of you put apart with himself, laying up what it shall well please him: that when I come, the collections be not then to be made.
first_reading.reason: 'the collections do not be then to be made' is broken English (faulty modernisation of 'be not then to be made') for 'ut non ... tunc collectæ fiant'.

second_reading.note: "ut non ... tunc collectæ fiant"; "do not be then to be made" is ungrammatical.

corrections.proposed_english: On the first day of the week, let each of you put apart with himself, laying up what it shall well please him: that when I come, the collections be not then to be made.

corrections.latin: Obsecro autem vos fratres, nostis domum Stephanæ, et Fortunati, et Achaici: quoniam sunt primitiæ Achaiæ, et in ministerium sanctorum ordinaverunt seipsos:
corrections.english: And I implore you, brothers, you know the house of Stephanus, and of Fortunatus, and of Achaicus, that they are the firstfruits of Achaia, and have dedicated themselves to the ministry of the saints:

first_reading.proposed: And I implore you, brothers, you know the house of Stephanas, and of Fortunatus, and of Achaicus, that they are the firstfruits of Achaia, and have dedicated themselves to the ministry of the saints:

corrections.proposed_english: And I implore you, brothers, you know the house of Stephanas, and of Fortunatus, and of Achaicus, that they are the firstfruits of Achaia, and have dedicated themselves to the ministry of the saints:

corrections.latin: Gaudeo autem in præsentia Stephanæ, et Fortunati, et Achaici: quoniam id, quod vobis deerat, ipsi suppleverunt:

first_reading.reason: 'Stephanæ' is the genitive of Stephanas; 'Stephanus' is a different name (Stephen).

second_reading.note: "Stephanæ" is genitive of Stephanas, the same man as 16:15; "Stephanus" is a different name form.

corrections.proposed_english: And I rejoice in the presence of Stephanas and Fortunatus and Achaicus: because that which was wanting on your part, they have supplied.

corrections.latin: ut non circumveniamur a Satana: non enim ignoramus cogitationes ejus.
corrections.english: That we do not be overreached by Satan. For we are not ignorant of his devices.

first_reading.proposed: That we be not overreached by Satan. For we are not ignorant of his devices.
first_reading.reason: 'That we do not be overreached' is broken English (faulty modernisation of 'be not overreached') for 'ut non circumveniamur'.

second_reading.note: "ut non circumveniamur"; "we do not be overreached" is ungrammatical.

corrections.proposed_english: That we be not overreached by Satan. For we are not ignorant of his devices.

corrections.latin: In omnibus tribulationem patimur, sed non angustiamur: aporiamur, sed non destituimur:
corrections.english: In all things we suffer tribulation: but are not distressed. We are constrained: but are not destitute.

first_reading.proposed: In all things we suffer tribulation: but are not distressed. We are perplexed: but are not destitute.
first_reading.reason: 'aporiamur' = we are perplexed, at a loss (DR 'straitened'); 'constrained' (forced, restricted) is not a sense of the verb.

second_reading.note: "aporiamur" = we are at a loss, perplexed; "constrained" (compelled, confined) is not a sense of the verb.

corrections.proposed_english: In all things we suffer tribulation: but are not distressed. We are perplexed: but are not destitute.

corrections.latin: Id enim, quod in præsenti est momentaneum et leve tribulationis nostræ, supra modum in sublimitate æternum gloriæ pondus operatur in nobis,
corrections.english: For that which is at present momentary and light of our tribulation works for us above measure, exceedingly an eternal weight of glory.

first_reading.reason: 'operatur in nobis' = works in us; 'for us' follows the Greek dative, not the Latin 'in nobis'.

second_reading.note: "operatur in nobis" = works in us; "for us" renders the Greek dative, not "in nobis".

corrections.proposed_english: For that which is at present momentary and light of our tribulation works in us above measure, exceedingly an eternal weight of glory.

corrections.latin: Si qua ergo in Christo nova creatura, vetera transierunt: ecce facta sunt omnia nova.
corrections.english: Therefore, if anyone is in Christ, there is a new creation. The old things have passed away; behold, all things have become new.

first_reading.proposed: Therefore, if there is any new creature in Christ, the old things have passed away; behold, all things have become new.

second_reading.note: "Si qua ... nova creatura": "qua" agrees with "creatura" inside the protasis; the apodosis is "vetera transierunt", not "there is a new creation".

corrections.proposed_english: Therefore, if there is any new creature in Christ, the old things have passed away; behold, all things have become new.

corrections.latin: Nemini dantes ullam offensionem, ut non vituperetur ministerium nostrum:

first_reading.proposed: Giving no offence to any man, that our ministry be not blamed.
first_reading.reason: 'that our ministry do not be blamed' is broken English (faulty modernisation of 'be not blamed') for 'ut non vituperetur'.

second_reading.note: "ut non vituperetur"; "do not be blamed" is ungrammatical.

corrections.proposed_english: Giving no offence to any man, that our ministry be not blamed.

corrections.latin: et viscera ejus abundantius in vobis sunt, reminiscentis omnium vestrum obedientiam: quomodo cum timore et tremore excepistis illum.
corrections.english: And his heart are more abundantly towards you: remembering the obedience of you all, how with fear and trembling you received him.

first_reading.proposed: And his heart is more abundantly towards you: remembering the obedience of you all, how with fear and trembling you received him.
first_reading.reason: 'his heart are' is ungrammatical (verb left plural after 'bowels' was changed to 'heart' for 'viscera ejus ... sunt').

corrections.proposed_english: And his heart is more abundantly towards you: remembering the obedience of you all, how with fear and trembling you received him.

first_reading.proposed: Now I have sent the brothers, that the thing which we boast of concerning you be not made void in this behalf, that (as I have said) you may be ready:
first_reading.reason: 'do not be made void' is broken English (faulty modernisation of 'be not made void') for 'ut ne ... evacuetur'.

second_reading.note: "ut ne ... evacuetur"; "do not be made void" is ungrammatical.

corrections.proposed_english: Now I have sent the brothers, that the thing which we boast of concerning you be not made void in this behalf, that (as I have said) you may be ready:

corrections.latin: Quare? quia non diligo vos? Deus scit.

second_reading.note: "Quare?" is the interrogative Why; "Therefore?" mistranslates it and makes no sense.

corrections.proposed_english: Why? Because I love you not? God knows it.

corrections.latin: Scio hominem in Christo ante annos quatuordecim, sive in corpore nescio, sive extra corpus nescio, Deus scit, raptum hujusmodi usque ad tertium cælum.
corrections.english: I know a man in Christ: above fourteen years ago (whether in the body, I know not, or out of the body, I know not: God knows), such a one caught up to the third heaven.

first_reading.proposed: I know a man in Christ: fourteen years ago (whether in the body, I know not, or out of the body, I know not: God knows), such a one caught up to the third heaven.

second_reading.note: "ante annos quatuordecim" = fourteen years ago; "above" (more than) has no Latin warrant.

corrections.proposed_english: I know a man in Christ: fourteen years ago (whether in the body, I know not, or out of the body, I know not: God knows), such a one caught up to the third heaven.

corrections.latin: ut revelaret Filium suum in me, ut evangelizarem illum in gentibus: continuo non acquievi carni et sanguini,

second_reading.note: "non acquievi carni et sanguini" = I did not acquiesce in or yield to; "confer with" renders the Greek verb.

corrections.proposed_english: to reveal his Son in me so that I might proclaim him among the Gentiles, I did not immediately yield to flesh and blood,

corrections.latin: At ubi venit plenitudo temporis, misit Deus Filium suum factum ex muliere, factum sub lege,

corrections.proposed_english: But when the fullness of time came, God sent his Son, made of a woman, made under the law,

corrections.latin: quæ sunt per allegoriam dicta. Hæc enim sunt duo testamenta. Unum quidem in monte Sina, in servitutem generans, quæ est Agar:

second_reading.note: "in monte Sina" = on Mount Sinai; "from" renders the Greek preposition, not "in" with ablative.

corrections.proposed_english: These things are spoken as an allegory. For these are two covenants. One is on Mount Sinai, bearing children for slavery. This is Hagar.

corrections.latin: Videte qualibus litteris scripsi vobis mea manu.
corrections.english: See how I have written to you with my own hand.

second_reading.note: "qualibus litteris scripsi" = with what letters I have written; "how" drops "litteris".

corrections.proposed_english: See with what letters I have written to you with my own hand.

corrections.english: Grace be to you and peace, from God the Father and from the Lord Jesus Christ.

corrections.proposed_english: Grace be to you and peace, from God our Father and from the Lord Jesus Christ.

first_reading.proposed: Blessed be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, who has blessed us with every spiritual blessing in heavenly places, in Christ:

second_reading.note: "in omni benedictione spirituali": "omni" is dropped and the singular made plural.

corrections.proposed_english: Blessed be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, who has blessed us with every spiritual blessing in heavenly places, in Christ:

corrections.latin: In quo habemus redemptionem per sanguinem ejus, remissionem peccatorum secundum divitias gratiæ ejus,
corrections.english: In whom we have redemption through his blood, the forgiveness of sins, according to the riches of his, grace,

corrections.latin: quia eratis illo in tempore sine Christo, alienati a conversatione Israël, et hospites testamentorum, promissionis spem non habentes, et sine Deo in hoc mundo.
corrections.english: That you were at that time without Christ, being aliens from the conversation of Israel and strangers to the testament, having no hope of the promise and without God in this world.

second_reading.note: "hospites testamentorum" is genitive plural; the singular "testament" is the wrong number.

corrections.proposed_english: That you were at that time without Christ, being aliens from the conversation of Israel and strangers to the testaments, having no hope of the promise and without God in this world.

corrections.latin: et ambulate in dilectione, sicut et Christus dilexit nos, et tradidit semetipsum pro nobis, oblationem et hostiam Deo in odorem suavitatis.

first_reading.reason: 'an fragrance' is ungrammatical (article left from 'an odour' when the noun was modernised).

second_reading.note: "in odorem suavitatis"; "an fragrance" is an article error.

corrections.proposed_english: And walk in love, as Christ also has loved us and has delivered himself for us, an oblation and a sacrifice to God for a fragrance of sweetness.

corrections.latin: Nihil solliciti sitis: sed in omni oratione, et obsecratione, cum gratiarum actione petitiones vestræ innotescant apud Deum.

corrections.proposed_english: Be nothing anxious: but in all prayer and supplication, with thanksgiving, let your petitions be made known to God.

corrections.latin: Habeo autem omnia, et abundo: repletus sum, acceptis ab Epaphrodito quæ misistis odorem suavitatis, hostiam acceptam, placentem Deo.

first_reading.reason: 'an fragrance' is ungrammatical (article left from 'an odour' when the noun was modernised).

second_reading.note: "odorem suavitatis"; "an fragrance" is an article error.

corrections.proposed_english: But I have all and abound: I am filled, having received from Epaphroditus the things you sent, a fragrance of sweetness, an acceptable sacrifice, pleasing to God.

corrections.latin: Filii, obedite parentibus per omnia: hoc enim placitum est in Domino.
corrections.english: Children, obey your parents in all things: for this is well pleasing to the Lord.

corrections.proposed_english: Children, obey your parents in all things: for this is well pleasing in the Lord.

corrections.proposed_english: Praying at the same time for us also, that God may open to us a door of speech to speak the mystery of Christ (for which also I am bound):

corrections.latin: Rogamus autem vos, fratres, per adventum Domini nostri Jesu Christi, et nostræ congregationis in ipsum:
