second_reading.note: "Rogamus ... per adventum" is an adjuration, by the coming; "concerning" renders the Greek preposition.

corrections.proposed_english: Now we appeal to you, brothers, by the coming of our Lord Jesus Christ and our gathering to him,

corrections.latin: Radix enim omnium malorum est cupiditas: quam quidam appetentes erraverunt a fide, et inseruerunt se doloribus multis.
corrections.english: For greed is the root of all evils. In pursuing it, some have wandered from the faith and pierced themselves with many sorrows.

first_reading.proposed: For greed is the root of all evils. In pursuing it, some have wandered from the faith and entangled themselves in many sorrows.
first_reading.reason: "inseruerunt se doloribus multis" means they thrust or entangled themselves in many sorrows; "pierced themselves" renders the Greek verb (as in the KJV), not "inseruerunt".

second_reading.note: "inseruerunt se doloribus multis" = thrust or entangled themselves in; "pierced" renders the Greek verb.

corrections.proposed_english: For greed is the root of all evils. In pursuing it, some have wandered from the faith and entangled themselves in many sorrows.

corrections.latin: Juvenilia autem desideria fuge, sectare vero justitiam, fidem, spem, caritatem, et pacem cum iis qui invocant Dominum de corde puro.
corrections.english: But flee you youthful desires, and pursue justice, faith, love and peace with them that call on the Lord out of a pure heart.

first_reading.proposed: But flee you youthful desires, and pursue justice, faith, hope, love and peace with them that call on the Lord out of a pure heart.
first_reading.reason: The Latin list is "justitiam, fidem, spem, caritatem, et pacem"; "spem" (hope) is missing from the English, which keeps the Douay-Rheims list without it.

second_reading.note: "justitiam, fidem, spem, caritatem, et pacem": "spem" (hope) is omitted from the English list.

corrections.proposed_english: But flee you youthful desires, and pursue justice, faith, hope, love and peace with them that call on the Lord out of a pure heart.

corrections.latin: Confitentur se nosse Deum, factis autem negant: cum sint abominati, et incredibiles, et ad omne opus bonum reprobi.
corrections.english: They profess to know God, but deny him by their deeds. They are detestable, disobedient, and unfit for any good work.

first_reading.proposed: They profess to know God, but deny him by their deeds. They are detestable, unbelieving, and unfit for any good work.
first_reading.reason: "incredibiles" here means unbelieving (compare "increduli" rendered so at 3:3); "disobedient" renders the Greek word, not the Latin.

second_reading.note: "incredibiles" here = unbelieving (Douay "incredulous"); "disobedient" renders the Greek word.

corrections.proposed_english: They profess to know God, but deny him by their deeds. They are detestable, unbelieving, and unfit for any good work.

corrections.latin: senes ut sobrii sint, pudici, prudentes, sani in fide, in dilectione, in patientia:
corrections.english: older men are to be sober, dignified, prudent, and sound in faith, love, and endurance;

first_reading.proposed: older men are to be sober, chaste, prudent, and sound in faith, love, and endurance;
first_reading.reason: "pudici" means chaste or modest (so rendered in 1 Timothy 3); "dignified" renders the Greek term, not this Latin word.

second_reading.note: "pudici" = chaste, modest; "dignified" renders the Greek term, not this Latin.

corrections.proposed_english: older men are to be sober, chaste, prudent, and sound in faith, love, and endurance;

corrections.latin: anus similiter in habitu sancto, non criminatrices, non multo vino servientes, bene docentes:
corrections.english: older women likewise are to be holy in their conduct, not slanderers or enslaved to much wine, but teachers of what is good,

first_reading.proposed: older women likewise are to be holy in their conduct, not slanderers or enslaved to much wine, but teaching well,
first_reading.reason: "bene docentes" is "teaching well" (adverb of manner); "teachers of what is good" makes the good the object taught, as in the Greek compound.

second_reading.note: "bene docentes": adverb plus participle, teaching well; "teachers of what is good" renders the Greek compound.

corrections.proposed_english: older women likewise are to be holy in their conduct, not slanderers or enslaved to much wine, but teaching well,

corrections.latin: verbum sanum, irreprehensibile: ut is qui ex adverso est, vereatur, nihil habens malum dicere de nobis.
corrections.english: and sound speech beyond reproach, so that an opponent may be put to shame, having nothing evil to say about us.

first_reading.proposed: and sound speech beyond reproach, so that an opponent may be afraid, having nothing evil to say about us.
first_reading.reason: "vereatur" means may fear or stand in awe; "be put to shame" renders the Greek verb, not the Latin.

second_reading.note: "vereatur" = may fear or stand in awe; "be put to shame" renders the Greek verb.

corrections.proposed_english: and sound speech beyond reproach, so that an opponent may be afraid, having nothing evil to say about us.

corrections.latin: Fidelis sermo est: et de his volo te confirmare: ut curent bonis operibus præesse qui credunt Deo. Hæc sunt bona, et utilia hominibus.
corrections.english: This saying is trustworthy, and I want you to insist on these things, so that those who believe God may take care to devote themselves to good works. These things are good and useful to people.

first_reading.proposed: This saying is trustworthy, and I want you to insist on these things, so that those who believe God may take care to excel in good works. These things are good and useful to people.
first_reading.reason: "bonis operibus præesse" means to be foremost or take the lead in good works; "devote themselves to" loses the sense of "præesse".

second_reading.note: "bonis operibus præesse" = to be foremost, take the lead in good works; "devote themselves to" loses "præesse".

corrections.proposed_english: This saying is trustworthy, and I want you to insist on these things, so that those who believe God may take care to excel in good works. These things are good and useful to people.

corrections.latin: Discant autem et nostri bonis operibus præesse ad usus necessarios: ut non sint infructuosi.
corrections.english: Let our people also learn to devote themselves to good works to meet necessary needs, so that they may not be unfruitful.

first_reading.proposed: Let our people also learn to excel in good works to meet necessary needs, so that they may not be unfruitful.
first_reading.reason: "bonis operibus præesse" means to be foremost or take the lead in good works; "devote themselves to" loses the sense of "præesse".

second_reading.note: "bonis operibus præesse" = to be foremost in good works; "devote themselves to" loses "præesse".

corrections.proposed_english: Let our people also learn to excel in good works to meet necessary needs, so that they may not be unfruitful.

corrections.latin: Forsitan enim ideo discessit ad horam a te, ut æternum illum reciperes:
corrections.english: For perhaps he was separated from you for a time so that you might receive him forever,

first_reading.proposed: For perhaps he departed from you for a time so that you might receive him forever,
first_reading.reason: "discessit" is active, "he departed"; the passive "was separated" renders the Greek passive verb, not the Latin.

second_reading.note: "discessit ... a te" is active, he departed; the passive "was separated" follows the Greek.

corrections.proposed_english: For perhaps he departed from you for a time so that you might receive him forever,

corrections.latin: Etenim cum deberetis magistri esse propter tempus, rursum indigetis ut vos doceamini quæ sint elementa exordii sermonum Dei: et facti estis quibus lacte opus sit, non solido cibo.
corrections.english: For whereas for the time you ought to be masters, you have need to be taught again what are the first elements of the words of God: and you are become such as need milk and not of strong food.

first_reading.proposed: For whereas for the time you ought to be masters, you have need to be taught again what are the first elements of the words of God: and you are become such as have need of milk and not of strong food.
first_reading.reason: "such as need milk and not of strong food" is broken grammar left by modernising "have need of milk, and not of"; Latin "quibus lacte opus sit, non solido cibo".

second_reading.note: "quibus lacte opus sit, non solido cibo"; "need milk and not of strong food" is broken grammar.

corrections.proposed_english: For whereas for the time you ought to be masters, you have need to be taught again what are the first elements of the words of God: and you are become such as have need of milk and not of strong food.

corrections.latin: Fide Moyses, natus, occultatus est mensibus tribus a parentibus suis, eo quod vidissent elegantem infantem, et non timuerunt regis edictum.
corrections.english: By faith Moses, when he was born, was hid three months by his parents: because they saw he was a fitting babe, and they feared not the king’s edict.

first_reading.proposed: By faith Moses, when he was born, was hid three months by his parents: because they saw he was a comely babe, and they feared not the king’s edict.
first_reading.reason: "elegantem infantem" means a fine, handsome child (Douay "comely"); "fitting" does not render "elegantem" and gives no sense here.

second_reading.note: "elegantem infantem" = a fine, handsome child; "fitting" does not render "elegantem".

corrections.proposed_english: By faith Moses, when he was born, was hid three months by his parents: because they saw he was a comely babe, and they feared not the king’s edict.

corrections.latin: Recogitate enim eum qui talem sustinuit a peccatoribus adversum semetipsum contradictionem: ut ne fatigemini, animis vestris deficientes.
corrections.english: For think diligently upon him that endured such opposition from sinners against himself that you do not be wearied, fainting in your minds.

first_reading.proposed: For think diligently upon him that endured such opposition from sinners against himself that you be not wearied, fainting in your minds.
first_reading.reason: "that you do not be wearied" is ungrammatical, a slip in modernising "that you be not wearied" for "ut ne fatigemini".

second_reading.note: "ut ne fatigemini"; "you do not be wearied" is ungrammatical.

corrections.proposed_english: For think diligently upon him that endured such opposition from sinners against himself that you be not wearied, fainting in your minds.

corrections.latin: Tu autem quis es, qui judicas proximum? Ecce nunc qui dicitis: Hodie, aut crastino ibimus in illam civitatem, et faciemus ibi quidem annum, et mercabimur, et lucrum faciemus:
corrections.english: But who are you that judge your neighbour? Behold, now you that say: To-day or to-next day we will go into such a city, and there we will spend a year and will traffic and make our gain.

first_reading.proposed: But who are you that judge your neighbour? Behold, now you that say: To-day or to-morrow we will go into such a city, and there we will spend a year and will traffic and make our gain.
first_reading.reason: "to-next day" is a garbled modernisation of "to-morrow" for "Hodie, aut crastino"; it is not English.

second_reading.note: "Hodie, aut crastino" = today or tomorrow; "to-next day" is not English.

corrections.proposed_english: But who are you that judge your neighbour? Behold, now you that say: To-day or to-morrow we will go into such a city, and there we will spend a year and will traffic and make our gain.

corrections.latin: si tamen gustastis quoniam dulcis est Dominus.
corrections.english: If so be have tasted that the Lord is sweet.

first_reading.proposed: If so be you have tasted that the Lord is sweet.
first_reading.reason: The subject "you" is missing ("si tamen gustastis"), leaving "If so be have tasted" broken.

second_reading.note: "si tamen gustastis" is second person plural; the subject "you" is missing.

corrections.proposed_english: If so be you have tasted that the Lord is sweet.

corrections.latin: et lapis offensionis, et petra scandali, his qui offendunt verbo, nec credunt in quo et positi sunt.
corrections.english: And a stone of stumbling and a rock of scandal, to them who stumble at the word, neither do believe, to what also they are set.

first_reading.proposed: And a stone of stumbling and a rock of scandal, to them who stumble at the word, neither do believe, to which also they are set.
first_reading.reason: "to what also they are set" is a faulty modernisation of "whereunto"; the relative "in quo et positi sunt" needs "to which".

second_reading.note: "in quo et positi sunt" is a relative clause; "to what" is a faulty relative.

corrections.proposed_english: And a stone of stumbling and a rock of scandal, to them who stumble at the word, neither do believe, to which also they are set.

corrections.latin: Viri similiter cohabitantes secundum scientiam, quasi infirmiori vasculo muliebri impartientes honorem, tamquam et cohæredibus gratiæ vitæ: ut non impediantur orationes vestræ.
corrections.english: You husbands, likewise dwelling with them according to knowledge, giving honor to the female as to the weaker vessel and as to the co-heirs of the grace of life: that your prayers do not be hindered.

first_reading.proposed: You husbands, likewise dwelling with them according to knowledge, giving honor to the female as to the weaker vessel and as to the co-heirs of the grace of life: that your prayers be not hindered.
first_reading.reason: "that your prayers do not be hindered" is ungrammatical, a slip in modernising "be not hindered" for "ut non impediantur".

second_reading.note: "ut non impediantur"; "do not be hindered" is ungrammatical.

corrections.proposed_english: You husbands, likewise dwelling with them according to knowledge, giving honor to the female as to the weaker vessel and as to the co-heirs of the grace of life: that your prayers be not hindered.

corrections.latin: qui increduli fuerant aliquando, quando exspectabant Dei patientiam in diebus Noë, cum fabricaretur arca: in qua pauci, id est octo animæ, salvæ factæ sunt per aquam.
corrections.english: who had once been unbelieving, when they waited during God’s patience in the days of Noah, while the ark was being built. In it a few, that is, eight souls, were saved through water.

first_reading.proposed: who had once been unbelieving, when they waited for God’s patience in the days of Noah, while the ark was being built. In it a few, that is, eight souls, were saved through water.
first_reading.reason: "exspectabant Dei patientiam": "patientiam" is the direct object, they waited for the patience of God; "waited during God’s patience" turns it into a circumstance.

second_reading.note: "exspectabant Dei patientiam": "patientiam" is direct object, waited for; "during" makes it a circumstance.

corrections.proposed_english: who had once been unbelieving, when they waited for God’s patience in the days of Noah, while the ark was being built. In it a few, that is, eight souls, were saved through water.

corrections.latin: Sic enim abundanter ministrabitur vobis introitus in æternum regnum Domini nostri et Salvatoris Jesu Christi.
corrections.english: For so an entrance shall be ministered to you abundantly into the ever-lasting kingdom of our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ.

first_reading.proposed: For so an entrance shall be ministered to you abundantly into the everlasting kingdom of our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ.
first_reading.reason: "ever-lasting" carries a stray hyphen; "æternum regnum" is "everlasting kingdom".

second_reading.note: "æternum regnum"; "ever-lasting" has a stray hyphen.

corrections.proposed_english: For so an entrance shall be ministered to you abundantly into the everlasting kingdom of our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ.

corrections.latin: Et habemus firmiorem propheticum sermonem: cui benefacitis attendentes quasi lucernæ lucenti in caliginoso loco donec dies elucescat, et lucifer oriatur in cordibus vestris:
corrections.english: And we have the more firm prophetical word: to what you do well to attend, as to a light that shines in a dark place, until the day dawn and the day star arise in your hearts.

first_reading.proposed: And we have the more firm prophetical word: to which you do well to attend, as to a light that shines in a dark place, until the day dawn and the day star arise in your hearts.
first_reading.reason: "to what you do well to attend" is a faulty modernisation of "whereunto"; the relative "cui" needs "to which".

second_reading.note: "cui benefacitis attendentes": relative "cui" needs "to which"; "to what" is faulty.

corrections.proposed_english: And we have the more firm prophetical word: to which you do well to attend, as to a light that shines in a dark place, until the day dawn and the day star arise in your hearts.

corrections.latin: Si enim Deus angelis peccantibus non pepercit, sed rudentibus inferni detractos in tartarum tradidit cruciandos, in judicium reservari.
corrections.english: For if God spared not the angels that sinned, but delivered them, drawn down by infernal ropes to the lower the underworld, to torments, to be reserved to judgment:

first_reading.proposed: For if God spared not the angels that sinned, but delivered them, drawn down by infernal ropes to the lower underworld, to torments, to be reserved to judgment:
first_reading.reason: "to the lower the underworld" has a doubled article left by replacing "hell"; Latin "in tartarum".

second_reading.note: "in tartarum"; "to the lower the underworld" has a doubled article.

corrections.proposed_english: For if God spared not the angels that sinned, but delivered them, drawn down by infernal ropes to the lower underworld, to torments, to be reserved to judgment:

corrections.latin: aspectu enim, et auditu justus erat: habitans apud eos, qui de die in diem animam justam iniquis operibus cruciabant.
corrections.english: For in sight and hearing he was just, dwelling among them who from day today vexed the just soul with unjust works.

first_reading.proposed: For in sight and hearing he was just, dwelling among them who from day to day vexed the just soul with unjust works.
first_reading.reason: "from day today" is a typo for "from day to day" ("de die in diem").

second_reading.note: "de die in diem" = from day to day; "day today" is a typo.

corrections.proposed_english: For in sight and hearing he was just, dwelling among them who from day to day vexed the just soul with unjust works.

corrections.latin: quod vidimus et audivimus, annuntiamus vobis, ut et vos societatem habeatis nobiscum, et societas nostra sit cum Patre, et cum Filio ejus Jesu Christo.
corrections.english: what we have seen and heard we announce to you also, so that you too may have fellowship with us, and our fellowship may be with the Father and with his Son Jesus Christ.

first_reading.proposed: what we have seen and heard we announce to you, so that you too may have fellowship with us, and our fellowship may be with the Father and with his Son Jesus Christ.
first_reading.reason: Latin has only "annuntiamus vobis, ut et vos": one "et", rendered by "you too". The extra "also" after "to you" reflects the Greek (kai hymin), not this Latin.

second_reading.note: "annuntiamus vobis, ut et vos" has one "et", already rendered "you too"; the extra "also" follows the Greek.

corrections.proposed_english: what we have seen and heard we announce to you, so that you too may have fellowship with us, and our fellowship may be with the Father and with his Son Jesus Christ.

corrections.latin: Majorem horum non habeo gratiam, quam ut audiam filios meos in veritate ambulare.
corrections.english: I have no greater joy than this: to hear that my children are walking in truth.

first_reading.proposed: I have no greater grace than this: to hear that my children are walking in truth.
first_reading.reason: "gratiam" is grace/favour; "joy" follows the Greek reading charan (Latin would be gaudium). The Vulgate's distinctive "Majorem horum non habeo gratiam" should be kept.

second_reading.note: "Majorem horum non habeo gratiam": "gratiam" is grace; "joy" follows the Greek reading, which would be "gaudium".

corrections.proposed_english: I have no greater grace than this: to hear that my children are walking in truth.

corrections.latin: Cum Michaël Archangelus cum diabolo disputans altercaretur de Moysi corpore, non est ausus judicium inferre blasphemiæ: sed dixit: Imperet tibi Dominus.
corrections.english: But when Michael the archangel, disputing with the devil, argued about the body of Moses, he did not dare to bring a blasphemous judgment against him, but said, “May the Lord rebuke you.”

first_reading.proposed: But when Michael the archangel, disputing with the devil, argued about the body of Moses, he did not dare to bring a blasphemous judgment against him, but said, “May the Lord command you.”
first_reading.reason: "Imperet tibi Dominus" is "May the Lord command you" (impero = command). "Rebuke" renders the Greek epitimesai (Latin would be increpet), not this Latin.

second_reading.note: "Imperet tibi Dominus" = may the Lord command you; "rebuke" renders the Greek, which would be "increpet".

corrections.proposed_english: But when Michael the archangel, disputing with the devil, argued about the body of Moses, he did not dare to bring a blasphemous judgment against him, but said, “May the Lord command you.”

corrections.latin: Dignus es Domine Deus noster accipere gloriam, et honorem, et virtutem: quia tu creasti omnia, et propter voluntatem tuam erant, et creata sunt.
corrections.english: “You are worthy, our Lord and God, to receive glory, honor, and power, because you created all things; through your will they existed and were created.”

first_reading.proposed: “You are worthy, O Lord our God, to receive glory, honor, and power, because you created all things; through your will they existed and were created.”
first_reading.reason: "Domine Deus noster" is a vocative "O Lord our God". "Our Lord and God" follows the Greek (ho kyrios kai ho theos hemon); the Latin has no "et" and "noster" goes with "Deus".

second_reading.note: "Domine Deus noster": vocative with no "et" and "noster" on "Deus"; "our Lord and God" follows the Greek.

corrections.proposed_english: “You are worthy, O Lord our God, to receive glory, honor, and power, because you created all things; through your will they existed and were created.”
